motivation: Quaternary Preparata codes are typically studied via their binary Gray images in the Lee metric; the authors instead analyze them as codes over a 4-letter alphabet in the Hamming metric to determine their covering properties.
method: The proof is a short computation using Teichmüller representatives in the Galois ring Z_{4^m}, which also yields the coset weight distribution.
result: For odd m the codes have covering radius 2 and minimum distance 4, so they are quasi-perfect; for even m the covering radius is 3. The covering density tends to 1, improving known bounds for quaternary covering codes, e.g., K_4(8,2) ≤ 48 (previous bound 352).
conclusion: These quaternary Preparata codes provide improved upper bounds on covering code sizes for various lengths and alphabets, with the octacode case giving a significant improvement over a 2005 bound.

title: Plotkin-type Bound On Function-Correcting Codes For Monomial Mappings
authors: B. Sundar Rajan Kanchana Lokshmii Jagatti
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Function-correcting codes, recently introduced by Lenz et al.\ (2023), provide a framework for the receiver to provide a higher level of protection against channel errors than the level of protection for messages. In this paper, we derive a generalised Plotkin-type bound on the redundancy of FCCs under the Hamming metric for arbitrary functions over finite fields. The proposed bound recovers the classical Plotkin bound for classical error-correcting codes as a special case. We further obtain explicit Plotkin-type bounds for linear functions, Hamming-weight functions, and Hamming-weight threshold functions. In addition, we study FCCs for monomial mappings [MATH] over [MATH], which are widely utilised in coding theory, cryptography, and finite geometry, and derive an explicit Plotkin-type redundancy bound.
tldr: The paper derives a generalized Plotkin-type redundancy bound for function-correcting codes under the Hamming metric and gives explicit bounds for monomial mappings.
motivation: Function-correcting codes provide unequal error protection for function values, and general redundancy bounds are needed to understand their fundamental limits.
method: The authors derive a Plotkin-type bound for arbitrary functions over finite fields, then specialize it to linear functions, Hamming-weight functions, Hamming-weight threshold functions, and monomial mappings.
result: The bound recovers the classical Plotkin bound as a special case and yields explicit redundancy bounds for the studied function classes, including monomial mappings over finite fields.
conclusion: The work establishes theoretical limits for FCCs and may inform code design in coding theory, cryptography, and finite geometry, but it is purely classical and not directly connected to quantum information.

title: Suslin-Rao Codes : The Bridge Between Pure And Applied
authors: Anuradha S. Garge Nitin Kenjale
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the year [MATH] while developing the theory of modules arising in the context of Serre's problem on projective modules in the paper ``On Stably Free Modules" (see ), A. A. Suslin constructed matrices inductively using unimodular rows. Our aim is to connect these matrices to the current and applicable field of coding theory. To this end, we construct Suslin-Rao codes, by using looking at certain unimodular all one vectors over the finite field [MATH]. Comparative analysis with standard families such as Hamming, Simplex and BCH codes shows that the Suslin-Rao codes achieve better performance than Hamming and Simplex codes in terms of code rate and error correction capability, though BCH codes may outperform them for large code lengths. Bit error rate (BER) versus signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) simulations further support the practical applicability of these codes in noisy channels. The recursive nature of the construction allows efficient encoder design, making the proposed codes attractive for real-time communication systems and hardware implementation.
tldr: The paper introduces Suslin-Rao codes by constructing matrices from unimodular all-one vectors over finite fields and evaluates their classical error-correction performance.
motivation: To bridge abstract algebra (Suslin's construction of stably free modules) with applied coding theory by creating new classical error-correcting codes.
method: They use unimodular all-one vectors over finite fields to recursively construct Suslin-Rao codes, then compare rate, error-correction capability, and BER vs SNR against Hamming, Simplex, and BCH codes.
result: Suslin-Rao codes outperform Hamming and Simplex codes in code rate and error correction, though BCH codes may be better for large lengths; BER simulations show practical applicability in noisy channels.
conclusion: The recursive construction enables efficient encoder design, making the codes attractive for real-time communication and hardware implementation.

title: Post-Quantum Authentication Protocol For Internet Of Medical Things
authors: Ranjitha Venkatesh Kartick Sutradhar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: IoMT communication systems should provide origin authentication and ensure integrity protection for the messages produced by patients' devices for transmission to gateways and further processing by other hospital services. With regard to IoMT, this paper discusses tampering, impersonation, and replay attacks on messages provided as medical reports. Long-term security of the communication system is also addressed considering potential quantum attacks. For this purpose, we design a protocol that meets requirements of practical implementation and employs an ISIS like lattice-based construction combined with concepts of the blockchain technology. Patients' devices generate a canonical JSON format medical report containing a timestamp and critical information. Using a nonce, the patients create a cryptographic signature of the message with a challenge generated from hash of a message. The gateway verifies signatures utilizing the public key of a trusted ledger associated with a particular patient and ensures freshness of the transmitted message. To optimize the performance in case when many devices interact with a gateway at once, the gateway performs batch signature validation using vectorized modular linear equations. The trusted ledger uses tamper-resistant REGISTER and TRUST UPDATE entries, maintaining a trust score of each registered patient and updating the value after each ACCEPT/REJECT operation. Our prototype application demonstrates registration procedure of a new patient, signing and verifying medical reports, auditing of the ledger, and performance assessment. Based on our experiments in the prototype, we argue that, when applied to large-scale systems, batch verification is superior to simple signature validation approach.
tldr: The paper proposes a post-quantum authentication protocol for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) using lattice-based signatures and blockchain for secure medical report transmission.
motivation: IoMT systems need origin authentication and integrity against tampering, impersonation, and replay attacks, while also considering long-term security against quantum attacks.
method: The protocol combines an ISIS-like lattice-based signature scheme with blockchain-based trust management, where patient devices sign canonical JSON reports and gateways verify signatures, including batch verification via vectorized modular linear equations.
result: A prototype demonstrates patient registration, signing, verification, ledger auditing, and performance assessment, arguing that batch verification outperforms simple signature validation in large-scale systems.
conclusion: The proposed protocol addresses post-quantum security and practical efficiency for IoMT, but its contribution lies in applied cryptography rather than quantum information theory.

title: A Linear-in-$q$ Range Of Dimensions For The Mds Conjecture Over $\mathbb F_q$ In Odd Characteristic
authors: Xiang Fan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a power of an odd prime [MATH]. We prove the MDS conjecture over [MATH] in dimension [MATH] whenever \[ 2\leqslant k\leqslant B(p,q) \quad\quad q+2-B(p,q)\leqslant k\leqslant q, \] where [MATH]. For fixed [MATH], this gives a range of dimensions linear in [MATH], in contrast with the square-root scale of the previously known general unconditional ranges over proper extension fields, and proves the conjecture in an asymptotic proportion [MATH] of all dimensions. The main structural ingredient is a full-support obstruction for determinant relations on arcs over arbitrary fields of odd characteristic. After projection from [MATH] points, local matching constraints followed by multilinear descent force the resulting homogeneous system to have zero kernel. For a hypothetical [MATH]-point arc over [MATH], the Ball--Lavrauw construction produces precisely the forbidden relations. The same framework also proves Chowdhury's conjecture that a family of inclusion matrices has full row rank.
tldr: The paper proves the MDS conjecture over odd-prime-power fields for a range of dimensions linear in q, using a full-support obstruction for determinant relations on arcs.
motivation: The MDS conjecture is a central open problem in classical coding theory and finite geometry, with previously known unconditional ranges over proper extension fields only reaching a square-root scale in q.
method: The main structural ingredient is a full-support obstruction for determinant relations on arcs over odd-characteristic fields, combined with projection from points, local matching constraints, and multilinear descent to force a homogeneous system to have zero kernel; the Ball-Lavrauw construction yields forbidden relations for hypothetical arcs.
result: The MDS conjecture is established for dimensions 2 ≤ k ≤ B(p,q) and q+2−B(p,q) ≤ k ≤ q, giving a linear-in-q range and proving the conjecture in an asymptotic proportion of all dimensions; the same framework also proves Chowdhury's conjecture on full row rank of a family of inclusion matrices.
conclusion: This is a significant advance in classical algebraic coding theory and finite geometry, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Champ: Cayley HAshing With Matrix Products
authors: Alexander Demin, Alexey Ovchinnikov, Vladimir Shpilrain
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cayley hash functions hash binary strings by representing the bits of the message as elements of a semigroup and multiplying the corresponding elements. This gives Cayley hash functions useful homomorphic properties. Here, we propose CHAMP, a Cayley hash function based on products of 2 by 2 matrices over a finite field, and discuss its security, implementation, and performance.
tldr: CHAMP proposes a classical Cayley hash function built from products of 2x2 matrices over a finite field, with discussion of its security, implementation, and performance.
motivation: Cayley hash functions encode binary messages as semigroup elements and multiply them, yielding useful homomorphic properties; the authors aim to construct and evaluate a new matrix-based instance.
method: The scheme hashes message bits by mapping them to 2x2 matrices over a finite field and multiplying the corresponding sequence, followed by security analysis and performance/implementation evaluation.
result: CHAMP is presented as a practical Cayley hash with homomorphic features, along with a security discussion and implementation/performance characterization.
conclusion: The work contributes a classical cryptographic primitive in the post-quantum-candidate space, but contains no quantum information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid-system content.

title: Benchmarking Ansatze For Pauli Correlation Encoding In The Maximum Independent Set Problem
authors: Cian C. Reeves, Aaron C. Kemp, Richard Padbury, Eva Lia Tarquini, Christoph Kloeffel, Vedangi Pathak, Hamed Mohammadbagherpoor, Vincent Beltrani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing complexity of 5G and emerging 6G wireless networks has intensified the need for scalable optimization techniques capable of addressing computationally challenging combinatorial problems. While quantum optimization offers a promising alternative, current near-term quantum hardware remains limited by qubit availability, noise, and scalability constraints. Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) has emerged as a qubit-efficient optimization framework that addresses these challenges through polynomial variable compression. However, the impact of compression on representability and solution recovery remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate the hypothesis that increasing compression ratios introduce representability constraints arising from algebraic closure relationships among encoded Pauli observables. Using Maximum Independent Set benchmark problems, we evaluate multiple PCE ansatz designs and compression ratios. We find that ansatz selection is critical to both solution quality and feasibility, with two ansatz families consistently outperforming alternatives and achieving approximation ratios approaching 0.9. Furthermore, increasing circuit repetitions provides limited benefit and can degrade performance. Most notably, reducing compression by increasing the number of available qubits significantly improves raw solution quality, while post-processed performance remains comparatively stable. These findings suggest that representability effects play an important role in compressed PCE encodings and provide new insight into the relationship among compression, ansatz design, decoding, and solution quality in scalable quantum optimization.
tldr: This paper benchmarks ansatz designs and compression ratios for Pauli Correlation Encoding in Maximum Independent Set problems, highlighting representability constraints and ansatz-dependent performance.
motivation: Scalable optimization for 5G/6G networks motivates quantum approaches, but near-term hardware is limited by qubits, noise, and scalability, making qubit-efficient encodings like PCE attractive despite unclear effects of compression on representability.
method: The authors encode Maximum Independent Set problems using PCE at varying compression ratios and benchmark multiple ansatz families with different circuit repetitions, evaluating both raw and post-processed solution quality.
result: Two ansatz families consistently outperform alternatives with approximation ratios near 0.9; increasing circuit repetitions offers limited or negative benefit; reducing compression by using more qubits improves raw solution quality while post-processed performance remains stable.
conclusion: Ansatz selection and compression-induced representability constraints significantly impact PCE performance, suggesting that algebraic closure relationships among encoded Pauli observables play a key role in scalable quantum optimization.

title: Exact Finite-Channel Schur Moments Of The Wigner-Smith Matrix With A Tunnel Barrier
authors: Israel F. Araujo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Wigner--Smith time-delay matrix of a chaotic cavity with broken time-reversal symmetry, a finite number [MATH] of equivalent open channels, and a uniform tunnel barrier of reflection probability [MATH]. Exact random-matrix results for nonideal coupling are known at the level of the joint matrix distribution, whereas explicit finite-channel formulas for Schur moments are much less developed. We show that every Schur moment of the nonideal Wigner--Smith matrix factorizes into its ideal-coupling inverse-Laguerre value and a barrier factor given by a circular unitary ensemble (CUE) average of a Schur polynomial. A dual-Cauchy generating function reduces the latter to a Toeplitz determinant with a rational symbol, placing the barrier problem within the classical theory of exact CUE characteristic-polynomial ratios. For one-row partitions, specializing the exact CUE ratio formula gives a closed generating function for all barrier coefficients and therefore all finite delay-time moments in the allowed range [MATH]. The exact ratio formula decomposes into a sector visible to the semiclassical expansion and an additional contribution proportional to [MATH], which is invisible to every algebraic order in [MATH]. For the second moment, this contribution exactly reproduces the exponentially small term in the known random-matrix expression for [MATH] that is absent from the semiclassical expansion. We also derive an exact finite sum for all one-column partitions and an exact complement symmetry for Schur averages inside the [MATH] square. The new contribution therefore lies not in the underlying CUE ratio identities, which are classical, but in combining them with the exact nonideal Wigner--Smith mapping and extracting the resulting finite-channel time-delay formulas and corrections to semiclassical Schur-moment conjectures.
tldr: Exact random-matrix results for finite-channel Schur moments of the Wigner-Smith time-delay matrix with a tunnel barrier, expressed via CUE averages and Toeplitz determinants.
motivation: Nonideal coupling in chaotic cavities is experimentally relevant, but explicit finite-channel formulas for time-delay moments beyond the joint matrix distribution were lacking.
method: The authors factorize Schur moments into ideal inverse-Laguerre values and a barrier factor, then evaluate the barrier factor as a CUE average of a Schur polynomial using a dual-Cauchy generating function and Toeplitz determinant techniques.
result: For one-row partitions, they obtain a closed generating function for all barrier coefficients and delay-time moments, and identify an exponentially small correction invisible to semiclassical expansion; they also derive exact finite sums for one-column partitions and a complement symmetry.
conclusion: The work bridges classical CUE ratio identities with the exact nonideal Wigner-Smith mapping to yield finite-channel time-delay formulas and corrections to semiclassical conjectures.

title: The Quantum Sphere: A Physically Realizable Optimization Benchmark With Provable Linear Convergence In White- And Black-Box Settings
authors: Ofer M. Shir
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit an established Quantum Control objective, characterize its exact local metric geometry, and reposition it as a rigorous benchmark for Search and Optimization. The trap-free topology of the landscape, established two decades ago, guarantees unhindered optimal pathways, but global topology alone does not govern convergence speed. Although the so-called Quantum Sphere is defined by the fourth power of the control field, we show that its yield gap admits an exact representation as a nonnegative linear combination of [MATH] terms. From this single identity, we derive a two-sided quadratic sandwich with ratio [MATH] on a certified, worst-case quarter-wave region, proving the optimal peak nondegenerate modulo its affine gauge and well-conditioned. For white-box optimization, on a halved (eighth-wave) region, the objective satisfies a Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz inequality with an explicit constant, granting Gradient Descent a linear rate of [MATH], where [MATH] is the condition number of the relevant Hessian block. For black-box optimization, we prove that the elitist single-parent Evolution Strategy converges linearly, almost surely and in expected hitting time, from a certified sublevel set, despite the landscape's continuous gauge symmetry and its lattice of periodic optima; the certified level is explicit whenever the landscape is trap-free, and near the optimum the strategy provably sees only the quadratic tangent of the peak. Systematic numerical simulations corroborate the theory. Finally, we show that additive input (actuator) noise reweights each term of the representation by a Debye-Waller factor without disrupting the landscape's structure, and outline open challenges: output (signal) noise, far-field plateau escape, angular-synchronization certificates, and another physically scalable benchmark (SHG with Glass).
tldr: The paper characterizes the local geometry of the Quantum Sphere control landscape and proves linear convergence rates for gradient descent and evolution strategies, proposing it as a rigorous optimization benchmark.
motivation: Quantum control landscapes are widely used in search and optimization, but global trap-free topology alone does not determine convergence speed, motivating a precise local convergence analysis.
method: The authors derive an exact representation of the yield gap as a nonnegative linear combination, establish a two-sided quadratic sandwich, and prove Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequalities for white-box and black-box optimization.
result: They show gradient descent achieves a linear rate on a certified quarter-wave region, and an elitist single-parent evolution strategy converges linearly almost surely from a certified sublevel set, with numerical simulations corroborating the theory.
conclusion: The Quantum Sphere provides a physically realizable benchmark with provable convergence guarantees, while noise analysis and open challenges point to future directions in quantum control optimization.

title: Exponentially Compressed And Garbage-Free Alias Sampling For Polynomial State Preparation
authors: Diyi Liu, Hanyu Wang, Shuchen Zhu, Jason Cong, Wibe Albert de Jong, David Williams-Young, Chao Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherent alias sampling implement an important subroutine for block encoding and qubitization based quantum simulation using quantum lookup table. Related constructions exploit data lookup and matrix structure to implement block encodings for use in quantum singular value transformation. For a state on [MATH] qubits, constructing and storing the alias table requires both classical and quantum resources exponential in [MATH]. We show that when the amplitudes are samples of a polynomial of degree at most [MATH], the table can be represented and evaluated coherently with cost polynomial in [MATH], [MATH], exponentially reduced from [MATH] classical and quantum cost. We construct a quantum circuit for coherently computing the alias table for polynomial states using reversible integer arithmetic. By employing fast arithmetic, we construct a deterministic circuit for preparing polynomial states over Clifford+[MATH] with a complete gate count of [MATH], where arithmetic width [MATH]. In the high precision limit for state fidelity [MATH] with fixed [MATH] and [MATH], it is sufficient have [MATH] and the complete gate count becomes [MATH]. Additionally, the effective representation of the alias table can also be used for classical sampling algorithms. Furthermore, we develop a novel technique for uncomputing the auxilary register generated by coherent alias sampling. This technique opens a research direction in sampling based initial state preparation.
tldr: The paper presents a compressed, garbage-free alias-sampling method for polynomial quantum state preparation, exponentially reducing alias-table resources.
motivation: Coherent alias sampling is a key subroutine for block encoding and qubitization in quantum simulation, but storing and constructing alias tables requires exponential classical and quantum resources.
method: The authors exploit polynomial structure in the amplitudes to represent the alias table compactly, using reversible integer arithmetic and a novel uncomputation technique to construct deterministic Clifford+T circuits.
result: For degree-d polynomial states, the table can be evaluated with polynomial cost in d and precision, yielding exponentially reduced resources and explicit gate counts, including a high-precision limit.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient polynomial state preparation for quantum simulation and also benefits classical sampling, opening a direction for sampling-based initial state preparation.

title: Quantum-Assisted Optimization Guided By Machine-Learned Risk Maps For Aerial Surveillance Routing
authors: Dorian Lauwerier, Alexis Vieloszynski, Yves B\'erub\'e-Lauzi\`ere, Victor Drouin-Touchette
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analog quantum computing with neutral atom computers is rapidly evolving into a promising way to perform combinatorial optimization tasks at scale. As technology matures, exploring real use cases leveraging such unique information processors becomes warranted; one example is logistics management where vehicles are assigned routes to perform a given task. Autonomous aerial vehicles (drones) are increasingly used for surveillance over a given territory. In this paper, we propose an innovative framework integrating classical machine learning forecasts and quantum annealing to find the best combination of tours for a given surveillance criterion. The risk maps produced by machine learning are used to find possible surveillance tours, while a quantum-assisted heuristic chooses the best combination, producing a full surveillance plan. By modelling our decision problem for drone paths as a Team Orienteering Problem (TOP) with additional constraints, we construct a new heuristic using quantum annealing to find good solutions. We apply this framework to wildfire prevention, where finding tours most likely to detect a starting fire has clear benefits. We study the effect of larger quantum resources on heuristic performance and compare those results to the use of classical resources.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid framework combining machine-learned risk maps and quantum annealing to optimize drone surveillance routes for wildfire prevention.
motivation: To explore real-world use cases for neutral-atom analog quantum computers in logistics and combinatorial optimization, where classical methods may struggle at scale.
method: The routing problem is modeled as a Team Orienteering Problem with additional constraints, and a quantum-assisted heuristic using quantum annealing selects the best combination of tours based on ML-generated risk maps.
result: The study examines how larger quantum resources affect heuristic performance and compares the results to classical resource baselines.
conclusion: The framework demonstrates a practical application of quantum-assisted optimization for aerial surveillance, but it does not advance quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Certification Failure In Variational-principle Observables
authors: Ganga Singh Manchanda
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algorithms which prepare states via the variational principle assume that closeness in energy implies closeness in state; we formalise how this assumption can fail by showing that a ground-state energy estimate converged to within [MATH] of the true value is compatible with observable expectation values in error by up to [MATH] at leading order, where [MATH] is the static susceptibility of the observable. As a result, the observable error can be orders of magnitude larger than the energy error, a mechanism we call non-linear error amplification, and because a variational algorithm cannot guarantee the correctness of these properties from energy alone, energy does not necessarily certify an observable. In light of our findings, we examine three algorithms: the variational quantum eigensolver on the transverse-field Ising chain, the density-matrix renormalisation group on a pair of weakly coupled hydrogen chains, and Krylov quantum diagonalisation on lithium fluoride. In each case we demonstrate that a well-converged energy can leave observables uncertified.
tldr: The paper shows that small ground-state energy errors in variational algorithms can correspond to arbitrarily large observable errors due to static susceptibility, undermining energy-based certification.
motivation: Variational algorithms assume that closeness in energy implies closeness in state, and thus energy convergence can certify observable expectation values, but this assumption can fail.
method: The authors formalize the error amplification to leading order, relating observable error to energy error and static susceptibility, and demonstrate it numerically with VQE on a transverse-field Ising chain, DMRG on weakly coupled hydrogen chains, and Krylov quantum diagonalisation on lithium fluoride.
result: Observable errors can be orders of magnitude larger than energy errors, so a well-converged energy leaves observables uncertified.
conclusion: Energy alone is insufficient to certify observable expectation values in variational quantum simulation, and additional checks are needed.

title: Casimir Force, Magnetization, And Susceptibility For \\ Ising Chain With An Impurity Atom In The Presence Of An External Field
authors: Daniel Dantchev
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article contains exact results for the behavior of the Casimir force of Ising chain of [MATH] atoms containing an impurity atom. The force is considered as a function of [MATH] and on both the temperature [MATH] and the external magnetic field [MATH]. The interactions between nearest neighbors within the chain are supposed to be of a ferromagnetic short-ranged type [MATH]. The impurity atom interacts with constants [MATH] with its nearest neighbors, where [MATH] can be both of ferromagnetic type, i.e., [MATH], as well as of antiferromagnetic type, i.e., [MATH]. It turns out that the Casimir force can be both attractive or repulsive, depending on the sign and the magnitude of the ratio [MATH].
tldr: Exact results are derived for the Casimir force, magnetization, and susceptibility of a classical Ising chain with a single impurity atom in an external magnetic field.
motivation: The paper aims to understand how an impurity atom and an external field modify the fluctuation-induced Casimir force in a simple spin chain.
method: Exact analytical calculations for a ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor Ising chain where the impurity interacts with its neighbors via either ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic couplings.
result: The Casimir force can be attractive or repulsive depending on the sign and magnitude of the impurity coupling ratio, and expressions for magnetization and susceptibility are obtained.
conclusion: The work provides exact benchmarks for impurity effects in Ising chains, but it is a pure statistical mechanics study with no direct link to quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Statistical Dark Matter: Synergy Is Everywhere But Is Hard To Capture
authors: Alberto Liardi, Fernando E. Rosas, Daniele Marinazzo, Thomas F. Varley, Pedro A. M. Mediano
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The information-theoretic construct of synergy refers to the statistical structure that is contained in three or more variables, but not in any subset of them. Here we leverage recent advances in multivariate information theory to show that synergy is far more prevalent in complex systems than previously thought. In particular, we show that many-body systems tend to become strongly dominated by synergy as the number of subcomponents grows. At the same time, our results also reveal that commonly used tools for statistical modelling severely underestimate synergistic structures. These findings imply that synergy constitutes a prevalent, yet often invisible, informational component of complex systems. With a certain poetic licence, we interpret these results as suggesting that synergy is the dark matter of statistics - interdependencies that we know exist, but standard instruments fail to detect.
tldr: Synergy—information in three or more variables not present in any subset—is pervasive in complex many-body systems and grows with system size, but common statistical tools severely underestimate it.
motivation: To assess how prevalent synergistic structures are in complex systems and whether standard statistical modelling can detect them.
method: Leveraging recent advances in multivariate information theory to quantify synergy in many-body systems and compare with commonly used statistical tools.
result: Many-body systems become increasingly dominated by synergy as the number of subcomponents grows, while typical modelling approaches fail to capture this synergy.
conclusion: Synergy is a prevalent yet often invisible informational component of complex systems, analogous to dark matter in statistics.

title: Effective Dimensions In Grothendieck--H\"older Inequalities
authors: Diana Serrano-Rodr\'iguez Joedson Santos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What becomes of Grothendieck's inequality when its Hilbert-space vectors are replaced by vectors in [MATH] and [MATH]? For an [MATH] matrix, we show that the universal dimensional loss is governed not by [MATH] alone, but by the effective dimension \[ d=\min\{r,m,n\}. \] More precisely, the optimal constant is bounded above and below, up to dimension-free factors, by \[ d^{|1/p-1/2|}. \] The upper bound rests on a pointwise Hilbertian stabilization: for every matrix [MATH], \[ G_2^{(r)}(A)=G_2^{(d)}(A). \] Combining this stabilization with Lewis's Euclidean distortion estimate gives the effective-dimensional Grothendieck--H\"older bound. Beyond the universal power law, we retain the finer rectangular geometry. At [MATH] we prove the exact compression formula \[ \Gamma_\infty^\K(r;m,n) = \rho\!\left( \ell_1^m(\K), \ell_1^{\min\{r,n\}}(\K) \right), \] and derive from it endpoint-sensitive lower bounds throughout the full H\"older scale. Over the complex field, interpolation between the Hilbertian problem and the exact rectangular endpoints yields corresponding upper bounds. Thus the effective dimension determines the universal exponent, whereas the tensor-norm endpoint retains additional aspect-ratio information. We determine the boundedness threshold when [MATH] approaches [MATH]: it is governed by \[ |1/p-1/2|\log d. \] For complex two-row matrices, the endpoint tensor ratios are explicit, and the general rectangular estimates give quantitative two-sided bounds for every [MATH].
tldr: The paper generalizes Grothendieck's inequality to Hölder settings and shows that the optimal constant is governed by an effective dimension d = min{r,m,n} via d^{|1/p-1/2|}.
motivation: Grothendieck's inequality is fundamental in functional analysis and has links to quantum information, but its behavior when Hilbert-space vectors are replaced by vectors in other norms is not well understood.
method: The authors use pointwise Hilbertian stabilization, Lewis's Euclidean distortion estimate, and tensor-norm compression formulas to derive upper and lower bounds.
result: The optimal constant is bounded above and below by d^{|1/p-1/2|} up to dimension-free factors; exact compression formulas and endpoint-sensitive lower bounds are obtained for p = ∞.
conclusion: The effective dimension determines the universal exponent, while tensor-norm endpoints retain aspect-ratio information; the boundedness threshold near p = 1/2 is governed by |1/p - 1/2| log d.

title: Temporal Branched Flow Of Light
authors: Weifeng Ding, Chaokai Yang, Zhaoying Wang, Fanglin Bao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Branched flow of light arises when spatially correlated disorder folds families of rays into caustics. Here, we demonstrate a temporal analog in the retarded-time coordinate of an optical pulse in a waveguide, where branched flow becomes hyper-dispersive. Retardation during pulse propagation induces spatiotemporal correlations that break propagation reciprocity and imprint a trajectory memory. This nonreciprocity enables unidirectional temporal branched flow with no spatial counterpart. A memory model is developed combining ray-density and phase fluctuations with single-ray dynamics in a memory cell. The model reveals competition between fluctuation-induced focusing and destruction, which yields nontrivial diagrams of propagation regimes with distinct dispersion scalings. For a 532-nm pulse in a [MATH] fiber, we predict that refractive-index disorder induced by active modulations or quantum vacuum fluctuations can produce first caustics on meter-to-kilometer scales, offering routes to experimental observation and to sensing ultra-weak fluctuations.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a temporal analog of branched flow of light in the retarded-time coordinate of an optical pulse in a waveguide, where spatiotemporal correlations induce nonreciprocal, hyper-dispersive caustic formation.
motivation: Branched flow has been studied spatially in disordered media, but its temporal counterpart in optical pulses and the role of propagation-induced correlations remained unexplored.
method: The authors develop a memory model combining ray-density and phase fluctuations with single-ray dynamics in a memory cell, and analyze dispersion scalings and propagation regimes for a 532-nm pulse in a multimode fiber.
result: Temporal branched flow is shown to be hyper-dispersive and nonreciprocal due to retardation-induced spatiotemporal correlations, with predicted first caustics on meter-to-kilometer scales arising from refractive-index disorder or quantum vacuum fluctuations.
conclusion: The work offers a route to experimental observation of temporal branched flow and to sensing ultra-weak fluctuations, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Amortized Score-Hamiltonian Policy Iteration: A Grid-Free Scheme For Relaxed Stochastic Control Problems
authors: Gu Wang Qi Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an amortized, grid-free implementation of continuous Langevin dynamics based policy-value iteration for entropy-regularized, infinite-horizon relaxed stochastic control problems. The improvement rate of the exact iteration is a discounted aggregate of relative Fisher information between the policy and the Gibbs law of its Hamiltonian. The associated score residual is the velocity with which the control's Langevin dynamics transport its law. We project this velocity onto a conditional sampler shared across states, instead of one Langevin dynamics per state, and the value dynamics onto a parametric critic, estimating both projections at sampled states to obtain coupled actor--critic flows. The score loss measures the actor's agreement with the current critic, while the policy-evaluation residual measures the critic's agreement with the actor. We also derive gradient and Hessian residuals, including a Feynman--Kac representation for the gradient equation, to control errors not detected by the projected value iteration. An exact decomposition of the HJB residual combines these errors into a policy-suboptimality bound under verification and logarithmic Sobolev assumptions. In the linear-quadratic class, both projections are exact and recover the pointwise iteration, and we provide numerical experiments on general models to demonstrate the coupled actor--critic learning in high-dimensions.
tldr: The paper develops a grid-free amortized actor-critic scheme for entropy-regularized infinite-horizon stochastic control based on continuous Langevin dynamics and score-Hamiltonian policy iteration.
motivation: Solving relaxed stochastic control problems in high dimensions is challenging due to grid-based methods and the need for per-state Langevin dynamics.
method: It projects the score residual onto a shared conditional sampler and the value dynamics onto a parametric critic, yielding coupled actor-critic flows, with gradient/Hessian residuals and an HJB residual decomposition.
result: The exact policy improvement rate is a discounted aggregate of relative Fisher information between the policy and its Hamiltonian's Gibbs law; in the linear-quadratic class the projections are exact and recover the pointwise iteration, and numerical experiments demonstrate high-dimensional learning.
conclusion: The framework provides a grid-free scheme with error control via a policy-suboptimality bound under verification and logarithmic Sobolev assumptions.

title: Quenched Growth Of Normal Matrices And Harmonic Measure
authors: Oleg Alekseev
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The eigenvalues of a large normal random matrix form a two-dimensional Coulomb gas. At fixed weight, the spectral droplet grows with the matrix rank, and its semiclassical density increment is harmonic measure. We freeze an [MATH]-eigenvalue configuration and sample [MATH] further eigenvalues using the projection onto polynomials of degree less than [MATH] that vanish at the frozen points. Their conditional law is an exact polynomial ensemble in the potential of the frozen charges. For a regular analytic droplet, we prove that the spatial distribution of the new eigenvalues converges to harmonic measure on the old boundary when [MATH] and [MATH]. This convergence holds conditionally on the frozen spectrum, outside a set of frozen configurations whose probability tends to zero. The equilibrium process formed from orthogonal polynomials of degrees [MATH] has the same limit. An exact finite-rank identity relates polynomial moments of the conditional mean to fluctuations of the frozen spectrum, with a remainder from polynomial modes of degree [MATH] and above.
tldr: The paper studies the growth of eigenvalues in large normal random matrices, showing that the incremental spectral distribution converges to harmonic measure on the original boundary.
motivation: Understanding how the spectrum of a random normal matrix grows when adding eigenvalues is a fundamental problem in random matrix theory and Coulomb gas physics.
method: The authors freeze an M-eigenvalue configuration, sample N further eigenvalues conditioned on the frozen points via a polynomial ensemble, and analyze the limiting spatial distribution for regular analytic droplets.
result: Conditional on the frozen spectrum outside a vanishing-probability set, the new eigenvalues' distribution converges to harmonic measure on the old boundary as M,N grow, and the same limit holds for the equilibrium process from orthogonal polynomials.
conclusion: The quenched growth of normal random matrices is governed by harmonic measure, with an exact finite-rank identity relating polynomial moments to fluctuations of the frozen spectrum.

title: Cdw-eis Calculations Of Atomic Ionization By Bare Ions And Antiprotons
authors: Dar\'io M. Mitnik, Jorge E. Miraglia, Claudia. C Montanari
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present calculations of atomic ionization by bare ions and antiprotons within the continuum distorted-wave eikonal initial-state (CDW-EIS) model. The dataset covers atomic targets from H to Kr, impacted by bare ions over a broad range of projectile charges and by antiprotons. Particular attention is given to elements in periods 3 and 4 of the periodic table, which are relevant to pigment analysis and technologically important materials. The resulting subshell-resolved total ionization cross sections are made openly available through an online repository covering a broad range of projectile--target systems, occupied initial subshells, and projectile velocities. We analyze systematic trends in the cross sections, including their dependence on projectile charge and velocity, binding-energy scaling, and charge-sign effects in proton and antiproton impact. To extend the practical coverage of the database, we also develop a neural-network surrogate, CDWEIS-NN, trained on the subset of the database with projectile charge [MATH]. The network interpolates the CDW-EIS results to additional projectile--target systems and impact energies, reproducing both held-out CDW-EIS calculations and the experimental benchmarks considered in this work with satisfactory accuracy.
tldr: The paper presents CDW-EIS calculations and a neural-network surrogate for atomic ionization cross sections by bare ions and antiprotons, aimed at applications in pigment analysis and materials.
motivation: There is a need for comprehensive, subshell-resolved ionization cross-section data across many projectile-target systems for applications such as pigment analysis and technologically relevant materials.
method: The authors use the continuum distorted-wave eikonal initial-state (CDW-EIS) model to compute ionization cross sections for targets from H to Kr, then train a neural-network surrogate (CDWEIS-NN) on a subset to interpolate to additional systems and energies.
result: The dataset provides subshell-resolved cross sections, reveals systematic trends in projectile charge, velocity, binding-energy scaling, and charge-sign effects, and the neural network reproduces held-out CDW-EIS calculations and experimental benchmarks with satisfactory accuracy.
conclusion: The openly available database and neural-network surrogate extend the practical coverage of CDW-EIS calculations, but the work lies in atomic collision physics and has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Lie Correspondence In The Setting Of Hopf And Frobenius Algebras
authors: Matt Alexander
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we demonstrate that Hopf algebras and Frobenius algebras provide an appropriate setting for an analogue of the classical Lie correspondence. We introduce a compatibility structure between Hopf and Frobenius algebras called Hopf-Frobenius modules, and give constructions that can be applied to any such module, which produce corresponding Lie groups and Lie algebras. Further, we show that classical Lie algebras and Lie groups give rise to Hopf-Frobenius modules for which the corresponding Lie groups and Lie algebras produced by our construction are those of the ordinary Lie correspondence.
tldr: The paper establishes an analogue of the classical Lie correspondence within the framework of Hopf and Frobenius algebras via a new compatibility structure called Hopf-Frobenius modules.
motivation: The classical Lie correspondence between Lie groups and Lie algebras is foundational, and the author seeks a more general algebraic setting in which an analogous correspondence can be formulated and recovered.
method: The author introduces Hopf-Frobenius modules, a compatibility structure combining Hopf and Frobenius algebras, and constructs Lie groups and Lie algebras from any such module.
result: Constructions are given that produce Lie groups and Lie algebras from Hopf-Frobenius modules, and it is shown that classical Lie algebras and Lie groups arise as Hopf-Frobenius modules yielding the ordinary Lie correspondence.
conclusion: Hopf and Frobenius algebras provide a suitable abstract setting for generalizing the Lie correspondence, subsuming the classical case as a special instance.

title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption For Statistical Modeling
authors: Balasubramanian Narasimhan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption allows arithmetic to be carried out on encrypted values, so that a party performing a computation need not see the data it operates on. This is useful wherever collaborating parties or sites cannot share data records or computed summaries yet need to do a joint analysis. We demonstrate the protocols needed to perform such analyses reproducibly via two packages in R, a platform widely used for applied statistics. The first, openfhe.R, is an interface to the OpenFHE C++ library, which exposes exact integer arithmetic (BFV, BGV), approximate real-valued arithmetic (CKKS), Boolean circuits, and multiparty key generation. The second is homomorpheR, which builds a small set of master/worker primitives for multi-party protocols on top of the first. Together, the two let an ordinary R statistical routine compose with an encrypted-arithmetic layer at the function-value boundary, provided the quantity crossing that boundary decomposes as a sum over sites. Two validation studies are presented: distributed stratified Cox regression, where stats4::mle() converges through an encrypted channel, and federated Cox-lasso via convex optimization using consensus ADMM, where the cross-site update is the only encrypted step. We also discuss federated similarity retrieval and two-party prediction. Throughout, the parties are assumed honest-but-curious, and threshold key generation removes the assumption that any single party holds a usable secret key.
tldr: The paper presents two R packages (openfhe.R and homomorpheR) that wrap the OpenFHE C++ fully homomorphic encryption library to enable privacy-preserving distributed statistical modeling such as federated Cox regression and Cox-lasso.
motivation: Collaborating parties or sites often cannot share raw data or computed summaries, yet still need joint statistical analyses; FHE offers a way to compute on encrypted values without revealing them.
method: The authors build an R interface to OpenFHE exposing BFV/BGV integer arithmetic, CKKS approximate real arithmetic, Boolean circuits, and multiparty threshold key generation, plus master/worker primitives for multi-party protocols where only quantities decomposable as sums over sites cross the encrypted boundary.
result: Two validation studies succeed: distributed stratified Cox regression where stats4::mle() converges through an encrypted channel, and federated Cox-lasso via consensus ADMM with the cross-site update as the sole encrypted step, under an honest-but-curious threat model with threshold key generation.
conclusion: FHE is shown to be practically composable with ordinary R statistical routines for federated analyses, demonstrating usable tooling for privacy-preserving collaborative statistics.

title: Learning To Watermark Speech Synthesis Against Model-Driven Reconstruction
authors: Weizhi Liu, Yue Li, Hui Tian, Zhaoxia Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern TTS systems increasingly generate synthetic speech at scale for diverse users. This setting calls for content-level provenance that can verify the origin of released speech and attribute it to the requesting user, which generative watermarking can support by embedding multi-bit identifiers directly into synthesized speech. Once released, however, speech may undergo heterogeneous learned transformations during distribution and editing, with reconstruction objectives that can preserve speech utility while affecting watermark recoverability differently. We find that no single watermark carrier remains consistently reliable across reconstruction models, as its survival depends jointly on the embedded structure, reconstruction mechanism, and observation representation. To this end, we propose Thrive, a multi-bit generative speech watermarking framework for modern autoregressive TTS, covering both discrete-token and continuous-representation generation under reconstruction attacks. Specifically, Rise synchronizes watermark injection into intermediate representations with its continued integration into subsequent generation, while Care combines waveform and spectral experts using bit-wise reliability selection. Experiments on both autoregressive paradigms show that Thrive preserves synthesis fidelity, achieves 87.6% average recovery accuracy under reconstruction attacks, and supports source attribution over candidate sets of up to 10,000 identities.
tldr: The paper proposes Thrive, a multi-bit generative speech watermarking framework for autoregressive TTS that remains recoverable under reconstruction attacks.
motivation: Modern TTS systems need content-level provenance to verify origin and attribute released speech to users, but learned distribution and editing transformations can disrupt watermark recovery.
method: Thrive synchronizes watermark injection into intermediate representations with continued generation (Rise) and combines waveform and spectral experts via bit-wise reliability selection (Care) to handle both discrete-token and continuous-representation generation.
result: Experiments on two autoregressive paradigms show preservation of synthesis fidelity, 87.6% average recovery accuracy under reconstruction attacks, and source attribution over up to 10,000 identities.
conclusion: The framework demonstrates robust multi-bit speech watermarking against model-driven reconstruction, enabling scalable provenance for synthetic speech.

title: Sera-ids: Structured Experience Retrieval-Augmented Intrusion Detection With Small Language Models
authors: Ayesha S. Dina Md Shamimul Islam
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a flexible approach to network intrusion detection, but direct classification of numerical flow records can be unreliable without traffic- specific decision boundaries. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enables LLMs to leverage external experience; however, free-form textual experience requires the model to infer the numerical conditions that distinguish traffic classes. We propose SERA-IDS, a Structured Experience Retrieval-Augmented Intru- sion Detection framework that learns decision knowledge from classification errors. A Small Language Model (SLM) analyzes misclassified flows and generates structured rules containing behavioral descriptions, feature conditions, class-confusion infor- mation, tool-derived confidence, and provenance. A confidence gate admits supported rules into the Experience Library. During testing, the library is frozen, and retrieved class-diverse rules are condition-matched to the query flow and provided as evidence to the decision SLM. The same library is evaluated with three small, locally deployable SLMs, namely Llama 3.1, Phi-4:14B, and Qwen2.5:7B, without fine-tuning or paid hosted inference. On the test sets, SERA-IDS improves macro F1 on NF-BoT- IoT from 11.66%, 9.26%, and 7.83% to 86.46%, 69.50%, and 83.51%, respectively, and on NF-ToN-IoT from 3.82%, 6.17%, and 1.94% to 84.16%, 87.66%, and 83.37%. These results show that structured experience retrieval enables small, free, and locally deployable SLMs to achieve strong intrusion-detection performance, including performance exceeding that of the re- ported existing work used in our comparison.
tldr: SERA-IDS combines retrieval-augmented generation with structured, rule-based experience libraries derived from classification errors to let small language models perform network intrusion detection without fine-tuning.
motivation: LLMs can aid network intrusion detection, but directly classifying numerical flow records is unreliable, and free-form textual experience forces the model to infer numeric decision boundaries itself.
method: A small language model analyzes misclassified flows and emits structured rules (behavioral descriptions, feature conditions, class-confusion info, tool-derived confidence, provenance); a confidence gate admits supported rules into a frozen Experience Library that is queried at test time with class-diverse, condition-matched evidence.
result: Evaluated with Llama 3.1, Phi-4:14B, and Qwen2.5:7B without fine-tuning, macro F1 improves from 11.66%/9.26%/7.83% to 86.46%/69.50%/83.51% on NF-BoT-IoT and from 3.82%/6.17%/1.94% to 84.16%/87.66%/83.37% on NF-ToN-IoT.
conclusion: Structured experience retrieval enables small, locally deployable, free SLMs to achieve competitive network intrusion-detection performance, surpassing the reported existing baselines compared against.

title: What Gradients Add To Text Leakage In Split Language Models, Counted Per Token And Per Document
authors: Evangelos Pappas Georgios Politis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Split learning lets a client train a language model on a server without sending its text. The client runs the first layers itself and sends the server only their output, a vector of numbers for each token. During training, the server sends gradients back. We show that an observer at the split can rebuild most of the client's text from this traffic, and we measure how much the gradients help. On GPT-2, an attacker who holds only the publicly released weights of the client's layers recovers 94.20% of tokens from the activations alone and 97.38% when it also sees the gradients, 3.17 percentage points more 95% interval [2.72, 3.64]. Counted by document, the difference is much larger. The attacker rebuilds 13.71% of 32-token documents exactly without the gradients and 37.77% with them, because a document only counts when every token is right. How we count also changes how good a defence looks. Secret mixup, which blends each outgoing vector with a decoy, stops the attacker from rebuilding almost any document exactly, yet the attacker still recovers 83-91% of tokens. In a second experiment on GPT-2 and Qwen3-0.6B, where the server trains only a run of consecutive layers, the layer at which the run starts changes both model quality and leakage, even when the run's length is fixed. We recommend reporting leakage both per token and per document, and treating what a split model sends as being as sensitive as the text itself.
tldr: Gradients meaningfully increase text leakage in split language-model training, especially when leakage is counted per document rather than per token.
motivation: Split learning is intended to protect client text by sending only intermediate activations, but an observer at the split may reconstruct the original text from activations and gradients.
method: The authors attack GPT-2 and Qwen3-0.6B split models, reconstructing client text from activations alone and with gradients, and evaluate token-level versus document-level leakage plus a secret mixup defense.
result: On GPT-2, token recovery rises from 94.20% with activations alone to 97.38% with gradients, while exact 32-token document recovery increases from 13.71% to 37.77%; secret mixup blocks exact documents but still leaves 83-91% token recovery.
conclusion: The authors recommend reporting leakage both per token and per document, and treating split-model traffic as sensitive as the original text.

title: Electrical And Optical Dipole Polarizabilities Of Two Lowest Triplet States Of The Beryllium Atom
authors: Krzysztof Strasburger Tymoteusz Mrozek
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-accuracy static and dynamic polarizabilities of the [MATH] and [MATH] states of the neutral beryllium atom are reported. The calculations employed explicitly correlated Gaussian (ECG) basis sets, and first-order wave functions were obtained by minimization of the Hylleraas functional. The final basis sets used for the response-property calculations contained c.a. 7000-8000 functions, depending on the polarizability component and the chosen symmetry. The results cover frequencies from the static limit, \(\omega = 0\), up to the third resonance for the \(2^{3}P_{u}\) state and up to the second resonance for the \(3^{3}S_{g}\) state. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first calculations of dynamic and static polarizabilities for these excited states of the beryllium atom using explicitly correlated basis sets.
tldr: High-accuracy calculations of static and dynamic dipole polarizabilities for the two lowest triplet states of neutral beryllium using explicitly correlated Gaussian basis sets.
motivation: Polarizabilities of excited states are important for precision atomic spectroscopy and response-property studies, but high-accuracy data for these beryllium triplet states were previously lacking.
method: Explicitly correlated Gaussian basis sets with first-order wave functions obtained by minimizing the Hylleraas functional; response properties were computed with roughly 7000–8000 basis functions across symmetries and frequencies.
result: Static and dynamic polarizabilities are reported from ω=0 up to the third resonance for the 2^3P_u state and up to the second resonance for the 3^3S_g state, claimed as the first such calculations using ECG basis sets.
conclusion: The work provides benchmark polarizability data for excited beryllium triplet states, useful for atomic physics and spectroscopy, but it is not aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Branching Gaps, Coexistence, And Boundary Influence For The Ising Model On Spherically Symmetric Trees
authors: Otabek Khakimov Farrukh Mukhamedov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor Ising model on rooted spherically symmetric trees with one or \(q\) children per vertex, according to a prescribed sequence of branching levels. Unbounded runs of one-child levels force uniqueness at every nonzero homogeneous field and every finite inverse temperature. We quantify this effect through the locations of sufficiently long nonbranching stretches. Conversely, uniqueness need not entail any uniform rate: for each prescribed vanishing sequence, we construct a density-one tree whose finite-volume boundary influence decays more slowly along a subsequence. The tree retains branching number \(q\), although its nonzero-field coexistence region disappears. For eventually bounded gaps, we prove an optimal uniform comparison with the periodic tree having the largest allowed gap and obtain an explicit interval of coexistence fields. Thus bounded gaps are equivalent, within this family, to coexistence at some finite temperature and nonzero field. For eventually periodic gaps, Gibbs uniqueness is equivalent to fixed-point uniqueness of the full-period return map. A negative Schwarzian derivative yields a complete classification: in the supercritical regime the map has three fixed points inside a closed coexistence interval, two at its endpoints, and one outside. The nonzero endpoints are automatically nondegenerate folds, with square-root splitting of the merging branches.
tldr: The paper analyzes ferromagnetic Ising models on rooted spherically symmetric trees with variable branching levels, relating branching gaps to Gibbs uniqueness, coexistence, and boundary influence decay.
motivation: Understanding how nonuniform branching affects phase transitions and boundary effects on tree-like graphs is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics and probability.
method: The authors use rigorous mathematical analysis of Gibbs measures, return maps, and Schwarzian derivative to classify uniqueness, coexistence regions, and boundary influence decay for prescribed branching sequences.
result: They show that unbounded runs of one-child levels force uniqueness, bounded gaps imply nonzero-field coexistence at finite temperature, and periodic gaps reduce uniqueness to fixed-point uniqueness of the return map, with fold bifurcations at coexistence boundaries.
conclusion: Branching structure quantitatively controls phase coexistence and boundary influence in tree Ising models, yielding a complete classification under negative Schwarzian derivative.

title: Concave Roofs And Downward Recovery For DR-Submodular Polynomial Maximization
authors: Donglei Du
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give approximation algorithms for [MATH], where [MATH] is a nonempty compact down-closed convex subset of the unit cube and [MATH] is a nonnegative diminishing-returns (DR) submodular polynomial: every entry of its Hessian is nonpositive on the cube. Starting from quadratic or cubic coefficients, we decompose the objective exactly into nonnegative rooted atoms and affine terms. Concave upper bounds for these components give a tractable roof. We then decrease the coordinates of a roof optimizer using maps that work for all components at once, recovering a fraction of the roof value while preserving feasibility. For quadratics, we also retain the concave diagonal residual exactly. Under the stated assumptions on optimization access, these constructions give deterministic polynomial-time factors of [MATH] for quadratics and [MATH] for cubics, up to any prescribed additive error. The cubic result includes positive cubic coefficients and repeated variables. The factor [MATH] also holds for two larger classes: supplied compatible rooted certificates of literal degree at most twelve, and sums of nonnegative submodular local functions of arity at most four. At arbitrary finite literal degree, a common scalar map attains the optimal single-map factor [MATH]. Global monotonicity and concave-cardinality structure give stronger guarantees for multilinear local-function sums, with no recovery beyond the identity map. Standard matroid rounding transfers the multilinear guarantees without loss. We also prove online preservation for directed-hypergraph cuts and, separately, a Unique-Games inapproximability bound of approximately [MATH] for explicit quadratic input under a cardinality upper bound.
tldr: The paper develops approximation algorithms for maximizing nonnegative diminishing-returns submodular polynomials over down-closed convex sets using concave roof decompositions and coordinate-decreasing recovery maps.
motivation: Submodular polynomial maximization captures non-convex optimization problems with diminishing returns, but prior methods lack tight guarantees for higher-order polynomials and structured constraints.
method: The objective is decomposed exactly into nonnegative rooted atoms and affine terms, upper-bounded by concave roofs; then a roof optimizer is adjusted downward via maps that preserve feasibility and recover a fraction of the roof value.
result: Deterministic polynomial-time approximation factors are obtained for quadratic and cubic cases, extended to supplied rooted certificates and sums of local functions, with a Unique Games inapproximability bound for quadratics.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified approach to submodular polynomial maximization, achieving optimal single-map factors and transferring guarantees through matroid rounding and online preservation results.

title: Learning In Large Populations With Anticipatory Payoffs: Bregman Meets Willems And Lyapunov
authors: Nuno C. Martins Tzuyu Jeng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study evolutionary Nash equilibrium learning in large populations whose payoffs are generated by dynamic mechanisms. Counterclockwise dissipativity (CCW) provides a passivity-like framework for establishing learning/convergence under a broad convex cone of so-called well-behaved learning rules satisfying a natural payoff-alignment condition according to which, away from equilibria, the population's state (strategic profile) moves in a direction positively correlated with the payoffs. The cone is closed under conic combinations and encompasses a broad range of noise-free rules, including discontinuous rules such as best response, imitative rules such as the replicator rule that is not [MATH]-passive, and all noise-free [MATH]-passive rules. Existing CCW results require no knowledge of the particular rule, but establish convergence without providing a Lyapunov function or Lyapunov stability. We develop a methodology that closes this gap by constructing rule-independent Lyapunov functions from CCW storage functions of the payoff mechanism. For a nonlinear class of anticipatory mechanisms, in which agents compare current payoffs with those associated with a smoothed population state, we show that a storage can be derived as a Bregman divergence. The resulting Lyapunov function combines a potential gap with this divergence and establishes global asymptotic stability. A congestion game with a nonlinear congestion-growth toll illustrates the results.
tldr: The paper develops rule-independent Lyapunov functions via counterclockwise dissipativity and Bregman divergence to prove global asymptotic stability for evolutionary Nash equilibrium learning in large populations with anticipatory payoffs.
motivation: Existing counterclockwise dissipativity results establish convergence of well-behaved learning rules but lack explicit Lyapunov functions and Lyapunov stability, limiting their explanatory power.
method: The authors construct Lyapunov functions from storage functions of the payoff mechanism, derive a storage as a Bregman divergence for a nonlinear class of anticipatory mechanisms, and combine a potential gap with this divergence.
result: They prove global asymptotic stability for the considered learning dynamics and illustrate the results with a congestion game featuring a nonlinear congestion-growth toll.
conclusion: The work bridges control-theoretic passivity, game-theoretic learning, and convex optimization, providing a general Lyapunov-based framework for equilibrium convergence in large populations.

title: Minimax Rates For Learning Smooth Populations Of Parameters
authors: Edward H. Kennedy Jungho Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study pointwise estimation of a smooth binomial mixing density and characterize its minimax rates. Assuming that the mixing density is [MATH]-H\"older smooth, we first consider the homogeneous setting with a common number of binomial trials [MATH]. We derive matching lower and upper bounds that reveal three regimes depending on the relative sizes of the sample size [MATH] and the number of trials [MATH]. When [MATH] is small, the finite number of trials creates an identification barrier that persists regardless of sample size; at intermediate [MATH], more data reduce sampling uncertainty, while the number of trials limits how finely the mixing density can be recovered; and when [MATH] is sufficiently large, the usual nonparametric density estimation rate is recovered. Our lower bounds exploit the polynomial structure of the binomial mixture model, while attainability is achieved by a suitably regularized orthogonal series estimator. We then extend the analysis to heterogeneous trial parameters, where the minimax rate depends on the full trial profile through the effective sample size available at each polynomial degree. These results characterize the fundamental statistical limits of learning smooth populations of binomial probabilities under both homogeneous and heterogeneous trials.
tldr: The paper characterizes minimax rates for estimating a smooth binomial mixing density under homogeneous and heterogeneous trial parameters.
motivation: Understanding fundamental statistical limits for learning smooth populations of binomial probabilities is important in mixture models and nonparametric estimation.
method: The authors derive matching lower and upper bounds using polynomial structure and a regularized orthogonal series estimator.
result: They identify three regimes depending on sample size and number of trials, and extend the analysis to heterogeneous trials via an effective sample size per degree.
conclusion: The work provides a complete minimax rate characterization for smooth binomial mixture density estimation in both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings.

title: Spectral Rigidity In Toroidal Grothendieck Rings And Multiparameter Quantum Groups
authors: Yu Zhang Xiaomin Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a bipartite Dynkin quiver of finite simply-laced type and [MATH] the corresponding Hernandez--Leclerc category. We study a two-parameter specialization of the Fedele--Hernandez toroidal Grothendieck ring and identify its generic positive part with a Cartan-type multiparameter quantum group. The structural input is the identity \[ 2D^{(2)}-D_0=\omega_Q\circ(\deg_Q,\deg_Q), \] where [MATH] are the two effective toroidal commutation forms and [MATH] is the antisymmetric Euler form of \(Q\). It realizes the specialized character algebra, after an auxiliary scalar extension, as a graded bicharacter twist of the one-parameter algebra at [MATH]. This yields the required root grading and PBW graded dimensions. For every source--sink edge [MATH], these dimensions combine with the local \(A\)--\(Y\) commutation formula to give a quadratic annihilator for \(_{Z_r}\). Consequently \[ _{Z_r}(Z_s)=\{t_0t,t_0^{-1}\}, \] without thinness or type-specific character formulas. The two spectral values yield the oriented multiparameter Serre relations. With \[ q_{ii}=t_0^2t,\qquad q_{ij}=t_0^{-1},\qquad q_{ji}=t_0^{-1}t^{-1}\quad(i\to j), \] and \(q_{ij}=1\) on nonedges, we obtain \[ U_{\mathbf q}^{+}(\mathfrak g) \simeq \mathscr K_\infty(\mathscr C_Q)\otimes_RK \] for [MATH] of type [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies a two-parameter specialization of the Fedele-Hernandez toroidal Grothendieck ring and identifies its generic positive part with a Cartan-type multiparameter quantum group via spectral rigidity and annihilator conditions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structure of toroidal Grothendieck rings and their connection to multiparameter quantum groups through spectral rigidity and root grading.
method: They use the identity involving the two effective toroidal commutation forms and the antisymmetric Euler form of a bipartite Dynkin quiver to realize a specialized character algebra as a graded bicharacter twist, then derive quadratic annihilators and Serre relations.
result: For source-sink edges, the annihilator yields two spectral values t0t and t0^{-1}, which produce oriented multiparameter Serre relations and an isomorphism U_q^+(g) ≅ K_∞(C_Q) ⊗_R K for type A_n.
conclusion: This provides a spectral rigidity approach to constructing multiparameter quantum groups from toroidal Grothendieck rings without thinness or type-specific character formulas.

title: An Inverse-stochastic-control Galerkin Estimator For Drift Potentials
authors: Yumiharu Nakano
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the ill-posed inverse problem of recovering the drift potential of an overdamped Langevin diffusion from discrete, possibly irregular position observations. Specializing the suboptimality gap for inverse stochastic control to drift-potential recovery, we parametrize the associated value function in a finite basis. Under a basis nondegeneracy condition, the resulting Galerkin estimator is obtained from one positive-definite linear system whose entries are smooth functionals of the empirical time marginals; no transition density is required. The gap equals one half of the squared energy distance to the true potential, yielding a best-approximation identity and energy-seminorm consistency as the basis becomes complete. At a fixed basis, we separate the sample fluctuation from the time-quadrature error, thereby avoiding the Euler--Maruyama [MATH] drift-discretization bias. We also analyze the finite basis as regularization, give a dimension-dependent convergence rate for a concrete basis family, and bound observation-noise bias. One- and two-dimensional experiments verify the predicted sampling-interval behavior. An application to irregular animal telemetry illustrates the method on a single long trajectory.
tldr: The paper develops a Galerkin estimator for recovering the drift potential of an overdamped Langevin diffusion from discrete position observations, using an inverse-stochastic-control suboptimality gap.
motivation: Recovering drift potentials from irregular, discrete observations is an ill-posed inverse problem that arises in stochastic modeling and data-driven dynamics, and standard Euler-Maruyama approaches introduce discretization bias.
method: The suboptimality gap of inverse stochastic control is specialized to drift-potential recovery, parametrizing the value function in a finite basis; under a basis nondegeneracy condition a positive-definite linear system yields the Galerkin estimator from empirical time marginals without requiring transition densities.
result: The gap equals half the squared energy distance to the true potential, giving a best-approximation identity and energy-seminorm consistency, with sample-fluctuation/time-quadrature error separated, a dimension-dependent convergence rate for a concrete basis family, and bounds on observation-noise bias, verified in 1D/2D experiments and animal telemetry.
conclusion: The method provides a principled, bias-avoiding estimator for drift potentials, but it is a purely classical stochastic-analysis and statistical-estimation contribution with no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Inference Of Hamiltonian And Lie-Poisson Structures From Vector Field Samples
authors: Georg A. Gottwald Jason E. Frank
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a method for the data-driven inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson dynamical systems from vector-field samples, in which the Hamiltonian and the underlying Poisson tensor are estimated jointly rather than assuming the structure is known. The Hamiltonian is represented as a linear combination of random feature maps with fixed random internal weights, so its estimation is a linear regression problem for any given Poisson structure. We treat three cases of increasing generality: a known Poisson tensor, an unknown constant invertible (symplectic) structure matrix, and Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson structures, with structure matrix linear in the state. In the constant case, the Hamiltonian and structure matrix are recovered jointly from an eigenvalue problem that avoids the trivial zero solution due to the scaling symmetry of Hamiltonian systems. For Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson systems we alternate between an initial Hamiltonian estimate from a generalized eigenvalue problem for an approximate first integral, and a constrained nonlinear least-squares fit of the structure constants that enforces the Jacobi identity and, for affine structures, the cocycle condition, via continuation in a penalty parameter. Orthogonal matching pursuit selects a compact, well-conditioned subset of random features. Because the learned Hamiltonian is a sum of single-feature terms, the model admits an explicit Poisson/symplectic splitting integrator, which we use to validate the learned systems via long-time Poincare sections. We demonstrate the approach on the four- and five-dimensional Lorenz-86 model and a six-dimensional Kirchhoff rigid-body system, recovering Hamiltonians, structure constants and Casimir invariants to high accuracy, and showing the inferred Poincare sections converge to the correct invariant-tori topology as the number of random features increases.
tldr: The paper presents a data-driven method to jointly infer Hamiltonians and Poisson/Lie-Poisson structures from vector-field samples using random feature maps and optimization.
motivation: Classical Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson systems are fundamental in mechanics, but inferring their governing structure from data remains challenging, especially when the Poisson tensor is unknown.
method: The authors represent the Hamiltonian as a linear combination of random features and solve for the Hamiltonian and structure matrix jointly via eigenvalue problems, alternating least squares, and continuation with penalty terms enforcing the Jacobi identity and cocycle condition.
result: The approach recovers Hamiltonians, structure constants, and Casimir invariants for the Lorenz-86 model and Kirchhoff rigid-body system with high accuracy, and the inferred Poincaré sections converge to correct invariant-tori topology.
