conclusion: The method enables interpretable, structure-preserving learning of Hamiltonian dynamics and provides an explicit splitting integrator for long-time validation.

title: An Extremal Formula For Elliptical Width And The Bourin--Lee Conjecture
authors: Mohammad Sababheh
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(X\in M_n(\mathbb C)\), \(n\geq2\), and let \[ \delta_2(X) = \sup_{\dim S=2}\delta(X_S), \] where \(X_S\) denotes the compression of \(X\) to \(S\), and \(\delta(X_S)\) is the diameter of the largest disk contained in the numerical range \(W(X_S)\). Bourin and Lee proved that every positive block matrix \[ M= A&X X^*&B \] satisfies \[ \leq+\delta_2(X). \] In the same work, they conjectured that the inequality \[ \leq \] for every positive block matrix with prescribed off-diagonal block \(X\) characterizes essentially Hermitian matrices. We resolve this conjecture by proving the stronger exact formula \[ \sup_{\left(A&X\\X^*&B\right)\geq0} \left\{ A&X\\X^*&B} - \right\} = \delta_2(X). \] Thus the elliptical width is precisely the optimal norm defect associated with a fixed off-diagonal block. The reverse inequality is obtained by lifting an arbitrary two-dimensional compression of \(X\) to an explicit family of positive block matrices, yielding quantitative two-sided estimates with error of order \(t^{-1}\). As a consequence, the norm inequality above holds universally if and only if \(X\) is essentially Hermitian, proving Conjecture 3.3 of Bourin and Lee. We also construct an explicit \(3\times3\) normal example showing that the radius constant in their normal-off-diagonal eigenvalue estimate is optimal at the leading eigenvalue level. By direct-sum amplification of this construction, we further prove that the same radius constant is sharp at every eigenvalue level \(j\geq0\), thereby resolving their corresponding sharpness question.
tldr: The paper resolves the Bourin–Lee conjecture by proving an exact formula expressing the elliptical width of a matrix as the optimal norm defect of positive block matrices with a fixed off-diagonal block.
motivation: The work addresses a conjecture by Bourin and Lee characterizing essentially Hermitian matrices through a norm inequality for positive block matrices, and studies the sharpness of a related radius constant.
method: It uses matrix analysis techniques, lifting arbitrary two-dimensional compressions of X to explicit families of positive block matrices, and direct-sum amplification to prove sharpness at every eigenvalue level.
result: It establishes the exact formula sup over positive block matrices of the norm defect equals delta_2(X), proves the universal norm inequality holds iff X is essentially Hermitian, and shows the radius constant is optimal at all eigenvalue levels.
conclusion: The Bourin–Lee conjecture is fully resolved, providing quantitative two-sided estimates and sharp constants for the elliptical width characterization.

title: Jasper: Special Session On Joint Reliability And Security Assessment Of SPlit Computing For Edge Robustness
authors: Enrico Magliano, Giuseppe Esposito, Amir Hossein Shahdadian, Rama Mounika Kodamanchili, Juan David Guerrero Balaguera, Juan Esteban Rodriguez Condia, Annachiara Ruospo, Roberta Siciliano, Stefano Di Carlo, Maksim Jenihhin, Marco Levorato, Alessandro Savino, Matteo Sonza Reorda, Christian Herglotz, Michael H\"ubner, Mahdi Taheri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Split Computing (SC) enables efficient deployment of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) by partitioning inference between edge devices and cloud servers. However, intermediate feature representations are simultaneously exposed to hardware faults and adversarial attacks, which are traditionally evaluated independently. This paper presents a unified framework for the joint assessment of reliability and security in Split Computing. First, reliability is characterized through neuron-level fault injection using the Mean Relative Accuracy Degradation (MRAD) while security through feature-map-aware adversarial attacks simulations using the Attack Success Rate (ASR). Based on these complementary analyses, the Joint Vulnerability Score (JVS) is introduced, along with a confidence-aware extension that jointly captures prediction errors and confidence degradation. The framework is evaluated on ten Split Computing configurations based on ResNet-50 trained on ILSVRC-2012. Experimental results show substantial differences across compression strategies, with MRAD ranging from 44.3% to 61.2% under fault injection, while adversarial attacks achieve up to 98.8% ASR. Furthermore, the proposed joint metrics reveal vulnerability trends that remain hidden when reliability and security are analyzed independently, providing a more comprehensive methodology for designing dependable Split Computing systems.
tldr: This paper introduces a unified framework, including a Joint Vulnerability Score (JVS), for jointly assessing hardware reliability and adversarial security of Split Computing deployments of DNNs on edge devices.
motivation: Split Computing partitions DNN inference between edge devices and cloud servers, but the intermediate feature representations are exposed to both hardware faults and adversarial attacks, which are traditionally evaluated in isolation rather than jointly.
method: The authors perform neuron-level fault injection to characterize reliability via Mean Relative Accuracy Degradation (MRAD) and feature-map-aware adversarial attack simulations to measure Attack Success Rate (ASR), then combine both into the Joint Vulnerability Score and a confidence-aware extension.
result: Across ten Split Computing configurations using ResNet-50 on ILSVRC-2012, MRAD varied from 44.3% to 61.2% under fault injection and adversarial attacks reached up to 98.8% ASR, with the joint metrics exposing vulnerability trends invisible to independent analyses.
conclusion: The proposed joint assessment methodology is argued to provide a more comprehensive basis for designing dependable Split Computing systems.

title: Identification And Recovery Of Linear Dynamics From Partial Trajectories
authors: Le Gong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the joint recovery of an unknown system matrix [MATH] and a rank-[MATH] initial-state matrix [MATH] from partial observations of the state matrices [MATH], for [MATH]. Each trajectory is observed at a fixed set of state coordinates, which may differ across trajectories. We derive necessary conditions for identifiability, including obstructions arising from incomplete spatial coverage and insufficient dynamical span, as well as lower bounds on the number of observations. We then characterize the Jacobian of the measurement map, account for the intrinsic symmetry of the low-rank factorization, and establish a rank-certificate principle yielding generic local identifiability. When the trajectories whose initial states form a basis of [MATH] are fully observed, we obtain necessary and sufficient rank conditions for global recovery, together with explicit reconstruction formulas. We formulate the joint recovery problem as a nonlinear least-squares problem over the system matrix [MATH] and the low-rank factors of [MATH], and solve it using Adam. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real-world data evaluate the recovery performance under different spatial sampling rates and observation horizons.
tldr: The paper studies identifiability and recovery of an unknown linear system matrix and a low-rank initial-state matrix from partially observed trajectories.
motivation: Many systems are observed only at limited coordinates, so it is important to understand when the underlying linear dynamics and initial states can be uniquely recovered from such partial data.
method: The authors derive necessary conditions for identifiability, analyze the Jacobian of the measurement map, account for low-rank factorization symmetry, establish generic local identifiability, and solve the joint recovery problem via nonlinear least squares with Adam.
result: They obtain rank conditions for global recovery in a special fully observed case with explicit reconstruction formulas, and provide numerical experiments on synthetic and real-world data under different sampling rates and observation horizons.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical and algorithmic foundations for recovering linear dynamics from partial trajectory observations, but it is not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Logit-Aware Mimo AirComp For Distributed Mixture-of-Experts Llm Inference Over Wireless Edge Networks
authors: Lyutianyang Zhang, Yunjian Jia, Liu Cao, Dengke Wang, Jinke Ren, Shuguang Cui
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed mixture-of-experts (MoE) inference is a promising architecture for deploying large language models (LLMs) at wireless edge networks because sparse experts can be placed across coordinated base stations (BSs), while the anchor node and user equipment (UE) can offload LLM inference tasks to BSs. The communication bottleneck is the MoE aggregation, where the anchor BS must recover a weighted sum of selected expert outputs before each decoding step. Over-the-air computation (AirComp) is well matched to this operation because the wireless multiple-access channel naturally superposes simultaneous transmissions. However, conventional AirComp minimizes communication distortion, whereas MoE aggregation errors have unequal impact on LLM outputs. We propose a logit-aware MIMO AirComp framework that estimates local logit sensitivity as block-level weights and jointly optimizes receive combiners and BS precoders under per-BS power constraints. We also develop an alternating algorithm that protects decoding decisions from aggregation perturbations. Using OpenCompass, we evaluate Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 on GSM8K and ARC-Challenge. At 30 dB aggregation SNR, perturbed Qwen3 retains 99.3% of clean GSM8K accuracy and 94.8% of clean ARC-Challenge accuracy. In a direct ARC-Challenge closed-loop audit over 295 examples, SW-AirComp achieves 43.73% accuracy at 30 dB and 26.78% at 20 dB, outperforming unweighted, matched-filter, and zero-forcing AirComp. In the wireless simulator, SW-AirComp reduces decision-relevant aggregation distortion; at 20 dB, its final weighted-sum mean-squared error is 53.5% lower than unweighted AirComp under the same channels, samples, and sensitivity weights. Logit-RMSE and logit-gap diagnostics further show that the gain comes from reducing output-logit perturbation and lowering the risk of top-token changes.
tldr: The paper proposes a logit-aware MIMO over-the-air computation framework to improve distributed mixture-of-experts LLM inference over wireless edge networks by optimizing precoders and combiners according to output-logit sensitivity.
motivation: Distributed MoE inference at the wireless edge is bottlenecked by aggregation of expert outputs, and conventional AirComp minimizes communication distortion rather than the decision-relevant impact of aggregation errors on LLM outputs.
method: The authors estimate local logit sensitivity as block-level weights and jointly optimize receive combiners and BS precoders under per-BS power constraints via an alternating algorithm that protects decoding decisions from aggregation perturbations.
result: Using Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8, the logit-aware SW-AirComp retains 99.3% GSM8K and 94.8% ARC-Challenge accuracy at 30 dB, achieves 43.73% ARC-Challenge accuracy at 30 dB, and reduces final weighted-sum MSE by 53.5% versus unweighted AirComp at 20 dB.
conclusion: Logit-aware weighting improves decision-relevant aggregation fidelity and LLM accuracy in wireless distributed MoE inference, but the work is classical wireless communications and machine learning with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Strictly Unfriendly $k$-Partitions: Sharp Degree Thresholds And ETH-Based Lower Bounds
authors: Sanjay Jain, Frank Stephan, Haoyun Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a complete complexity classification and fine-grained analysis for the Strictly Unfriendly [MATH]-Partition problem ([MATH]), which asks whether the vertices of a graph can be partitioned into [MATH] classes such that every vertex has strictly more neighbors in each of the other [MATH] classes than in its own. We first establish a sharp tractability-intractability threshold with respect to the maximum degree [MATH]: for [MATH], [MATH] is solvable in polynomial time when [MATH], but becomes [MATH]-hard and ETH-hard immediately on subcubic graphs ([MATH]), resolving the degree limitations in prior work and establishing subcubic graphs as the precise frontier of intractability. Furthermore, under the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), we establish the first fine-grained lower bounds via direct reductions from [MATH]-SAT. On general graphs, we establish a uniform lower bound across all partition parameters [MATH], revealing a striking complexity convergence where the core exponential complexity remains invariant despite technical divergences in gadget constructions. On subcubic graphs, we formally quantify the "cost of sparsity," deriving explicit lower bound constants to demonstrate how enforced structural degree restrictions degrade reduction efficiency.
tldr: The paper provides a complete complexity classification and fine-grained ETH-based lower bounds for the Strictly Unfriendly k-Partition problem on graphs, establishing sharp degree thresholds and reduction costs.
motivation: The problem generalizes unfriendly partitions and had unresolved degree limitations; the authors aim to pin down the exact tractability frontier and quantify exponential-time lower bounds.
method: They use polynomial-time algorithms for bounded degree cases and direct reductions from k-SAT under the Exponential Time Hypothesis to derive fine-grained lower bounds and gadget constructions.
result: They prove a sharp threshold: for maximum degree ≤2 the problem is polynomial-time solvable, while on subcubic graphs (degree ≤3) it becomes NP-hard and ETH-hard, with explicit lower bound constants on general and subcubic graphs.
conclusion: The work resolves the degree frontier for Strictly Unfriendly k-Partition and quantifies the 'cost of sparsity' in reductions, offering a complete complexity landscape for this partition problem.

title: Learning Ota: A Unified Framework For Edge Sensing, Computation, And Communication
authors: Mehdi Karbalayghareh, David J. Love, Christopher G. Brinton
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most federated learning (FL) studies implicitly assume that training data is readily available at participating edge devices. In practice, this data must first be acquired through heterogeneous sensors with potentially different measurement modalities, and the quality and cost of this acquisition process can directly affect the learning performance. This dependence creates a coupled relationship among sensing, computation, and communication, necessitating a system model that captures their joint effect on resource efficiency and learning accuracy. This paper develops such a unified treatment for an over-the-air (OTA) FL system in which each device configures its sensing modality, power, resolution, and sample size, with aggregations conducted OTA at the server. We derive models for sensing noise, energy consumption, latency, and OTA aggregation distortion, and establish a non-convex convergence bound quantifying how these factors influence the global model trajectory. Guided by this analysis, we formulate a per-round optimization that balances energy, latency, and learning quality under physical device constraints. The resulting mixed optimization is addressed through an alternating procedure with closed-form and one-dimensional updates for continuous variables and a lightweight discrete search. Numerical experiments corroborate the advantage of jointly optimizing sensing, computation, and communication decisions.
tldr: This paper develops a unified optimization framework for over-the-air federated learning that jointly configures sensing, computation, and communication resources at edge devices.
motivation: Federated learning studies often assume data is readily available at edge devices, while in practice it must be acquired via heterogeneous sensors whose quality and cost affect learning performance.
method: The authors model sensing noise, energy, latency, and over-the-air aggregation distortion, derive a non-convex convergence bound, and solve a per-round mixed optimization via alternating closed-form, one-dimensional, and discrete search updates.
result: Numerical experiments show that jointly optimizing sensing, computation, and communication decisions improves resource efficiency and learning accuracy compared to baselines.
conclusion: A coupled system model and optimization framework are proposed for OTA federated learning, demonstrating the benefits of cross-layer resource allocation in edge sensing-computation-communication systems.

title: Time-dependent Integrable Quantum Field Theories With Dynamical Boundaries
authors: Pradip Kattel
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a method for constructing time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on a finite spatial interval from the scattering and reflection data of an autonomous integrable model. Each particle carries a spectral label that is constant along its free trajectory. Requiring a right--left scattering event at a fixed time to be independent of its position forces the map from characteristic coordinates to spectral labels to be affine, with the same slope for both chiralities. As a result, all bulk scattering events at a given time sample one common spectral argument, and the two boundary reflections sample the corresponding endpoint arguments. The bulk and boundary drives are not independent time-dependent deformations: their time dependence is fixed by the same affine spectral coordinate. Successive reflections at the two endpoints translate the spectral label by a finite amount. Following a particle through a complete round trip then produces a difference transport whose consistency gives the boundary quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equations. The Yang--Baxter and reflection equations ensure local compatibility, while BqKZ flatness ensures compatibility of complete round trips. We then reconstruct the local Hamiltonian by inverting the one- and two-particle matching problems. The bulk matrix fixes the contact interaction, while the reflection matrix fixes the corresponding boundary coupling. The same autonomous factorized data determine the boundary qKZ transport problem and the local driven Hamiltonian. Once the boundary qKZ system is solved, its characteristic pullback gives the corresponding time-dependent many-body wavefunction. We illustrate the construction with rational [MATH] models and an [MATH]-invariant model with dynamical boundary impurities, obtaining driven Kondo interactions whose couplings are fixed by the same affine spectral coordinate.
tldr: Constructs time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on a finite interval with dynamical boundaries from the scattering and reflection data of an autonomous integrable model.
motivation: To understand how time-dependent bulk and boundary drives in integrable quantum field theories are constrained by the consistency of scattering and reflection events.
method: Uses an affine spectral coordinate mapping, Yang-Baxter and reflection equations for local compatibility, boundary quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov flatness for round-trip consistency, and inverse matching to reconstruct the local Hamiltonian and many-body wavefunction.
result: The bulk and boundary time dependence is fixed by the same affine spectral coordinate, yielding boundary qKZ equations and driven Kondo interactions for rational and SU(N)-invariant models with dynamical boundary impurities.
conclusion: Provides a systematic framework for constructing driven integrable models with dynamical boundaries from autonomous factorized scattering data.

title: Transport, Hall Effect, And Collective Dynamics Of Driven Particles In Active Chiral Media
authors: C. J. O. Reichhardt C. Reichhardt
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the dc driven transport of particles with Yukawa interactions through an assembly of chiral active particles undergoing circular motion. The driven particles exhibit a jammed phase, a nonlinear disordered or plastic regime where there is a finite Hall effect produced by interactions with the active chiral particles, and a high drive linear regime where the driven and nondriven particles phase separate and the Hall effect nearly disappears. The chiral particles experience strong drag and Hall effects from the driven particles, and these effects vary monotonically with changing thermal fluctuations or chiral motion parameters. The different dynamical phases are correlated with features in the longitudinal and transverse transport curves, and we map out the phases as a function of active orbit size, thermal fluctuations, and particle density.
tldr: This paper studies dc-driven transport of Yukawa particles through chiral active particles, identifying jammed, plastic Hall-effect, and phase-separated regimes.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how driven particles interact with an active chiral medium and how this produces emergent Hall and drag effects.
method: They use numerical simulations of particles with Yukawa interactions moving through a bath of chiral active particles undergoing circular motion, mapping phases as functions of orbit size, temperature, and density.
result: They find a jammed phase, a nonlinear plastic regime with finite Hall effect, and a high-drive linear regime where phase separation occurs and the Hall effect nearly vanishes.
conclusion: The chiral medium experiences strong drag and Hall responses from the driven particles, and the dynamical phases correlate with longitudinal and transverse transport features.

title: Joint Forecasting Of Extreme Events Through Dual-Stage Cascade Reservoir Computing
authors: Yueyang Wang, Juncheng Huang. Hanxu Zhou, Tao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) offers an efficient data-driven approach for forecasting extreme events (EEs), which correspond to rare and large-amplitude dynamical occurrences. We propose a dual-stage cascade framework that jointly predicts both the timing and peak intensity of upcoming EEs. A traditional RC branch integrates long-term precursor dynamics to support stable detection and long-horizon prediction, while an NGRC branch captures local nonlinear waveform geometry to improve fine-grained time-to-peak localization and complement peak-intensity estimation. The fused features then feed a ridge classifier that issues a binary alarm upon detecting precursors. Only then do two ridge regressors, trained on true-positive snapshots, estimate time-to-peak and peak intensity. This classify-then-regress design addresses severe class imbalance without data resampling. Evaluated on simulated pump-modulated VCSEL data, the hybrid model achieves a SEDI value >0.8, with MAEs around 0.2 ns and 0.2 a. u., maintaining performance up to a 20 ns warning horizon. The framework advances extreme-event forecasting from binary warnings to fully quantitative dual-objective prediction.
tldr: A dual-stage cascade reservoir computing framework jointly forecasts the timing and peak intensity of extreme events in pump-modulated VCSEL data.
motivation: Extreme events are rare, large-amplitude dynamical occurrences that are difficult to predict, and existing reservoir computing approaches typically provide only binary warnings rather than quantitative dual-objective forecasts.
method: The framework combines a traditional reservoir computing branch for long-term precursor detection with an NGRC branch for local waveform geometry, then uses a ridge classifier to issue alarms and ridge regressors to estimate time-to-peak and peak intensity.
result: On simulated pump-modulated VCSEL data, the hybrid model achieves SEDI > 0.8 with mean absolute errors around 0.2 ns and 0.2 a.u., maintaining performance up to a 20 ns warning horizon.
conclusion: The classify-then-regress cascade advances extreme-event forecasting from binary warnings to fully quantitative dual-objective prediction while addressing class imbalance without resampling.

title: Efficient Demodulation For Coset Codes On Lattices
authors: Chloe Makdad, Leopold Bertholet, Mairead Cummins, Stephen Mackes, Matthew Robinson
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lattice constellations can provide significant coding and shaping gains over traditional quadrature amplitude modulations (QAMs), but have not been widely adopted due to the high implementation complexity of modulation, demodulation, and decoding. Voronoi constellations (VCs) enable an efficient modulation map that achieves shaping gain using the Voronoi cell of a lattice. Multilevel coset codes (MLCCs) are a recently proposed coded modulation scheme for VCs that realizes more efficient decoding. However, MLCCs still suffer from a soft demodulation complexity of [MATH] for a [MATH]-dimensional lattice with spectral efficiency [MATH] bits per real dimension. In this paper, we propose fast quantize-walk demodulation (FQWD), an efficient demodulation scheme for MLCCs that reduces the complexity to [MATH]. Our strategy utilizes novel radial projections onto the Voronoi cells of the [MATH] and [MATH] lattices. Experimental results demonstrate that FQWD has only negligible loss in block error rate (BLER) relative to maximum likelihood demodulation under the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel. Using FQWD, we simulate MLCCs on higher-dimensional lattices with [MATH] bits per dimension under AGWN for the first time, achieving BLER gains over multilevel polar codes on QAMs of up to 0.6 dB for the [MATH] lattice and 1.2 dB for [MATH].
tldr: Proposes fast quantize-walk demodulation (FQWD) for multilevel coset codes on lattices, reducing demodulation complexity with negligible block error rate loss.
motivation: Lattice constellations offer coding and shaping gains over QAM but suffer from high implementation complexity, and existing multilevel coset codes still have high soft demodulation complexity.
method: FQWD uses novel radial projections onto Voronoi cells of the E8 and Leech lattices to efficiently demodulate multilevel coset codes.
result: FQWD achieves negligible BLER loss relative to maximum likelihood demodulation under AWGN and enables simulations of higher-dimensional lattices, yielding up to 0.6 dB gain for the E8 lattice and 1.2 dB for the Leech lattice over multilevel polar codes on QAM.
conclusion: FQWD makes practical multilevel coset codes on high-dimensional lattices feasible, providing significant performance gains over conventional QAM schemes.

title: On The Involution Preserving Properties Of Semi-discrete Active Flux Methods On Simplex
authors: Remi Abgrall, Yongle Liu, Mario Ricchiuto
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the involution-preserving properties of the Active Flux method on unstructured triangular meshes. Two model problems are considered: the two-dimensional linear acoustic system, which satisfies a curl involution on the velocity field, and the two-dimensional Maxwell equations with an in-plane magnetic field, which satisfy a divergence involution. Both systems can be written in conservative form. The question we address is how a single discretization can satisfy the conservative form and the involution at the same time. Within a discrete Active Flux framework on simplices, we derive explicit formulas for a discrete curl operator that is exactly preserved by the scheme for acoustics, and for a discrete divergence operator preserved for the Maxwell system. The analysis applies to general simplex meshes and to any polynomial degree, including extensions of the method beyond third order. Numerical experiments with the third-order scheme confirm the theoretical results. Highlights: 1-Active Flux on unstructured triangular meshes preserves discrete involutions, 2-Explicit discrete curl operator preserved by the scheme for linear acoustics, 3- Explicit discrete divergence operator preserved for 2D Maxwell equations, 4- Results hold on general simplex meshes,% and for any polynomial degree 5- Third-order numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
tldr: The paper develops discrete curl and divergence operators for the Active Flux method on unstructured triangular meshes that exactly preserve the involutions of the linear acoustic system and the 2D Maxwell equations.
motivation: Numerical schemes for systems with involutions (like curl-free velocity fields in acoustics or divergence-free magnetic fields in Maxwell) must satisfy both the conservative form and the involution constraint simultaneously, which is challenging on unstructured meshes.
method: Within a discrete Active Flux framework on simplices, the authors derive explicit formulas for a discrete curl operator for acoustics and a discrete divergence operator for Maxwell, valid on general simplex meshes and for general polynomial degree.
result: The derived operators are exactly preserved by the scheme, and third-order numerical experiments on triangular meshes confirm the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Active Flux methods can be constructed to simultaneously satisfy conservative form and discrete involution preservation on unstructured simplices, extending the method beyond third order.

title: Conditioning And Singular Value Distribution Of Jacobi Weighted Histopolation Matrices
authors: Allal Guessab, Federico Nudo, Stefano Serra-Capizzano
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first study the singular value distribution of the unscaled matrices arising from Jacobi weighted histopolation. For the Jacobi weight with parameters [MATH], and using the Jacobi basis with parameters [MATH], we previously proved that, for [MATH] and quasi-uniform meshes, the growth of these matrices in the sense of singular value distribution is slower than any positive power of the logarithm of the matrix size. However, the numerical behavior of the unscaled matrices suggested a nontrivial singular value symbol, which we identify explicitly in this paper. Starting from the standard asymptotic formula for Jacobi polynomials, we derive an asymptotic representation of the weighted cell averages defining the entries of the histopolation matrices. This representation allows us to analyze the associated Gram sequence by means of GLT theory. We identify its GLT symbol and, consequently, we obtain the singular value distribution of the histopolation matrices for any [MATH]. We also characterize the set [MATH] where the resulting symbol vanishes and compute its measure, showing that this set depends only on the mesh, while the Jacobi parameters affect the values of the symbol on its support. When this measure is positive, the singular value distribution implies the discrete asymptotic ill-posedness of the problem, while a comparison with the Toeplitz setting suggests exponential growth of the spectral condition number. When the measure of [MATH] is zero, the problem is well-posed and the observed conditioning is algebraic in the matrix size. Finally, numerical experiments supporting the theoretical findings are reported and discussed, while conclusions are given in the final section of the current work together with a few open problems.
tldr: The paper analyzes the singular value distribution and conditioning of Jacobi weighted histopolation matrices using GLT (generalized locally Toeplitz) theory.
motivation: Previous work showed that unscaled Jacobi weighted histopolation matrices grow slower than any positive power of the logarithm of matrix size, but numerical behavior hinted at a nontrivial singular value symbol that had not been identified.
method: Starting from the standard asymptotic formula for Jacobi polynomials, the authors derive an asymptotic representation of the weighted cell averages defining the matrix entries, then analyze the associated Gram sequence via GLT theory to identify its symbol.
result: They explicitly identify the GLT symbol governing the singular value distribution for any Jacobi parameter, characterize the vanishing set of the symbol, compute its measure (depending only on the mesh), and relate positive measure to discrete asymptotic ill-posedness and exponential growth of the spectral condition number.
conclusion: The work fully characterizes the conditioning of Jacobi weighted histopolation matrices, with numerical experiments supporting the theory, and outlines several open problems.

title: Localize-and-Detect: Auditing Task-Level Poisoning In Instruction-Tuned Models
authors: Luze Sun, Cristina Nita-Rotaru, Alina Oprea
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Instruction fine-tuning adapts a pretrained language model to follow instructions by training it on instruction--response pairs from a collection of tasks, such as summarization and question answering. Task-level poisoning exploits this task structure to manipulate the fine-tuned model into producing attacker-specified biased content on a particular target task, without requiring an explicit input trigger. Detecting such attacks is challenging because there is no explicit trigger to identify, the target task and biased content are unknown, and benign fine-tuning itself changes model behavior. We introduce Localize-and-Detect, a two-stage black-box auditing method for task-level poisoning that requires only outputs from both the base and fine-tuned models. In the first stage, we localize the target task by identifying candidate tasks on which the fine-tuned and base models have the largest differences in their next-token distributions. In the second stage, we search the shortlisted tasks for biased content that repeatedly appears in the fine-tuned model's responses but not in those of the base model. We evaluate Localize-and-Detect on 216 poisoned models across two model families, varying the target task, poisoning mode, poison budget, and type of biased content. Our evaluation demonstrates that Localize-and-Detect can effectively localize target tasks and detect biased content across a range of poisoning settings and models, with detection that tracks attack success and few false positives on clean models.
tldr: Localize-and-Detect is a two-stage black-box auditing method that localizes the target task of a task-level poisoning attack on instruction-tuned language models and then detects the attacker-injected biased content using only base and fine-tuned model outputs.
motivation: Instruction fine-tuning on instruction–response pairs creates a task structure that adversaries can exploit to implant task-specific biases without any explicit trigger, and such poisoning is hard to detect because the target task, the biased content, and benign behavioral drift are all unknown a priori.
method: The approach first localizes the poisoned target task by comparing next-token distributions between the base and fine-tuned models, then searches the shortlisted tasks for biased content that recurs in the fine-tuned model's responses but not in the base model's, all in a black-box setting.
result: Evaluated on 216 poisoned models spanning two model families and varying target task, poisoning mode, poison budget, and bias type, the method effectively localizes target tasks and detects biased content with detection rates tracking attack success and few false positives on clean models.
conclusion: Output-only auditing can reliably expose task-level poisoning in instruction-tuned models, offering a practical defense tool for model supply-chain security and fine-tuning integrity.

title: Scrm: An Actionable Framework For Space Cyber Risk Management
authors: Ekzhin Ear, Caleb Chang, Shouhuai Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Space infrastructures play critical roles in modern society, including satellite communications (SATCOM). Like the Internet, space infrastructures are vulnerable to cyber attacks, or space cyber attacks, highlighting the importance of managing cyber risks to space infrastructures, or space cyber risks. However, adequately managing space cyber risks is an open problem. In this paper, we propose the first Space Cyber Risk Management (SCRM) framework to systematically analyze and mitigate space cyber risks. The framework models space infrastructures, space missions, and space cyber attacks, while offering algorithms for space mission risk analysis and hardening. We demonstrate its usefulness by conducting a case study on real-world space cyber attacks against the SATCOM infrastructure implemented in our testbed. Our results show, among other things, that: (i) dealing with space cyber attack cascading effects is essential to space cyber risk management; (ii) the framework can effectively harden space missions; (iii) National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) security controls can effectively mitigate space cyber risks.
tldr: The paper proposes SCRM, a framework for systematically analyzing and mitigating cyber risks in space infrastructures, with a case study on real-world SATCOM attacks.
motivation: Space infrastructures such as satellite communications are critical but vulnerable to cyber attacks, and adequate risk management for them remains an open problem.
method: The authors develop a Space Cyber Risk Management framework that models space infrastructures, missions, and attacks, and provides algorithms for mission risk analysis and hardening, tested in a SATCOM testbed.
result: The case study shows that cascading effects are essential to manage, the framework can effectively harden space missions, and NIST security controls can mitigate space cyber risks.
conclusion: SCRM offers an actionable approach to space cyber risk management, though it falls outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems research directions.

title: Language Model Fingerprinting Requires Rethinking Watermark Teachers
authors: Jeongyeon Hwang, Anshul Nasery, Sewoong Oh, Jungseul Ok
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM fingerprinting via watermark distillation embeds a statistical watermark signal into model weights, enabling model owners to identify their models behind black-box APIs. Revisiting a recent protocol, we find that its utility evaluation understates text quality degradation in open-ended generation, favoring overly strong watermark teachers. Weakening the watermark improves text quality but sacrifices detectability. To move beyond this trade-off, we rethink whether text watermarks designed for verifying generated text are suitable distillation teachers for model fingerprinting. Such watermarks are typically designed to remain detectable from an individual output, limiting how sparse the watermark signal can be. In contrast, fingerprint verification can aggregate signal across queries, making sparser watermark signals viable. This raises a key question: where should the sparse signal be placed? We analyze signal placement through token surprisal and show that, even at comparable watermark strength, different placements can target tokens with different plausibility under the base model. This motivates near-tie restriction, which uses top-1-relative logit gaps to restrict the watermark bias to tokens close to the base model's top prediction. Across multiple models, near-tie improves detection--quality frontiers under deployment changes, preserves higher text quality across query budgets, and further improves existing watermarking schemes when combined with them.
tldr: The paper rethinks watermark distillation for LLM fingerprinting, arguing that text watermarks designed for per-output detection are poor distillation teachers, and proposes a 'near-tie restriction' that places sparse watermark signals on tokens close to the base model's top prediction.
motivation: Existing LLM fingerprinting protocols using watermark distillation overstate text quality degradation in open-ended generation, favoring overly strong watermark teachers, while weakening the watermark sacrifices detectability.
method: The authors analyze signal placement via token surprisal and introduce near-tie restriction, which uses top-1-relative logit gaps to confine the watermark bias to near-tie tokens, and evaluate detection-quality frontiers across multiple models and deployment shifts.
result: Near-tie restriction improves detection–quality frontiers under deployment changes, preserves higher text quality across query budgets, and enhances existing watermarking schemes when combined with them.
conclusion: Designing distillation teachers specifically for fingerprint verification—exploiting aggregation across queries to allow sparser signals—is more effective than reusing conventional text watermarks.

title: Symbolic Search Is Not Exhausted: Persistent Proof-Space Exploration In Lean4
authors: Ruoran Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formal theorem proving increasingly combines learned semantic guidance with verified symbolic execution. The quality of the symbolic search substrate therefore determines how much useful mathematical structure can be accumulated, reused, and exposed under a finite inference budget. We introduce ViaLean, a Lean4 prover that organizes symbolic reasoning as bounded exploration of a persistent proof-state graph. Its search preserves coverage across complementary reasoning modes, merges semantically equivalent goals, retains verified intermediate structure, and observes short symbolic futures before committing to a transition. On the complete miniF2F test split, the model-free configuration solves 122/244 problems (50.0% pass@1). Historical and recent symbolic reference points range from Lean's earlier tidy search to modern grind and SMT-backed verification, showing that proof-space organization remains a substantial source of capability. The same persistent state also provides a natural interface for neural--symbolic agents: neural reasoning can operate over verified regions and intermediate objects while Lean continuously expands and validates the local proof space.
tldr: ViaLean is a Lean4 theorem prover that organizes symbolic search as bounded exploration of a persistent proof-state graph, achieving 50.0% pass@1 on miniF2F without learned models.
motivation: Formal theorem proving increasingly combines neural guidance with symbolic execution, so improving the symbolic search substrate is important for efficiently accumulating and reusing mathematical structure under limited inference budgets.
method: The prover maintains a persistent proof-state graph, preserving coverage across reasoning modes, merging semantically equivalent goals, retaining verified intermediate structure, and observing short symbolic futures before committing to transitions.
result: The model-free ViaLean configuration solves 122/244 miniF2F problems (50.0% pass@1), outperforming or comparing favorably with earlier tidy search and modern grind/SMT-backed verification.
conclusion: Proof-space organization remains a substantial source of capability, and the persistent state also provides a natural interface for neural-symbolic agents to reason over verified regions while Lean validates local proofs.

title: CyTReX: Explainable AI-Based Cybersecurity Threat Reasoning Framework For Der Networks
authors: Damilola Popoola, Souradeep Bhattacharya, Manimaran Govindarasu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) environments rely on network communication protocols to coordinate control commands, measurements, and device states across edge assets and cloud systems. Edge anomaly detection systems (ADS) monitor this traffic to identify deviations from normal communication behavior, flagging suspicious flows for further investigation. When the ADS flags abnormal network traffic, a single attack label is often insufficient for operational response: the label reports the detector's selected class but does not expose alternative threat interpretations that may warrant investigation. This paper presents Cybersecurity Threat Reasoning with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (CyTReX), an evidence-grounded threat reasoning framework for DER security that transforms network-level anomaly alerts into ranked, analyst-facing threat hypotheses designed to support Security Operations Center (SOC) triage and investigation. CyTReX constrains large language model (LLM) reasoning through a structured evidence packet, defined as a consolidated record of detection outputs, model explanations, and cyber threat intelligence (CTI) context. The evidence packet integrates edge-layer anomaly detection evidence, cloud reasoning layer attack interpretation, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) network-feature attributions, surrogate decision rules, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-enabled CTI enrichment. This ensures that every ranked hypothesis and attack-tree branch is traceable to explicit evidence rather than free-form LLM inference, and that incomplete or conflicting evidence is communicated rather than suppressed. Evaluation across five configurations shows that additional reasoning components improve hypothesis specificity, evidence traceability, and analytical grounding, with the complete pipeline providing the richest evidence-grounded reasoning context.
tldr: CyTReX is an explainable AI framework that converts network anomaly alerts in distributed energy resource environments into ranked, evidence-grounded cybersecurity threat hypotheses for SOC triage.
motivation: Single-label anomaly alerts in DER networks lack the alternative threat interpretations and traceable evidence needed for effective security operations triage and investigation.
method: The framework constrains LLM reasoning with a structured evidence packet combining edge anomaly detection outputs, SHAP feature attributions, surrogate decision rules, and MCP-enabled cyber threat intelligence enrichment.
result: Evaluation across five configurations shows that adding reasoning components improves hypothesis specificity, evidence traceability, and analytical grounding, with the complete pipeline yielding the richest evidence-grounded reasoning context.
conclusion: Evidence-grounded LLM reasoning can enhance DER cybersecurity triage by producing traceable, ranked threat hypotheses rather than opaque single-label alerts.

title: Guess My Weight: Profiled Side-Channel Recovery Of Floating-Point Neural-Network Weights
authors: Timon Lum\'ir Fillo, J\'an Mikulec, Anubhab Baksi, Jakub Breier, Xiaolu Hou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural-network parameters deployed on embedded devices may be exposed through physical side-channel leakage during inference. Existing side-channel attacks on floating-point neural-network parameters have often targeted reduced numerical precision, while recovering the complete IEEE-754 representation remains considerably more challenging because of the large and structured 32-bit candidate space. We present a profiled template attack for bit-exact recovery of an IEEE-754 single-precision neural-network weight from power measurements. The attack targets the floating-point multiplication between a known input and a first-layer weight. During profiling, multivariate Gaussian templates are learned from randomized network configurations using Hamming-weight classes of the multiplication result, while the remaining network parameters act as nuisance variables. To efficiently search the structured 32-bit floating-point candidate space, we use a hierarchical coarse-to-fine-to-exact procedure that progressively increases both the numerical and leakage-model resolution. Experiments on a ChipWhisperer-Lite with an Arm Cortex-M4 demonstrate recovery of the exact float32 representation of the target weight. In the evaluated setting, the attack reaches a bit-exact success rate of 99% with 171 traces and 100% from 263 traces onward. These results demonstrate that profiling can enable practical full-precision extraction of floating-point neural-network parameters from physical leakage.
tldr: Profiled side-channel attack recovers exact IEEE-754 single-precision neural-network weights from power measurements on an Arm Cortex-M4.
motivation: Floating-point neural-network parameters deployed on embedded devices may leak through physical side channels, but recovering the full IEEE-754 representation is difficult due to the structured 32-bit candidate space.
method: The attack uses multivariate Gaussian templates learned from randomized configurations with Hamming-weight classes, and a hierarchical coarse-to-fine-to-exact search over the 32-bit float candidate space.
result: On a ChipWhisperer-Lite with an Arm Cortex-M4, bit-exact recovery of a float32 weight achieved 99% success with 171 traces and 100% from 263 traces onward.
conclusion: Profiling side-channel analysis can practically extract full-precision floating-point neural-network parameters from physical leakage, with no quantum information or thermodynamics relevance.

title: Timely Persuasion With Opposing Senders: When Does Competition Help The Receiver?
authors: Melih Bastopcu Ahmet Bugra Gundogan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Status updates let a receiver track a changing process, but a sender that controls when they are sent can steer the receiver's estimate without misreporting. We study competition between two such senders with opposing preferences, who report on a binary continuous-time Markov chain using state-dependent Poisson rates under individual budgets. The receiver follows the reports through a zero-order-hold estimator only if this yields at least the long-run weighted correct-estimation utility of a prior-based default estimate. We model the interaction as a Stackelberg game in which the sender favored by this default leads, the opposing sender follows, and the receiver then selects its estimator. We characterize the pure-strategy equilibria in closed form. When the follower can obtain positive utility against a silent leader, limited state-[MATH] reporting by the leader merely frees part of the follower's budget for state-[MATH] reports, so every optimal leader policy is either silence or full-budget state-[MATH] reporting, depending on explicit budget thresholds. A single sender with the same total budget leaves the receiver at its default utility, whereas the full-budget intervention outcome makes the receiver's participation constraint slack and strictly improves its utility. At the intervention threshold, silence and full-budget intervention yield identical sender payoffs but different receiver utilities. Numerical results illustrate these regimes and compare equilibrium performance with a receiver-optimal reporting benchmark.
tldr: The paper studies competition between two opposing senders who control status update timing to influence a receiver's estimate of a binary Markov chain.
motivation: Status updates can be strategically timed to steer a receiver's estimate without explicit misreporting, so the authors examine whether competition between senders with opposing preferences benefits the receiver.
method: The interaction is modeled as a Stackelberg game where a leading sender, a following sender, and a receiver with a zero-order-hold estimator interact; pure-strategy equilibria are characterized in closed form.
result: Optimal leader policies are either silence or full-budget reporting depending on budget thresholds; competition can make the receiver's participation constraint slack and strictly improve utility, with silence and intervention yielding identical sender payoffs at a threshold.
conclusion: Competition between opposing senders can improve receiver utility under specific budget conditions, offering insights into strategic information provision in status update systems.

title: Attestable Audit: Property-Based Attestation For Proprietary Workloads Without Artifact Disclosure
authors: Takuma Imamura
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) prove the integrity of code and data to a remote peer through remote attestation: the TEE issues an attestation report by signing, with a hardware-bound key, its configuration information, including measurements (cryptographic digests) of the code loaded inside it. A verifier appraises the report by matching these measurements against reference values. When the measured artifact is proprietary, however, the verifier cannot derive the reference values itself: it can only confirm that something with a given measurement is running inside the TEE---not that the program behaves as expected---forcing full trust in the reference value provider. We propose an architecture that closes this gap without disclosing the artifact, composing two TEE workloads: attestable build (Hugenroth et al., 2025), which binds a source code digest to a build artifact measurement, and attestable audit (proposed in this paper), which binds the same source code digest to the verdicts of automated audits---fuzzing, static analysis, AI code auditing, formal methods---executed inside a TEE. Both are instances of Confidential Computing Proofs: TEE attestation viewed as a hardware-backed zero-knowledge proof. Chaining the two certificates lets the verifier conclude that the running artifact was built from source code satisfying the audited properties, without disclosing either the source code or the build artifact. A proof-of-concept implementation on Intel SGX with the Gramine Library OS, running the Bandit security analyzer on Python code, demonstrates the practicality of the approach.
tldr: The paper proposes a TEE-based architecture for property-based attestation of proprietary workloads without disclosing source code or build artifacts.
motivation: Remote attestation traditionally requires verifiers to know reference measurements, which is impossible for proprietary artifacts, forcing trust in the reference provider.
method: The architecture composes attestable build and attestable audit, both viewed as Confidential Computing Proofs, and binds source code digests to audit verdicts executed inside a TEE, demonstrated with Intel SGX and Gramine running Bandit.
result: A proof-of-concept implementation shows that a verifier can conclude an artifact was built from audited source code satisfying specified properties without seeing the source or artifact.
conclusion: The work closes a trust gap in TEE attestation for proprietary software, but it is a classical security/confidential computing contribution unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On Hyperfine Structure Of The Rotationally Excited $1 S_{\mu} N\ell_{e}$-states In Helium Muonic Atoms
authors: Alexei M. Frolov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The new approach is develop to determine the hyperfine structure of the rotationally excited [MATH]-states in the three-body helium muonic [MATH]He [MATH] and [MATH]He [MATH] atoms. The formulas derived in this study allow one to evaluate the hyperfine structure splittings for an arbitrary rotationally excited (bound) [MATH]-state in the three-body helium muonic atoms. Similar formulas have never been produced in earlier studies and this explains why these hyperfine structure splittings are still unknown for these bound states.
tldr: Develops formulas for the hyperfine structure of rotationally excited 1S_mu Nl_e states in three-body helium muonic atoms.
motivation: Hyperfine structure splittings for rotationally excited bound states in helium muonic atoms were previously unknown and no general formulas existed.
method: A new analytical approach is developed to derive general expressions for hyperfine structure splittings for arbitrary rotationally excited states in three-body helium muonic atoms.
result: The derived formulas allow evaluation of hyperfine splittings for any rotationally excited bound state in 3He_mu and 4He_mu atoms.
conclusion: The work provides the first such formulas, filling a gap in the spectroscopy of muonic helium atoms.

title: Pointwise Convergence Of Random Ergodic Averages At The \(l^1\) Endpoint
authors: Will Burstein, Lorenzo Catani, Ben Krause
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In his highly influential paper, , Bourgain introduced the study of pointwise convergence of ergodic averages along randomly generated subsets of the integers, developing a robust \(L^p\)-theory for \(p>1\). More recently, this theory was partially complemented at the \(L^1\) endpoint by work of LaVictoire, who treated averages along random sequences that are ``slightly denser" than the set of squares, for which universal \(L^1\) pointwise convergence is known to fail. In this work, we prove that, almost surely, for every measure-preserving system and every integrable function, the ergodic averages formed by sampling along random sequences with quadratic growth converge almost everywhere. Our proof combines harmonic-analytic methods developed by M.~Christ with a ``random sampling" of quadratic forms, thereby overcoming the main uniformity obstruction.
tldr: The paper proves almost-sure pointwise convergence of ergodic averages along randomly sampled sequences with quadratic growth at the L1 endpoint.
motivation: Bourgain's random ergodic averages theory covered Lp for p>1, and later work partially addressed the L1 endpoint for slightly denser random sequences, leaving open the quadratic-growth case.
method: The proof combines harmonic-analytic methods of M. Christ with random sampling of quadratic forms to overcome the main uniformity obstruction.
result: For almost every random sequence with quadratic growth, the ergodic averages converge almost everywhere for every measure-preserving system and every integrable function.
conclusion: This establishes pointwise convergence at the L1 endpoint for random quadratic-growth sequences, extending the known theory beyond the density regime where universal L1 convergence fails.

title: Time-reliability Optimization Of Multi-pass Underfill Dispensing Sequences On Printed Circuit Boards: A Schedule-dependent Reliability Model Solved By A Multiset-permutation Binary-addition-tree Algorithm
authors: Wei-Chang Yeh
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-pass underfill dispensing couples cycle time with process reliability because the sequence determines the inter-pass flow times. This paper formulates a tri-objective multiset-permutation routing model that minimises nominal cycle time and additive duration variance while maximising reliability under hard- and soft-dwell policies; reliability combines pass, schedule-dependent flow and travel terms. Under independent durations and deterministic dwell thresholds, the variance measure equals the cycle-time variance under soft dwell and bounds it from above under hard dwell. A multiset-permutation binary-addition-tree algorithm enumerates the feasible routes without duplication and prunes prefixes by dominance. Six instances, including three BeagleBone Black benchmarks, yield reference Pareto fronts, the largest search space of [MATH] routes in 38 minutes on 20 CPU cores. Among simulated candidates, the nominally cost-selected routes incur maximum estimated excess costs of USD 0.0014 per board at the modelled duration variability and USD 0.0035 with it doubled. Round-robin dispatch is within 3.7 % of the reference optimum at the tested costs; NSGA-II and simplified swarm optimisation show at most 0.53 % observed cost regret while recovering about 30 % of the largest hard-dwell front. The framework quantifies sequencing trade-offs and heuristic decision regret; physical reliability prediction requires inspection-based calibration.
tldr: The paper proposes a tri-objective scheduling model for multi-pass underfill dispensing on printed circuit boards, optimizing cycle time, duration variance, and reliability via a multiset-permutation binary-addition-tree algorithm.
motivation: Multi-pass underfill dispensing couples cycle time with process reliability because inter-pass flow times depend on the sequence, so selecting an optimal route is important for manufacturing cost and reliability.
method: The authors formulate a multiset-permutation routing model that minimizes nominal cycle time and additive duration variance while maximizing reliability under hard- and soft-dwell policies; they solve it with a multiset-permutation binary-addition-tree algorithm that enumerates feasible routes without duplication and prunes prefixes by dominance.
result: Six instances, including three BeagleBone Black benchmarks, yield reference Pareto fronts, with the largest search space solved in 38 minutes on 20 CPU cores; simulated candidates show maximum estimated excess costs of USD 0.0014 per board at modelled variability and USD 0.0035 when doubled, while round-robin dispatch is within 3.7% of the reference optimum and NSGA-II/Swarm show at most 0.53% observed cost regret.
conclusion: The framework quantifies sequencing trade-offs and heuristic decision regret, though physical reliability prediction requires inspection-based calibration.

title: Solving VeriContest With A Lean-Backed Rust Verifier
authors: Traian Serbanuta, Jun Xu, Andrei Stefanescu, Cosmin Radoi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: VeriContest is a benchmark of 1007 competitive-programming problems in Rust, each with a Verus specification, a judge-accepted solution, and a Verus proof. Its authors report that proof generation is the bottleneck for frontier models: given the specification and the code, the best model produces an accepted Verus proof for 13.95% of the problems on the first attempt. We report on solving the same proof-generation task with Rust-Prover, a verifier for Rust backed by Lean 4. The Verus specification and the Rust code are restated and translated into Lean, each specification becomes a theorem, and agents prove the theorems with Lean's kernel as the final check. All 1325 theorems of all 1007 problems were proved. 1259 of them were proved in one run of under 32 hours on Claude Opus 5.5, at a median of 3.2 minutes and $1.17 per proof, and 70% of them on the first iteration. The restated specifications were checked against the benchmark's test suites, and reviewed where no suite applies. None was wrong or weakened. The translated Lean programs were run on 21,413 of the benchmark's test cases and produced the same output as the Rust programs on every one. Across four Claude and four GPT models at five reasoning-effort settings, every current frontier model proves nearly all of a ten-theorem sample at every setting, and more effort raises the cost without raising the number of proofs. The cheapest Claude setting, Sonnet 5.5 at low effort, proves all of the 50 hardest theorems. We also rerun the benchmark's own Verus protocol with Claude Opus 5.5 on the 50 problems with the longest reference proofs. Opus 5.5 alone fails to prove one of them.
tldr: A Lean 4-backed Rust verifier (Rust-Prover) plus LLM agents solves all 1325 proof obligations of the VeriContest benchmark, far outperforming Verus-based proof generation.
motivation: Proof generation, not code generation, is the bottleneck for frontier models on verified-programming benchmarks such as VeriContest (13.95% first-attempt success reported), motivating a different verification backend and agent workflow.
method: Verus specifications and Rust programs are restated and translated into Lean 4, each specification becomes a theorem, and LLM agents (Claude/GPT families at varying reasoning effort) attempt proofs with the Lean kernel as final checker; translations are cross-validated against the benchmark's test suites.
result: All 1325 theorems across 1007 problems were proved, 1259 in a single <32-hour run at median 3.2 minutes and $1.17 per proof with 70% first-iteration success; translated Lean programs matched Rust outputs on all 21,413 test cases, and the cheapest Claude setting proved the 50 hardest theorems.
conclusion: Lean-backed verification combined with agentic proof search substantially surpasses the benchmark's native Verus protocol, suggesting the verification toolchain, not model capability, is the dominant limiting factor.

title: Two Generalizations Of Shininess
authors: Yoni Zohar Guilherme V. Toledo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shininess is one of the main theory combination methods in Satisfiability Modulo Theories. We present two infinite families of generalizations of it: one involving a property between gentleness and shininess, which helps us see gentleness itself as a variation of shininess; and another having no further computability requirements on the weaker theory, in addition dropping the need for smoothness. We prove these methods sharp, and compare them with existing methods.
tldr: The paper presents two infinite families of generalizations of the shininess method for theory combination in Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT).
motivation: Shininess is a main theory combination method in SMT, and the authors aim to generalize it to relax computability and smoothness requirements.
method: The authors define two infinite families of generalizations: one between gentleness and shininess, and another with no further computability requirements on the weaker theory and without smoothness, then prove these methods sharp and compare them with existing methods.
result: The generalizations are proven sharp and compared with existing theory combination methods, showing that gentleness can be seen as a variation of shininess.
conclusion: The work broadens the landscape of theory combination in SMT but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multiple Access In Pinching-Antenna Systems: A Survey, Impairment Analysis, And Evaluation
authors: Hans Dieter Schotten Wei Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching-antenna systems attach dielectric pinches to a waveguide, creating line-of-sight radiation points within a few meters of any user. The pinches on one waveguide, however, radiate the same signal, unlike a conventional array, where each element transmits a dedicated signal. Separating the signals of multiple users therefore becomes challenging and requires a new perspective on multiple access. Most existing studies rest on an idealized model, and no survey examines the access schemes under realistic impairments. This article surveys multiple access in pinching-antenna systems and organizes fifty-six works into a unified taxonomy by spatial degrees of freedom. The users of one waveguide can be separated only in time, frequency, power, or guided mode, while multiple waveguides add the space domain. The article then identifies the impairments critical to this separation, which perturb the effective channel, leak interference across orthogonal resources, or couple the pinches on the uplink, and summarizes them in an impairment-versus-method map. A unified evaluation of time-, frequency-, power-, and space-domain access under identical channel and impairment models reveals that the degradation is method specific. The analytical and numerical results give insight into multiple access in these systems and provide a basis for its impairment-aware design, a necessary step toward their adoption in practical networks.
tldr: A survey and unified impairment-aware evaluation of multiple-access schemes in pinching-antenna systems, where dielectric pinches on a waveguide radiate the same signal and users must be separated in time, frequency, power, guided mode, or space.
motivation: Pinching-antenna systems offer line-of-sight radiation near users but, unlike conventional arrays, all pinches on one waveguide share the same signal, making multi-user separation difficult; existing studies rely on idealized models and no survey covers realistic impairments.
method: The authors organize fifty-six prior works into a taxonomy based on spatial degrees of freedom, identify channel-perturbing, interference-leaking, and pinch-coupling impairments, map impairments against methods, and perform a unified analytical and numerical evaluation of time-, frequency-, power-, and space-domain access under identical channel and impairment models.
result: Performance degradation is found to be method specific, with impairments affecting different multiple-access schemes in distinct ways as revealed by the comparative evaluation.
conclusion: The findings clarify multiple access in pinching-antenna systems and provide a basis for impairment-aware design, an important step toward practical network adoption.

title: How To Bake A Composition Operator From Scratch
authors: Michael R Pilla
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At face value, composition operators look like something first experienced in algebra. It's just composition of functions after all. However, there is a deep and technical setting in which these objects live, behaving like infinite-dimensional matrices acting on strange yet fascinating spaces. We take a novel approach to introducing a dense mathematical topic by mirroring that of a so-called scratch kitchen, where ingredients are not prepackaged, processed, or frozen but rather are fresh. While some mathematical maturity will certainly help in the same way that baking experience helps with a new recipe, nothing in one's background is assumed. Along the way, we make no reservations about making historical or philosophical comments to spark reader's interest as well. Bon appetit!
tldr: An expository, 'from-scratch' introduction to composition operators on infinite-dimensional function spaces, written in the style of a scratch kitchen recipe.
motivation: The author aims to make a dense and technical topic in functional analysis accessible to readers with minimal background by adopting an informal, metaphor-rich pedagogical style.
method: The paper presents a self-contained, pedagogically oriented exposition of composition operators and the operator-theoretic framework in which they act, interspersed with historical and philosophical comments.
result: No new theorems or technical results are claimed; the contribution is an accessible narrative exposition of the subject matter.
conclusion: The work is a mathematical expository article intended to spark reader interest rather than to advance quantum information theory or any related physics field.

title: Intrinsic Path Following On $\mathsf{SO}(3)$
authors: Adeel Akhtar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies intrinsic path following for fully actuated rigid-body attitude dynamics over a broad class of attitude paths, namely arbitrary smooth embedded closed curves on [MATH]. We construct a tangential--transverse state decomposition on a tubular neighborhood using normal and pullback bundle geometry. The resulting second-order dynamics admit a smooth feedback transformation that independently assigns tangential and transverse covariant accelerations. A transverse proportional--derivative law renders the path-following manifold invariant and locally uniformly exponentially stable on an explicit forward-invariant neighborhood, while leaving the tangential dynamics freely assignable. This allows independent regulation of progression along the path, stabilization of a selected attitude on the path, or tracking of a time-varying motion. For a representative fiber path, the tubular coordinates are obtained in closed form up to the natural cut-locus obstruction, and simulations illustrate point stabilization and trajectory tracking.
tldr: The paper develops an intrinsic geometric control framework for path following of fully actuated rigid-body attitude dynamics on SO(3) using tangential-transverse decomposition and feedback linearization.
motivation: Path following for attitude dynamics is typically treated in local coordinates, which obscures global geometric properties and complicates the design of independent tangential and transverse control objectives.
method: The authors construct a tangential-transverse state decomposition on a tubular neighborhood of a smooth embedded closed curve on SO(3) using normal and pullback bundle geometry, then derive a smooth feedback transformation that independently assigns tangential and transverse covariant accelerations.
result: A transverse proportional-derivative law makes the path-following manifold invariant and locally uniformly exponentially stable on an explicit forward-invariant neighborhood, while the tangential dynamics remain freely assignable; closed-form tubular coordinates are obtained for a representative fiber path up to the cut locus, with simulations demonstrating point stabilization and trajectory tracking.
conclusion: The approach enables independent regulation of progression along the path, stabilization of a selected attitude, and tracking of time-varying motions, providing a geometrically intrinsic solution for rigid-body attitude path following.

title: Auditing The Privacy Of Synthetic Gene Expression Data: A Unified Weighted-Distance Framework For No-Box Membership Inference
authors: Owen Tucker, Lily Wang, Harutoshi Okumura, Ruixuan Liu, Li Xiong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic gene expression data is increasingly proposed as a privacy-preserving substitute for controlled-access genomic repositories, but its safety depends on empirical auditing. Membership inference attacks (MIAs) provide that audit by testing whether a patient's gene expression profile was used to train a generative model. We report a red-team study on synthetic gene expression data derived from bulk RNA-seq profiles in The Cancer Genome Atlas, released by the ELSA Health 2026 Challenge. We unify five no-box attacks under a single weighted-distance framework in which each variant differs only in how it weights genes: uniformly (baseline), by variance, by synthetic-versus-reference KL divergence, by spectral residualization removing dominant principal components, and by curated pathway membership. Against a conditional variational autoencoder, spectral residualization raises AUC from 0.8251 to 0.8951 and TPR at 1% FPR from 0.3842 to 0.5970 on pan-cancer TCGA. Biological pathway priors did not transfer across targets.
tldr: This paper presents a red-team audit of privacy risks in synthetic gene expression data by unifying five no-box membership inference attacks under a weighted-distance framework.
motivation: Synthetic gene expression data is proposed as a privacy-preserving alternative to controlled-access genomic repositories, but its safety requires empirical auditing against membership inference attacks.
method: The authors unify five no-box attacks differing only in gene weighting schemes (uniform, variance, synthetic-vs-reference KL divergence, spectral residualization, and pathway membership) and evaluate them against a conditional variational autoencoder on TCGA bulk RNA-seq data.
result: Spectral residualization improved attack performance, raising AUC from 0.8251 to 0.8951 and TPR at 1% FPR from 0.3842 to 0.5970 on pan-cancer TCGA, while biological pathway priors did not transfer across targets.
conclusion: Privacy auditing of synthetic genomic data benefits from weighting strategies that remove dominant principal components, but biological priors may not generalize across datasets.

title: Uniform Meandric Systems As Percolation On Planar Maps: Conjectures And A Numerical Study
authors: David Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We perform a numerical study of uniform meandric systems via their encoding by pairs of simple random walks and their interpretation as a model of critical percolation on random planar maps. We investigate certain natural box-crossing events and provide numerical evidence for a strong negative association between opposite open crossings and formulate conjectures on their asymptotic behavior. Our second contribution is a simple law-preserving dynamics on meandric systems, by local peak/valley flips in the walk encoding. Our simulations suggest that the percolation structure decorrelates much faster than the underlying random planar map.
tldr: A numerical and conjectural study of uniform meandric systems, interpreting them as critical percolation on random planar maps and introducing a local flip dynamics.
motivation: Meandric systems are combinatorially rich objects that admit random-walk encodings, and the authors aim to understand their large-scale percolation-like structure and dynamics.
method: The paper uses pairs of simple random walks to encode meandric systems, performs Monte Carlo simulations of box-crossing events, and defines a law-preserving local peak/valley flip dynamics.
result: Simulations provide evidence for strong negative association between opposite open crossings and suggest conjectures on asymptotic behavior, while the proposed dynamics appears to decorrelate the percolation structure faster than the underlying random planar map.
conclusion: The work contributes numerical observations and conjectures about uniform meandric systems as percolation on planar maps, but it lies outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Cooperation Thrives When Moral Judgment Matches Moral Conduct
authors: Jorge Pe\~na, Julian Garcia, Toby Handfield
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A leading explanation for why humans cooperate with strangers is indirect reciprocity: when conduct is observed, individuals earn good reputations by cooperating with the deserving. Previous research has identified many "moral systems" that sustain cooperation through indirect reciprocity - each pairing a strategy for how to act with a norm for how to judge others - yet what makes them succeed, and whether that success generalizes beyond the donation game, has remained unclear. Here we evaluate all 1,048,576 moral systems whose norms condition on both players' reputations and actions, across every two-player social dilemma. We find that every highly stable, cooperative system pairs a "discriminating" strategy - one that cooperates with the good and defects against the bad when in good standing - with a "consistent" norm that deems good exactly those who act as the strategy prescribes. Such systems "practice what they preach" and preach what they practice. In the limit of small errors, only one strategy paired with a consistent norm remains stable across all social dilemmas: the "contrite discriminator", which cooperates to make amends when its standing is bad. Our results unify decades of research on indirect reciprocity, revealing moral consistency as the common ingredient of every stable, cooperative moral system.
