tldr: A comprehensive evolutionary game-theoretic analysis of 1,048,576 moral systems shows that stable cooperation via indirect reciprocity requires a consistent match between moral judgment and moral conduct across social dilemmas.
motivation: Indirect reciprocity explains human cooperation with strangers, but it was unclear which of the many possible moral systems sustain cooperation and whether that success generalizes beyond the donation game.
method: The authors evaluate all 1,048,576 moral systems whose norms condition on both players' reputations and actions across every two-player social dilemma, analyzing stability and cooperation in the limit of small errors.
result: Highly stable, cooperative systems pair a discriminating strategy with a consistent norm, and in the small-error limit only the 'contrite discriminator' paired with a consistent norm remains stable across all social dilemmas.
conclusion: Moral consistency—practicing what you preach and preaching what you practice—is the common ingredient of every stable, cooperative moral system, unifying decades of research on indirect reciprocity.

title: An Absorbing State Model With An Emergent Ising Transition
authors: Shen Ai, Dov Levine, Paul Chaikin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a dynamical model of repulsive needles with centers fixed on a square lattice. Needles that overlap are active and receive a repulsive rotation [MATH]; needles with no overlap do not move. This model exhibits an absorbing state transition. Nematic order was observed for long needles. For a range of needle lengths and [MATH], the system self-organizes into a state with checkerboard symmetry. As [MATH] is increased, this phase melts and becomes disordered. Remarkably, we find that this phase boundary exhibits critical exponents identical to those of the equilibrium 2D Ising model.
tldr: A classical dynamical model of repulsive needles on a square lattice exhibits an absorbing state transition with an emergent Ising-like phase boundary.
motivation: The authors aim to study how simple dynamical rules for repulsive needles can produce collective ordering and critical behavior reminiscent of equilibrium phase transitions.
method: They simulate a lattice model where overlapping needles are active and rotate repulsively, while non-overlapping needles remain fixed, and analyze the resulting phases and critical exponents.
result: Nematic order appears for long needles, and for certain parameters a checkerboard-symmetric phase emerges that melts upon increasing the repulsive rotation strength, with critical exponents matching the 2D Ising universality class.
conclusion: The model provides a classical example of an absorbing state transition with emergent Ising criticality, connecting nonequilibrium dynamics to equilibrium universality.

title: Verification Of The Outer Space Treaty With Active Interrogation
authors: Patrick Huber
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analysis of active interrogation in space with the goal to verify the absence of nuclear weapons hidden in a large constellation of satellites. We propose a 16 MeV photon beam generated by advanced laser wakefield accelerators and the detection of fission neutrons using segmented organic scintillators. We use Starlink as a real-world example for the constellation and solve the inspector routing problem against this set of 7,852 satellites over a 5-year mission period. We perform detailed simulation of the nuclear and orbit physics: signal generation and detection with GEANT4 against an orbit-resolved neutron and gamma background, routes flown with Orekit including the effects from the Earth's oblateness, and detection decided by a likelihood ratio test. We identify different encounter types and fleet designs based on a range of inspector platforms. The radiation dose to target satellites from the beam can be kept to about 1% or less of the 5-year space environment dose. We find that a small number of inspection platforms, 20-70 depending on the accelerator assumptions, can serve inspections to the full constellation with a detection probability of 90% against a single deployed warhead. A 10% random sample of the whole fleet can be inspected by 2-20 platforms providing a 37% detection probability against 5 deployed warheads.
tldr: The paper analyzes active interrogation using a photon beam and neutron detection to verify the absence of nuclear weapons in large satellite constellations, using Starlink as a case study.
motivation: To verify compliance with the Outer Space Treaty by detecting hidden nuclear weapons in satellite constellations.
method: Simulates a 16 MeV photon beam from laser wakefield accelerators, fission neutron detection with organic scintillators, GEANT4 nuclear and orbital background modeling, Orekit routing, and a likelihood ratio test.
result: For Starlink's 7,852 satellites, 20-70 inspector platforms achieve 90% detection probability against one warhead; a 10% sample with 2-20 platforms yields 37% detection against five warheads.
conclusion: Active interrogation is feasible for treaty verification with radiation doses about 1% of the 5-year space environment dose.

title: Neural Network Solvers For Nonlinear ODEs: Benchmarking MLPs And B-Spline/Chebyshev KANs
authors: Mahidhar Reddy Patukuri, B. Veena S. N. Rao, S. M. Mallikarjunaiah
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Three neural networks are compared as solvers of nonlinear ordinary differential equations: a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) whose edges are B-splines, and a KAN whose edges are Chebyshev series. Each network is trained only on the residual of the equation and on its initial or boundary conditions. The exact solution, or a numerical solution accurate to [MATH], is used only afterward to measure the error. Five test problems of differential orders one to four are investigated: the logistic equation, a singular Lane-Emden type initial value problem, a singular boundary value problem, the Falkner-Skan equation with suction, a fourth-order problem. The same training budget and the same choice of five activation functions are allocated to all networks. No numerical failures are encountered in any of the \nRuns{} training runs. For every problem, the best KAN is found to be at least as accurate as the best MLP while \paramsKANmin{} to \paramsKANmax{} parameters are used instead of \paramsMLP{}; the margin ranges from a tie to a factor of three. In the Falkner-Skan setting of an earlier study, the B-spline KAN is shown to be 34 to 220 times more accurate at every published test point. Much smaller MLPs are also found to be competitive, whereas at orders three and four, failures are experienced more frequently by KANs, and a coarse basis is required. The derivatives in the equation are distorted by the usual grid extension of a B-spline KAN; consequently, it is replaced with knot insertion, by which the logistic error is lowered more than a hundredfold, though no improvement is provided at order four.
tldr: This paper benchmarks multilayer perceptrons against B-spline and Chebyshev Kolmogorov-Arnold networks as solvers for nonlinear ordinary differential equations.
motivation: The authors aim to compare the accuracy and parameter efficiency of MLPs and KAN variants for solving nonlinear ODEs, including singular and higher-order problems, while training only on residuals and boundary/initial conditions.
method: Three neural networks (MLP, B-spline KAN, Chebyshev KAN) are trained using the same budget and activation functions on five test ODE problems of orders one to four, using only the equation residual and initial/boundary conditions; exact or reference solutions are used only for error evaluation.
result: For every problem, the best KAN matches or exceeds the best MLP with far fewer parameters, with margins up to a factor of three; in a Falkner-Skan comparison, the B-spline KAN is 34–220 times more accurate. However, B-spline KANs suffer from derivative distortion due to grid extension, which is mitigated by knot insertion, improving logistic equation accuracy over a hundredfold but not at order four.
conclusion: KANs, particularly B-spline variants, can be more parameter-efficient and accurate than MLPs for certain nonlinear ODEs, but they face challenges at higher orders and require careful basis and knot handling.

title: Tilings Of Closed Surfaces By Congruent Most Curvilinear Polygons
authors: Min Yan Haofang Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study tilings of closed surfaces by congruent most curvilinear polygons. By relating such tilings to branched coverings determined by planar diagrams and vertex types, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a given closed topological surface to admit a metric of constant curvature supporting a tiling with prescribed combinatorial data and number of tiles. We also characterize minimal tilings, which do not descend through nontrivial unbranched coverings to tilings with fewer tiles, in terms of common block decompositions of the associated permutations. Explicit permutation constructions yield infinite families of minimal tilings with prescribed vertex types, even when the planar diagram and vertex types are fixed. In the hyperbolic setting, these results also give finite-index subgroups of the universal tiling symmetry groups that are maximal among torsion-free subgroups, with the index equal to the number of tiles.
tldr: The paper studies tilings of closed surfaces by congruent curvilinear polygons and characterizes existence and minimality via branched coverings and permutations.
motivation: The authors aim to understand when a closed topological surface admits a constant-curvature metric supporting a tiling with prescribed combinatorial data and a given number of tiles.
method: They relate tilings to branched coverings determined by planar diagrams and vertex types, and analyze minimal tilings using permutations and common block decompositions.
result: They establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of such tilings, characterize minimal tilings via permutation decompositions, and construct infinite families of minimal tilings with fixed planar diagram and vertex types.
conclusion: In the hyperbolic setting, the results yield finite-index subgroups of universal tiling symmetry groups that are maximal among torsion-free subgroups, with index equal to the number of tiles.

title: Repunit Coordinates For The Erd\H{o}s Ternary-Digit Problem
authors: Michael A. Idowu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Paul Erds conjectured that the only powers of two whose ternary expansions contain no digit 2 are 1, 4, and 256. Despite extensive computational verification, the conjecture remains open. We reformulate the problem using generalised base-4 repunits. Any admissible exponent is even, say \(n=2s\), and \[ 2^{2s}=4^s=3R_s(4)+1,\qquad R_s(4)={3}. \] Thus \(2^{2s}\) omits the ternary digit 2 if and only if \(R_s(4)\) does. For each depth \(m\), the map \(\Phi_m:s\bmod 3^m\mapsto R_s(4)\bmod 3^m\) is a permutation of the residue classes modulo \(3^m\). Hence every prescribed \(m\)-digit ternary suffix has a unique canonical exponent seed modulo \(3^m\), and all exponents producing that suffix form an arithmetic progression. The lifting identity \[ R_{r+q3^m}(4)\equiv R_r(4)+q3^m} \] gives three lifts at each depth, exactly two of which preserve admissibility. The finite maps assemble into an isometric homeomorphism of the 3-adic integers conjugating \(x \mapsto x+1\) with \(y \mapsto 4y+1\). The unresolved global integer problem remains. No proof of the Erds conjecture is claimed.
tldr: This paper reformulates the Erdős ternary-digit problem using base-4 repunits and 3-adic maps, but does not prove the conjecture.
motivation: Erdős conjectured that only 1, 4, and 256 are powers of two whose ternary expansions contain no digit 2, and the problem remains open despite computational verification.
method: The author expresses 2^{2s} as 3 R_s(4)+1 and studies the map from exponents modulo 3^m to base-4 repunits modulo 3^m, showing it is a permutation and deriving a lifting identity.
result: Each prescribed m-digit ternary suffix corresponds to a unique canonical exponent seed modulo 3^m, and the finite maps assemble into a 3-adic isometric homeomorphism conjugating x -> x+1 with y -> 4y+1.
conclusion: The reformulation provides structural insight but leaves the global integer problem unresolved, and no proof of the Erdős conjecture is claimed.

title: The Upper semi-Fredholm Radius, Extensions Of Restrictions, And Subprojectivity
authors: Abdelhalim Azzouz
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a bounded operator [MATH] between Banach spaces, let [MATH] be its distance to the operators that are not upper semi-Fredholm, and let [MATH] be Schechter's quantity [MATH] over infinite-dimensional subspaces [MATH]. One always has [MATH], and Gonz\'alez and Martin\'on showed that the two quantities are not equivalent in general. We prove that [MATH] is the infimum of the norms of operators on the whole space that extend a restriction of [MATH] to some infinite-dimensional subspace. The gap between [MATH] and [MATH] thus becomes an extension problem, and projection constants enter naturally. If the domain is uniformly subprojective with constant [MATH], then [MATH]. In the other direction we prove a quantitative obstruction: a complemented Hilbertian subspace all of whose infinite-dimensional subspaces have projection constant at least [MATH] produces operators with [MATH]. Consequently, on the subprojective but not uniformly subprojective space [MATH] with [MATH], there is no uniform comparison between [MATH] and [MATH]. We conjecture that uniform comparison is equivalent to uniform subprojectivity. Finally, we compute [MATH] for inverses and for shears in terms of the quantity [MATH], and we use the arbitrary distortability of Hilbert space to show that a rectangular diagonal operator [MATH] built from two isomorphisms with [MATH] can have arbitrarily small [MATH]. In contrast, every operator [MATH] on a complex Banach space satisfies [MATH], so every automorphism satisfies [MATH] and the same mechanism cannot work for endomorphisms.
tldr: The paper studies the upper semi-Fredholm radius of bounded operators on Banach spaces and relates it to extension problems for restrictions to infinite-dimensional subspaces, projection constants, and subprojectivity.
motivation: The quantities measuring distance to non-upper-semi-Fredholm operators and Schechter's quantity over infinite-dimensional subspaces are known not to be equivalent in general, and the paper seeks a structural explanation through extension and projection-constant properties.
method: The author proves that one quantity is the infimum of norms of global operators extending a restriction to an infinite-dimensional subspace, then uses uniform subprojectivity and complemented Hilbertian subspaces to obtain quantitative bounds and obstructions.
result: Uniform subprojectivity yields a comparison between the quantities, while quantitative obstructions show no uniform comparison exists on subprojective but not uniformly subprojective Banach spaces; explicit computations are given for inverses and shears.
conclusion: The gap between the two semi-Fredholm quantities is characterized as an extension problem involving projection constants, leading to the conjecture that uniform comparison is equivalent to uniform subprojectivity.

title: Directional Measure Rigidity For Time-changed First Row Unipotent Actions
authors: Daren Wei Davide Ravotti
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study flows on finite volume homogeneous manifolds arising as directional restrictions of time changes of higher rank abelian unipotent actions. We establish Ratner-type rigidity results in this setting. For first row actions on finite volume quotients of [MATH], we show that natural quantitative assumptions on the cocycle force the flow to be algebraic and its ergodic invariant measure to be homogeneous. These results extend to higher dimensional subactions and to a general abstract setting. We also show that, on compact quotients of [MATH], the smooth time change is smoothly conjugate to a linear algebraic action by a leaf preserving diffeomorphism if and only if the cocycle of the directional flow has bounded deviations along one direction. We also obtain precise asymptotics for compact root increments. The principal thresholds in our results are sharp.
tldr: The paper proves Ratner-type rigidity results for directional flows arising from time-changed higher-rank abelian unipotent actions on finite-volume homogeneous manifolds.
motivation: The study is motivated by understanding measure rigidity and algebraic structure of directional restrictions of time-changed unipotent flows, extending Ratner's theorems to a more general setting.
method: The authors use quantitative assumptions on the cocycle, bounded deviations along one direction, and smooth conjugacy arguments on compact quotients to establish homogeneity of ergodic invariant measures.
result: They show that under natural quantitative assumptions the flow must be algebraic and its ergodic invariant measure homogeneous, and on compact quotients a smooth time change is smoothly conjugate to a linear algebraic action iff the cocycle has bounded deviations along one direction.
conclusion: The results provide sharp thresholds and extend to higher-dimensional subactions and an abstract setting, contributing to rigidity theory in homogeneous dynamics.

title: Ris Aided Multi-Way Communication Systems Based On Sic Decoding Techniques
authors: Harry Leib Lingya Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work considers reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) aided multi-way communication systems employing QPSK. The objectives of such system is to allow multiple users to exchange information, exploiting the full-duplex capabilities of RIS. The system under consideration comprises [MATH] user terminals and an RIS with [MATH] reflective elements. Each user terminal is equipped with one transmit and [MATH] receive antennas. To mitigate inter-user interference caused by the full-duplex operation of the RIS, three successive interference cancellation (SIC) techniques are considered. We investigate three SIC ordering methods: [MATH] descending channel variances, [MATH] increasing mean square error, [MATH] optimization approach which maximizes the combined channel gain within the system. The bit error rate (BER) performance of these three SIC methods are evaluated using extensive Monte-Carlo simulations for different numbers of RIS elements, ranging from 4 to 64, and a varying number of transmitting users, ranging from 1 to 5. Additionally, an RIS phase shift optimization method for RIS with reflection elements of varying amplitudes is considered. In this case the previous SIC optimization technique is adapted to address phase-dependent amplitudes in RIS reflection elements. Simulation results indicate that in both ideal and varying amplitude scenarios, when the number of RIS elements is small, SIC with ordering based on increasing mean square error achieves the best BER performance. However, as the number of RIS elements increases, SIC ordering based on the optimization method achieves the best BER performance.
tldr: This paper studies reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multi-way communication systems using QPSK and successive interference cancellation (SIC) decoding techniques.
motivation: The work aims to enable multiple users to exchange information simultaneously by exploiting the full-duplex capabilities of an RIS while mitigating inter-user interference.
method: Three SIC ordering methods are considered: descending channel variances, increasing mean square error, and an optimization approach maximizing combined channel gain; performance is evaluated via Monte-Carlo simulations with varying RIS elements and users, including a phase-shift optimization method for varying reflection amplitudes.
result: Simulations show that for a small number of RIS elements, SIC ordering based on increasing mean square error achieves the best BER performance, whereas for larger numbers of RIS elements, the optimization-based SIC ordering performs best in both ideal and varying-amplitude scenarios.
conclusion: The paper provides a comparative analysis of SIC ordering schemes for RIS-aided multi-way communication, identifying the preferred ordering depending on the number of RIS elements.

title: Mean Squared Error Reduction Of (plug-in) Look-ahead Estimators For Markov Chains
authors: Romain Aza\"is, Beno\^it Henry, Henri P\'echoux
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the estimation of the invariant distribution [MATH] of a Markov kernel on a discrete state space (or of the mean value [MATH] of a functional [MATH] under [MATH]) when solving the invariance equation is not feasible. Look-ahead estimators exploit the knowledge of the kernel by propagating the empirical occupation measure through [MATH] steps of the chain. When the kernel is known, as in Markov chain Monte Carlo, we compare their mean squared error with that of the empirical estimator, for independent or Markovian data, stationary or not. Our main result establishes that, for Markovian data, the one-step estimator always improves on the empirical one asymptotically, and that the improvement grows with [MATH] for reversible kernels. A non-reversible counterexample shows that reversibility cannot simply be dropped. In the statistical setting where the kernel belongs to a parametric family with unknown parameter, we introduce plug-in look-ahead estimators, which perform the look-ahead step with an estimated kernel. When the parameter is estimated at the parametric rate, we give a necessary and sufficient condition under which the plug-in look-ahead estimator outperforms the empirical one. The theoretical results are illustrated by extensive simulation studies, which also shed further light on the behaviour of the estimators at hand. Both settings are finally applied to real data arising from geographical mobility problems in the Lyon metropolitan area, France.
tldr: The paper analyzes mean squared error improvements of look-ahead and plug-in look-ahead estimators for Markov chain invariant distributions, with applications to geographical mobility data.
motivation: Estimating invariant distributions or functionals of Markov kernels can be difficult when solving the invariance equation is infeasible, motivating estimators that exploit known or estimated kernel information.
method: The authors compare empirical and look-ahead estimators using asymptotic mean squared error analysis for independent and Markovian data, introduce plug-in versions when the kernel is parameterized, and validate with simulations and real data.
result: For Markovian data, the one-step look-ahead estimator asymptotically improves on the empirical estimator, with greater improvement for reversible kernels as the number of steps increases; a non-reversible counterexample shows reversibility is essential, and a necessary and sufficient condition is given for plug-in estimators to outperform the empirical one.
conclusion: Look-ahead and plug-in look-ahead estimators can reduce mean squared error in Markov chain estimation, but their advantage depends on reversibility and the parametric estimation rate, as illustrated by simulations and mobility data.

title: Continuous Families Of Central Configurations For Even-Power Homogeneous Potentials
authors: Pawel Nurowski
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study central configurations for [MATH] bodies interacting through pair potentials \[ U_\sigma = {\sigma} \sum_{i<j}m_i m_j r_{ij}^{\sigma}, \] with logarithmic limit at [MATH]. For the Newtonian exponent [MATH], the classical Chazy--Wintner--Smale finiteness problem asks whether, for prescribed positive masses, there are only finitely many central configurations up to similarity. Finiteness is known in several important special cases and under additional dimensional or genericity hypotheses. It is therefore natural to ask whether an analogous finiteness principle continues to hold for other homogeneous exponents. We show that for every positive even exponent \[ \sigma=2k, \qquad k\ge2, \] the answer is emphatically negative. In fact, these exponents admit an abundance of continuous families of pairwise non-similar central configurations. The mechanism is provided by spherical designs: on a common sphere the force kernel for [MATH] restricts to a polynomial of degree at most [MATH], and consequently every positive weighted spherical [MATH]-design is a central configuration. We compute the corresponding central multiplier explicitly.
tldr: The paper shows that for even-power homogeneous potentials, the finiteness problem for central configurations fails dramatically, with continuous families arising from spherical designs.
motivation: The classical Chazy–Wintner–Smale problem asks whether the number of central configurations is finite for given positive masses, and it is natural to ask whether analogous finiteness holds for other homogeneous exponents.
method: The authors analyze central configurations for pair potentials of the form U_sigma = sigma sum_{i<j} m_i m_j r_{ij}^sigma, focusing on even exponents sigma = 2k, and use the connection to spherical designs to construct continuous families.
result: For every positive even exponent sigma = 2k with k >= 2, there exist continuous families of pairwise non-similar central configurations; in fact, any positive weighted spherical (2k)-design gives a central configuration, and the central multiplier is computed explicitly.
conclusion: The finiteness principle for central configurations does not generalize to even homogeneous exponents, revealing a rich and unexpected solution structure driven by spherical designs.

title: Consistency Of Penalized Maximum Likelihood Estimation For Multidimensional Change-in-velocity Detection
authors: Linh Do, Dat Do, Scott A. Mckinley
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish statistical consistency for the penalized maximum-likelihood estimator underlying CPLASS, a method for detecting changes in velocity in [MATH]-dimensional time-series data. The signal is modeled as a continuous piecewise-linear trajectory observed with independent Gaussian noise. Unlike classical change-in-mean models, continuity across adjacent segments couples their parameters and prevents direct application of standard segmentation arguments. Under compact parameter spaces, minimum segment-length and velocity-jump conditions, and a strengthened Schwarz information criterion penalty [MATH] with [MATH], we prove joint consistency of the estimated number of segments and all changepoint locations in the high-frequency regime [MATH]. The maximum changepoint-location error is [MATH]. The proof first uses empirical-process theory to establish convergence of the fitted signal, variance, and likelihood for each fixed model size. It then combines overfitting and underfitting arguments with a two-stage geometric localization analysis, yielding an initial [MATH] rate that is sharpened by exploiting the local two-segment continuous piecewise-linear structure.
tldr: The paper proves statistical consistency of a penalized maximum-likelihood estimator for detecting changes in velocity in multidimensional time-series data.
motivation: Change-in-velocity detection is important for analyzing continuous piecewise-linear trajectories, but existing theory for change-in-mean models does not directly apply because continuity couples adjacent segments.
method: The authors use empirical-process theory to show convergence for fixed model sizes, then combine overfitting and underfitting arguments with a two-stage geometric localization analysis to establish consistency in the high-frequency regime.
result: Under compact parameter spaces, minimum segment-length and velocity-jump conditions, and a strengthened Schwarz information criterion penalty, they prove joint consistency of the estimated number of segments and all changepoint locations, with maximum changepoint-location error decaying at a certain rate.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous statistical guarantees for the CPLASS method and sharpens the localization rate by exploiting the local two-segment continuous piecewise-linear structure.

title: Computing Equilibria In Integer Programming Games With Shared Constraints
authors: Bainian Hao, Hyunwoo Lee, Robert Hildebrand, Carla Michini
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a cutting-plane algorithm for computing pure Nash equilibria in finite integer games with shared constraints, where a deviation may be feasible against one opponent profile and infeasible against another. Conditional equilibrium inequalities capture this dependence through an explicit activation term. We give affine encodings of costs and activation conditions and prove that the resulting inequalities characterize the equilibrium set exactly. Embedded as lazy constraints in branch-and-cut, they yield the Generalized Zero-Regret algorithm for optimizing a linear objective over exact or approximate equilibria; a bisection procedure maintains certified bounds on the smallest achievable approximation factor. We also prove that, when the conditional polytopes have integral vertices, a concave cost is constant on the minimal face containing an equilibrium strategy, so strict concavity forces vertex strategies; for uniform integer-splittable bin packing, a cost-preserving transformation yields vertex equilibria even without strict concavity. We give formulations for bin packing, network formation, and knapsack games with shared capacities and evaluate the algorithm on 3,300 instances, computing a socially optimal equilibrium on all but 43, certifying nonexistence on 16, and certifying approximation factors within a few percent where no exact equilibrium exists.
tldr: The paper develops a cutting-plane algorithm for computing pure Nash equilibria in finite integer programming games with shared constraints.
motivation: Equilibrium computation in games with shared constraints is challenging because deviations can be feasible or infeasible depending on opponent profiles.
method: It introduces conditional equilibrium inequalities with activation terms, affine encodings, and embeds them as lazy constraints in a branch-and-cut framework called the Generalized Zero-Regret algorithm.
result: The algorithm computes socially optimal equilibria on most of 3,300 instances, certifies nonexistence on 16, and bounds approximation factors within a few percent when no exact equilibrium exists.
conclusion: The approach provides exact equilibrium characterizations and practical computation for integer games, with applications to bin packing, network formation, and knapsack games.

title: Optimal Community Recovery By Spectrally Initialized Variational Em In General Stochastic Block Models
authors: Jiangzhou Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Chernoff-exponent guarantee for the output of spectrally initialized batch variational EM after a prescribed iteration budget, without assuming global maximization of its variational objective. The iteration repeatedly estimates the entire block probability matrix and community proportions from the same sparse graph. We consider a fixed number of communities with proportions bounded away from zero and fixed, positive, distinct connectivity profiles; neither assortativity nor full rank is required. The algorithm uses simultaneous softmax updates without sample splitting or posterior thresholding. Its analysis must control the feedback between estimated parameters, soft labels and reused edges at an exponentially small risk scale. We establish a uniform one-step bound over data-dependent soft assignments whose random remainder has exponentially small expectation. Combined with an exponentially reliable regularized spectral initializer, this yields an unconditional expected misclassification rate bounded by [MATH] throughout the sparse, diverging-degree regime, where [MATH] is the minimum nodewise Chernoff information. Matching lower bounds establish first-order logarithmic minimax optimality on local parameter spaces allowing unknown connectivity and varying community counts. The algorithm also attains the sharp first-order exact-recovery threshold. Numerical experiments illustrate refinement gains and sensitivity to initialization and imbalance.
tldr: This paper proves Chernoff-exponent guarantees for spectrally initialized variational EM in general stochastic block models, achieving optimal community recovery in sparse regimes.
motivation: Community detection in stochastic block models is a central problem in network analysis, and variational EM with spectral initialization is a popular practical approach, but its theoretical guarantees have been limited.
method: The authors analyze a batch variational EM algorithm that uses simultaneous softmax updates, no sample splitting, and a regularized spectral initializer, controlling the feedback between estimated parameters, soft labels, and reused edges.
result: They establish an unconditional expected misclassification rate bounded by the minimum nodewise Chernoff information and prove matching lower bounds, showing first-order logarithmic minimax optimality and the sharp exact-recovery threshold.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous theoretical foundations for spectrally initialized variational EM in general stochastic block models, with numerical experiments illustrating refinement gains and sensitivity to initialization and imbalance.

title: Arbitrarily High-Order Structure-Preserving Parametric Finite Element Methods For Geometric PDEs Via Local Pullback Flow Maps
authors: Weizhu Bao, Yifei Li, Dongmin Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop arbitrarily high-order structure-preserving parametric finite element methods for geometric PDEs including surface diffusion and volume-preserving mean curvature flow based on local pullback flow maps. The central idea is to reformulate the geometric PDEs on an arbitrary intermediate hypersurface and represent the subsequent evolution through a local pullback flow map. Using admissible local pullbacks, we derive two formulations from the corresponding pullback identities for the Laplace-Beltrami operator, referred to as the conformal and equidistribution formulations. We discretize both formulations using arbitrary-degree isoparametric finite elements and Runge-Kutta collocation methods with positive weights. For the conformal formulation, weighted averages of the normal-Jacobian vector ensure exact preservation of the enclosed area or volume, while algebraic stability of the Runge-Kutta method additionally guarantees dissipation of the perimeter or surface area. For the equidistribution formulation, a path-averaged normal-Jacobian vector and a geometric discrete gradient guarantee both exact preservation of the enclosed area or volume and dissipation of the perimeter or surface area, without requiring algebraic stability. Numerical experiments confirm the expected high-order accuracy and structure-preserving properties.
tldr: The paper develops arbitrarily high-order structure-preserving parametric finite element methods for geometric PDEs such as surface diffusion and volume-preserving mean curvature flow using local pullback flow maps.
motivation: Geometric PDEs require numerical methods that preserve geometric structures like enclosed volume and perimeter dissipation, and existing methods often lack arbitrary high-order accuracy or structure preservation.
method: The authors reformulate the PDEs on an intermediate hypersurface via local pullback flow maps, derive conformal and equidistribution formulations, and discretize using arbitrary-degree isoparametric finite elements and Runge-Kutta collocation methods with positive weights.
result: The conformal formulation preserves enclosed area/volume exactly and dissipates perimeter/surface area with algebraically stable Runge-Kutta methods, while the equidistribution formulation achieves both without algebraic stability; numerical experiments confirm high-order accuracy and structure preservation.
conclusion: The proposed methods provide a general framework for arbitrarily high-order structure-preserving numerical simulation of geometric PDEs, with rigorous preservation and dissipation properties.

title: Control OSWorld: An Ai Control Environment For Gui Computer Use Agents
authors: Mikhail Terekhov Maria Sanchez Del Rio
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents that operate a computer through its graphical user interface (GUI) are being widely deployed. AI control studies how to prevent an AI system from causing harm even if it is misaligned and actively trying to do so. Most control research to date has focused on coding agents, leaving computer use largely unexplored. We introduce Control OSWorld, a control evaluation that pairs 318 tasks from OSWorld with 81 harmful side tasks (e.g., exfiltrating a private file) that an agent must complete without being caught. We use Control OSWorld to create and study control monitors that detect malicious agents interacting with a GUI. We find that a weaker monitor can reliably distinguish honest from malicious trajectories produced by a more capable agent when it sees the full trajectory (97% recall at 3% false positive rate). However, when the monitor has to score each step before it is executed, recall drops at low false positive rates because each action is judged with less context. Monitor performance also depends on what the monitor can see: access to the agent's visible text is critical, while screenshots provide little additional value.
tldr: Control OSWorld is an AI control evaluation for GUI computer-use agents that tests whether monitors can detect malicious behavior, finding high full-trajectory recall but reduced stepwise recall.
motivation: AI agents that operate computers via GUI are widely deployed, but AI control research has focused mainly on coding agents, leaving GUI computer use largely unexplored.
method: The authors introduce Control OSWorld, pairing 318 OSWorld tasks with 81 harmful side tasks, and use it to build and study monitors that detect malicious GUI agents from full trajectories versus step-by-step actions.
result: A weaker monitor can reliably distinguish honest from malicious trajectories when seeing the full trajectory (97% recall at 3% false positive rate), but stepwise scoring drops recall at low false positive rates; access to visible text is critical while screenshots add little.
conclusion: Control monitors can work for GUI computer-use agents if given full context, but real-time stepwise monitoring remains challenging and effective monitoring depends more on textual than visual information.

title: From Requirements To Attack Trees: Grounded Llm Agents For Design-Time Security Review
authors: Akash Iyer, Taha Demirkan, Keerthi Koneru, Aaryan Siddharthan, Sheethal Kumar, Ramesh Radhakrishnan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Design-level security weaknesses can arise from requirements, trust assumptions, missing controls, and data flows before implementation begins. Existing security practices often identify these issues after code is written. We present a multi-agent LLM framework for design-time security analysis from product requirement documents and architecture diagrams. The proposed framework parses architecture diagrams into graph representations, generates misuse and failure cases, constructs attack trees, checks governance and compliance gaps, recommends mitigations, assigns enterprise security-domain tags, and produces a candidate revised architecture recommendation for expert review. The framework does not retrieve from Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) databases at inference time. Instead, it analyzes system behavior, trust boundaries, component interactions, and data-flow assumptions. Misuse cases act as intermediate representations that link findings to system components and attack paths, while a validation and refinement loop filters unsupported findings and improves grounding, traceability, and actionability. We evaluate the framework on a Microsoft reference-labeled threat-modeling example, labeled synthetic PRD--architecture pairs, and two open-ended systems: Berty and Gas Town. The reference-labeled case supports threat-recovery and actionability analysis, while the open-ended cases evaluate validity, noise, traceability, actionability, redundancy, and attack-tree quality. Results show that architecture-informed, misuse-driven reasoning improves review quality compared with single-shot and ablation baselines. Keywords: LLM Multi-Agent Systems, Design-Time Security, Threat Modeling, Vulnerability Discovery, Architecture Diagrams, Security Analysis, Misuse Case Derivation, Attack Trees, Iterative Reasoning, Security Governance.
tldr: A multi-agent LLM framework performs design-time security analysis from requirements and architecture diagrams, generating misuse cases, attack trees, and mitigation recommendations.
motivation: Design-level security weaknesses are often only discovered after implementation, so there is a need for automated, design-time threat modeling.
method: The framework parses architecture diagrams into graphs, derives misuse and failure cases, constructs attack trees, checks governance gaps, and uses a validation/refinement loop to improve grounding.
result: Evaluation on a Microsoft reference threat-modeling example, synthetic PRD-architecture pairs, and two open systems shows improved review quality over single-shot and ablation baselines.
conclusion: Architecture-informed, misuse-driven LLM reasoning can assist expert security review at design time, though the work is outside quantum information research.

title: $q$ Can Play That Game: Online Fitted $Q$-Iteration For Continuous-Action Zero-Sum Markov Games With Convex-Concave Function Approximation
authors: Kushagra Gupta, Jingqi Li, Cade Armstrong, Lasse Peters, Ross E. Allen, Ufuk Topcu, David Fridovich-Keil
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-sum Markov games arise in a wide variety of sequential decision-making problems such as adversarial learning and planning against modeled uncertainties. However, prior work on finite-sample guarantees on the learned state-action value function ([MATH]-function) for zero-sum Markov games is largely restricted to finite-action settings, or to continuous-action games in which agents have linear dynamics and quadratic rewards (i.e. linear-quadratic, or LQ, games). A central challenge in extending such guarantees to more general continuous-action zero-sum Markov games is that the associated Bellman operator involves a minimax problem that need not admit a tractable saddle-point solution. To this end, we first introduce a class of neural network function approximators for the [MATH]-function that is convex-concave in the players' actions, which guarantees that this minimax problem admits a pure-strategy saddle point. We then study an online variant of fitted [MATH]-iteration employing this function class and establish, to the best of our knowledge, the first finite-sample guarantees for non-LQ zero-sum Markov games with continuous states and actions. Our code can be found at [URL].
tldr: The paper introduces convex-concave neural network Q-function approximators and an online fitted Q-iteration algorithm for continuous-action zero-sum Markov games, providing the first finite-sample guarantees beyond linear-quadratic settings.
motivation: Finite-sample guarantees for zero-sum Markov games are largely limited to finite-action or linear-quadratic continuous-action settings, with general continuous-action games hindered by intractable minimax Bellman operators.
method: The authors design a neural network function approximator class that is convex-concave in the players' actions, guaranteeing a pure-strategy saddle point, and analyze an online variant of fitted Q-iteration using this class.
result: They establish, to the best of their knowledge, the first finite-sample guarantees for non-LQ zero-sum Markov games with continuous states and actions.
conclusion: This work advances theoretical foundations for multi-agent reinforcement learning in continuous control, offering provable learning guarantees and providing accompanying code.

title: The TellTail Of Embeddings: Fingerprinting Retrievers In Black-Box Systems
authors: Abdullah Garra, Matan Ben-Tov, Mahmood Sharif
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dense embedding models are core to modern text retrieval, enabling systems ranging from web search to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Yet, retrievers are usually deployed within opaque systems, exposing only ranked results, cited sources, or generated answers. This opacity prevents users from verifying which retrievers providers serve and may create a false sense of robustness against retrieval attacks. We show that attackers can infer retrievers' identity only through queries. We introduce TellTail, a fingerprinting attack for identifying retrievers behind black-box systems across a spectrum of access levels. Despite sharing many properties, retrievers can be steered to emit distinct results. When retrieved passages are exposed, TellTail compares retrieval overlap to deduce the underlying model. When only the final generated response is exposed, TellTail optimizes model-specific queries that induce a chosen retrieval behavior on the target retriever but transfer poorly to others. Interestingly, the poor transferability that limits attacks elsewhere is exactly what makes them useful for fingerprinting. We evaluate TellTail using 53 retrievers under three increasingly restrictive settings. TellTail perfectly identifies the deployed retriever from full retrieval rankings; in 94.3% of attempts with unordered top-3 results; and in 92.5% of cases from language-model-generated answers alone. Furthermore, fingerprinting succeeds against a popular RAG system (OpenWebUI). Overall, TellTail shows that retrieval-based systems leak the identity of their embedding model---exposing intellectual property and enabling reconnaissance ahead of model-specific attacks such as corpus poisoning.
tldr: The paper introduces TellTail, a fingerprinting attack that identifies dense embedding retrievers behind black-box retrieval or RAG systems using only queries and observed outputs.
motivation: Retrievers are often deployed opaquely, preventing users from verifying which embedding model a provider serves and potentially creating false robustness against retrieval attacks.
method: TellTail compares retrieval overlaps when passages are exposed, and when only generated answers are visible, it optimizes model-specific queries that induce distinct retrieval behavior on the target retriever while transferring poorly to others.
result: Evaluated across 53 retrievers and three access levels, TellTail perfectly identifies the retriever with full rankings, achieves 94.3% accuracy from unordered top-3 results, and 92.5% from generated answers alone, also succeeding against OpenWebUI.
conclusion: The work shows that retrieval-based systems leak the identity of their embedding model, exposing intellectual property and enabling reconnaissance for model-specific attacks such as corpus poisoning.

title: Deterministic Stackelberg Strategies In Robotaxi Assignment Games
authors: Ioannis Caragiannis, Kostas Kollias, Mohammad Roghani, Aaron Schild, Ali Kemal Sinop
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In autonomous mobility duopolies, platforms compete for riders based on vehicle proximity. A critical operational challenge---faced by an incumbent proactively defending against a market entrant---is how to dispatch fleets to minimize demand poached by a reactive competitor. We model this competition as a zero-sum robotaxi assignment game, focusing on computing optimal deterministic Stackelberg strategies for the leader. We formulate this problem as an exact single-level integer linear program and use its relaxation to design a polynomial-time approximation algorithm achieving an additive error from the optimum. We argue that this is not far from best possible by proving that deciding whether a strictly positive payoff is achievable is NP-complete, and that approximating the optimal payoff within an additive error scaling linearly with the number of riders is NP-hard. We also provide an exact polynomial-time dynamic programming algorithm for computing the optimal Stackelberg payoff when riders and vehicles are on the Euclidean line. Finally, we complement our theoretical findings with an empirical evaluation using real-world ride-hailing data. The experiments demonstrate that our LP-based algorithm significantly outperforms its worst-case guarantee in practice, while lightweight heuristics achieve highly competitive payoffs with negligible computational overhead, offering practical solutions for large-scale deployments.
tldr: The paper studies deterministic Stackelberg strategies for a leader in a zero-sum robotaxi assignment game against a reactive competitor, providing integer programming formulations, approximation algorithms, hardness results, and a dynamic programming solution for the Euclidean line case.
motivation: Autonomous mobility duopolies require incumbent platforms to optimally dispatch fleets to minimize demand lost to a reactive entrant.
method: The authors formulate the problem as an exact single-level integer linear program, design a polynomial-time approximation algorithm based on its relaxation, prove NP-completeness and NP-hardness of additive approximation, and give an exact dynamic programming algorithm for the Euclidean line.
result: The LP-based algorithm achieves an additive error from optimum, which is near-optimal under the hardness results; empirical evaluation on real ride-hailing data shows the algorithm outperforms its worst-case guarantee and lightweight heuristics achieve competitive payoffs with low overhead.
conclusion: The work provides both theoretical insights and practical algorithms for competitive robotaxi assignment, with experiments validating their effectiveness for large-scale deployments.

title: From Temporary Access To Persistent Surveillance: Why Matter Matters In Smart Homes
authors: Nicolas Nino, Timothy Minning, Le Guan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matter aims to unify smart home ecosystems through an open, interoperable, and secure standard, relying on cryptographic mechanisms for device authentication and data confidentiality. However, its openness also exposes protocol details, credential structures, and implementation characteristics to adversaries. We show that an attacker with temporary physical access can exploit design and implementation flaws to extract credentials and impersonate devices and controllers. These replicas integrate seamlessly into the fabric, enabling persistent surveillance and control even after the attacker departs. Notably, the attack is vendor-agnostic and requires no device-specific reverse engineering, as long as the device is not physically secured. We validate its practicality through a proof-of-concept on a simulated smart home with both commercial devices and development boards. Our findings uncover previously underestimated attack surfaces in Matter, particularly under physical access scenarios, and motivate four targeted mitigation strategies.
tldr: A security analysis showing that temporary physical access to Matter smart home devices can allow credential extraction and persistent surveillance, with vendor-agnostic attacks validated on a simulated smart home.
motivation: Matter aims to unify smart home ecosystems via an open, interoperable, and secure standard, but its openness may expose protocol details and credential structures to adversaries.
method: The authors demonstrate that an attacker with temporary physical access can exploit design and implementation flaws to extract credentials and impersonate devices and controllers; they validate practicality through a proof-of-concept on a simulated smart home with commercial devices and development boards.
result: The attack is vendor-agnostic and requires no device-specific reverse engineering if the device is not physically secured, enabling replicas that integrate seamlessly for persistent surveillance and control after the attacker departs.
conclusion: The findings uncover previously underestimated attack surfaces in Matter under physical access scenarios and motivate four targeted mitigation strategies.

title: Autonomous Active Directory Exploitation Via Multi-Model Harness Orchestration: A Benchmark Study With NeuroSploit On Goad
authors: Joas Antonio Dos Santos Barbosa
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active Directory (AD) remains the predominant identity and access management infrastructure in enterprise environments, and its compromise represents the highest-impact outcome in internal penetration tests. Recent work has shown that large language models (LLMs) can autonomously conduct assumed-breach penetration testing against AD, but these studies employ standalone agents lacking structured guardrails, deterministic validation, and multi-stage chain orchestration. We present a benchmark evaluation of NeuroSploit v4.2.0, an open-source Rust-based autonomous pentest harness, against the Game of Active Directory (GOAD), a deliberately vulnerable multi-forest AD lab maintained by Orange Cyberdefense comprising five virtual machines, two forests, and three domains. The harness orchestrates 22 AD-specific agents and 7 multi-stage attack-chain playbooks covering the full AD kill chain: enumeration, Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, NTLM relay and coercion, Kerberos delegation abuse, AD CS exploitation (ESC1-ESC8), MSSQL linked-server pivoting, DCSync, cross-forest trust abuse, and persistence detection. We benchmark nine frontier LLMs (Claude Opus 4.6/4.7/4.8, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6, Qwen 3.8, GLM 5.3, Kimi k3) within the harness, comparing against direct invocation across 14 technique categories and 7 chains. The harness achieves 96-100% technique coverage with 90-97% precision, while direct invocation covers only 21-54% and produces 3.2x more false positives. Time to full three-domain compromise with Opus 4.8 was 134 minutes with guardrail activations preventing lockout-triggering sprays, unauthorized DCSync dumps, and out-of-scope reconnaissance. Results demonstrate that structured harness orchestration with domain-specialized agents, POMDP belief tracking, and cross-model voting substantially outperforms unstructured LLM usage for AD penetration testing.
tldr: The paper benchmarks NeuroSploit, a Rust-based autonomous penetration-testing harness that orchestrates multiple LLM agents and attack-chain playbooks to compromise Active Directory environments.
motivation: Active Directory compromise is a high-impact goal in internal penetration testing, and prior LLM-based approaches lack structured guardrails, deterministic validation, and multi-stage chain orchestration.
method: The authors evaluate nine frontier LLMs within NeuroSploit v4.2.0 against the Game of Active Directory (GOAD) multi-forest lab, comparing orchestrated harness execution with direct LLM invocation across 14 technique categories and 7 attack chains.
result: The harness achieves 96–100% technique coverage and 90–97% precision, versus 21–54% coverage and 3.2× more false positives for direct invocation, with full three-domain compromise in 134 minutes using Opus 4.8.
conclusion: Structured harness orchestration with domain-specialized agents, POMDP belief tracking, and cross-model voting substantially outperforms unstructured LLM usage for Active Directory penetration testing.

title: GrayShield: Bit-Level Sanitization For Transformer Model Supply-Chain Security
authors: Armstrong Foundjem, Tsung-Hsien Chuang, Foutse Khomh, Mohamed Amine Merzouk
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer models such as BERT and Vision Transformer~(ViT) achieve strong performance via densely parameterized attention backbones. However, the least significant bits~(LSBs) of their 32-bit floating-point weights can be abused as covert channels to conceal malicious payloads, posing a serious threat to the AI model supply chain. We propose \GS (\GSabbr), a lightweight, post-training, zero-data sanitization method that completely replaces the declared mantissa-LSB channel with a Gray-code-guided low-transition sequence. Complete payload-independent overwrite, whether keyed or public, makes the sanitized target bits independent of the embedded payload and gives that declared channel zero capacity. Gray coding supplies overwrite structure, while a keyed per-tensor phase supplies pattern diversity. Benchmarked against seven post-training defenses on four Transformer model presets and two real-world malware payloads, \GSabbr maintains sub-[MATH] accuracy impact and achieves [MATH] percentage-point Recovery Reduction (RR) under five implemented attacker variants. Because pre-defense recovery is effectively [MATH], RR near 50 percentage points corresponds to post-sanitization bit accuracy at binary chance. Its main empirical advantage is stable near-chance sanitization with substantially smaller weight-distribution shift than the evaluated near-chance baselines PatternMask (PM) and Post-Training Quantization (PTQ).
tldr: GrayShield proposes a post-training bit-level sanitization method that overwrites least significant bits of Transformer weights to remove covert-channel malware payloads, assessed on standard vision and language models.
motivation: Malicious actors can hide payloads in the least significant bits of floating-point model weights, threatening AI supply chains, so a lightweight defense is needed that sanitizes models without retraining or data.
method: The method replaces declared mantissa LSB channels with a Gray-code-guided low-transition overwrite sequence, using a keyed per-tensor phase for diversity, and benchmarks against seven post-training defenses on four Transformer presets and two real malware payloads.
result: GrayShield achieves sub-0.5% accuracy impact and records near-chance bit accuracy (about 50 percentage points recovery reduction) under five attacker variants, with smaller weight-distribution shift than PatternMask and post-training quantization baselines.
conclusion: The approach provides stable near-chance sanitization for Transformer supply-chain security, effectively neutralizing the declared LSB covert channel with minimal model performance loss.

title: Copex: Benchmarking Llm Robustness To Adversarial Context Across Model Context Protocol Layers
authors: Nahom Birhan, Mehrdad Rostamzadeh, Sidhant Narula, Mahmoud Nazzal, Mohammad Ghasemigol, Daniel Takabi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models increasingly mediate tool use in Model Context Protocol (MCP) systems, where adversarial influence may enter through user instructions, tool schemas, tool outputs, or protocol messages. Existing benchmarks often evaluate deployed agents, conflating model susceptibility with guardrails, orchestration, and general task capability. We introduce COPEX (COntext Provider EXploitation), a controlled benchmark that isolates the model as an MCP client by fixing the surrounding agent stack and varying only the tool-selecting model. COPEX covers 25 attack types instantiated as 125 scenarios across four entry surfaces: model/agent, client, server/tool, and transport. Across nine models and 3,375 trials, the mean attack success rate is 64.4%, with surface-level means ranging from 58.3% to 71.4%. Some client- and transport-level attacks succeed partly outside the model's observation or control, separating system exposure from model susceptibility. Combined input and context scanning reduces mean attack success by 49.6% on an eight-attack defense subset relative to the undefended setting. The benchmark is available at [URL].
tldr: COPEX is a benchmark for evaluating LLM robustness to adversarial context across Model Context Protocol layers, isolating the model as an MCP client.
motivation: As LLMs increasingly mediate tool use in MCP systems, adversarial influence can enter via user instructions, tool schemas, outputs, or protocol messages, but existing benchmarks conflate model susceptibility with agent stack factors.
method: The benchmark fixes the surrounding agent stack and varies only the tool-selecting model, covering 25 attack types instantiated as 125 scenarios across four entry surfaces: model/agent, client, server/tool, and transport.
result: Across nine models and 3,375 trials, mean attack success rate is 64.4%, with surface-level means from 58.3% to 71.4%; combined input and context scanning reduces mean attack success by 49.6% on an eight-attack defense subset.
conclusion: COPEX provides a controlled way to separate system exposure from model susceptibility in MCP-based LLM agents and shows that context scanning can substantially reduce attack success.

title: Maximizing $p$-Mean Social Welfare In The High-Multiplicity Setting: Few Agent Types And Few Item Types
authors: Khaled Elbassioni Trung Thanh Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The [MATH]-mean welfare objective unifies several classical social welfare criteria for the allocation of indivisible goods. We study its maximization under additive nonnegative utilities when item and agent multiplicities are encoded in binary. For every fixed finite rational [MATH], [MATH], we show that the problem is [MATH]-hard with only two item types. Nash welfare ([MATH]) and egalitarian welfare ([MATH]) are NP-hard with three item types. These results hold both for computing an optimal allocation and for rational-threshold decision, and the utilities and threshold can be required to be positive integers. We also show that maximizing [MATH]-mean social welfare is strongly NP-hard with one agent type and an unrestricted number of item types, for every fixed finite rational [MATH] and for [MATH]. A quantitative gap in this reduction rules out an FPTAS in the latter setting unless [MATH]. On the positive side, for a fixed number of item types and an arbitrary number of agent types, we give an FPTAS for every fixed [MATH]. Its running time is polynomial in the compact input length and in [MATH], and it returns a compressed allocation. For a fixed number of agent types and an unrestricted number of item types, we give a PTAS for every fixed finite rational [MATH], also in the fully compact model. We further give explicit compact-model proofs of the classical exact allocation algorithms for one item type, and for egalitarian welfare with two item types. These results essentially settle the complexity and approximability of [MATH]-mean welfare maximization with few item types and/or few agent types, leaving only the exact complexity of Nash welfare maximization with two item types unresolved in the small-item-type classification.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity and approximability of maximizing p-mean social welfare for allocating indivisible goods in high-multiplicity settings with few agent and item types.
motivation: The p-mean welfare objective unifies several classical social welfare criteria, and understanding its computational limits is important for fair allocation of indivisible goods.
method: The authors use NP-hardness reductions and design approximation schemes (FPTAS and PTAS) under compact input encodings with few item types or few agent types.
result: They show NP-hardness with only two item types for any fixed p, strong NP-hardness with one agent type and unrestricted item types, and give an FPTAS for fixed item types and a PTAS for fixed agent types.
conclusion: The results essentially settle the complexity and approximability of p-mean welfare maximization in these high-multiplicity regimes, leaving only the exact complexity of Nash welfare with two item types unresolved.

title: The Same Zero: Why Identical Asr Can Imply Different Guarantees In LLM-Agent Security
authors: Yajie Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-agent security has produced a dense landscape of defenses - prompt hardening, content filters, permission gates, sandboxes - yet no framework tells a deployer what a defense actually guarantees, or where that guarantee comes from. We apply Verification Autonomy Levels (VAL) - L0: LLM self-declaration; L1: deterministic rules; L2: objective ground truth; L3/L4: decidable completeness; L5: impossible - to 22 agent-security defenses; the taxonomy is falsifiable (10/10 prediction hits on frozen cards, flagged). We run the first controlled deployment-value comparison: at equal budget, a VAL-guided stack (confirmation gate + schema sandbox) versus a mainstream intuition stack (prompt hardening + keyword filter), 50 scenarios, 12 attack variants, adaptive/white-box/PAIR escalation (~7,000 testbed calls; ~10,000 harness calls on AgentDojo/JADE). The VAL stack holds 0.000 attack success at 1.000 benign success (0.5% ASR at 79.7% utility on AgentDojo banking vs 4.3% undefended); the intuition stack reaches 0.000 ASR but kills all benign actions - security by model-behavior luck, not structure. Across testbeds of rising attack-surface hardness the intuition stack's zero drifts (0->1.9%->6.2%, n=16 on JADE) while the VAL stack's holds within its ODD (0->0->0), its only breach a disclosed out-of-ODD password gap (0.5%). The same zero, two different guarantees: zero is an outcome, not a guarantee.
tldr: This paper introduces a Verification Autonomy Levels (VAL) taxonomy to compare LLM-agent security defenses and argues that identical attack success rates can mask fundamentally different security guarantees.
motivation: LLM-agent security lacks a framework for specifying what a defense actually guarantees, making deployment decisions opaque and potentially misleading.
method: The authors classify 22 agent-security defenses using VAL levels L0–L5, then run controlled comparisons between a VAL-guided stack and an intuition-based stack across 50 scenarios, 12 attack variants, and adaptive/white-box/PAIR escalation on AgentDojo and JADE.
result: The VAL-guided stack maintains 0.000 ASR with high benign success, whereas the intuition stack also reaches 0.000 ASR but only by blocking all benign actions; under harder attacks the intuition stack's zero drifts to 6.2%, while the VAL stack remains within its operational design domain.
conclusion: A zero attack success rate is an outcome, not a guarantee; structural verification-based autonomy levels provide more reliable deployment assurances than behavior-dependent defenses.

title: Library-Grade Modal Logic
authors: Fabrizio Montesi Marianna Girlando
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modal logic comprises a broad family of logics to reason about relational structures. The literature presents many such logics, displaying diverse operators, semantics, and applications. This plurality is reflected in a zoo of mechanised modal logics, which often duplicate syntax, semantics, metatheory, and reasoning infrastructure. We present a library-grade formalisation of modal logic in Lean, developed as part of CSLib (the Lean Computer Science Library) and designed around two complementary forms of reuse: vertical reuse, whereby specialised logics inherit from common abstractions, and horizontal reuse, whereby modal logic becomes a reasoning tool for independently formalised domains. Our development provides a generic framework for polyadic modal languages, reusable metatheory and proof automation, and derived interfaces for specialised modal logics. We exemplify our infrastructure by deriving basic modal logic, basic temporal logic, and Hennessy-Milner Logic; the latter subsumes and extends CSLib's previous implementation while reducing its logic-specific code by 67%. We further apply the same modal infrastructure to reasoning about mathematics (radicals of ideals), theory of programming languages (the type safety strategy for the simply typed [MATH]-calculus), and concurrency theory (reasoning about processes in the Calculus of Communicating Systems). Our experience suggests that reuse, automation, and integration with the strong Lean ecosystem should be treated as first-class design concerns when formalising theories for shared libraries.
tldr: Presents a library-grade formalisation of modal logic in Lean with vertical and horizontal reuse, deriving several modal/temporal logics and applying them to mathematics, programming languages, and concurrency.
motivation: Mechanised modal logics often duplicate syntax, semantics, metatheory, and reasoning infrastructure, motivating a reusable library-based approach.
method: The authors develop a generic framework for polyadic modal languages in Lean, including reusable metatheory, proof automation, and derived interfaces for specialised logics.
result: The framework derives basic modal logic, basic temporal logic, and Hennessy-Milner Logic, reducing logic-specific code by 67% for the latter, and is applied to radicals of ideals, type safety for the simply typed lambda-calculus, and CCS reasoning.
conclusion: Reuse, automation, and integration with the strong Lean ecosystem should be first-class design concerns when formalising theories for shared libraries.

title: StegoMemory: Agentic Memory Acts As Covert Steganographic Channel
authors: Arun Nair Snehasis Mukhopadhyay
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Is agentic memory robust against stealthy steganographic attacks? We carry out a large-scale red-teaming exercise to test whether agents can encode attacker-controlled strings in one session and recover them in another without triggering safety oversight. Following SHADE-Arena-style tasks, we embed malicious side tasks to encode secret strings using steganography within otherwise benign tasks and evaluate them using independent task-completion and safety oversight. We test 14,000 attack trials spanning 91 model-attack configurations, 13 models, and 7 steganographic schemes: Acrostic, Mesostic, Telestich, Word-choice, Capitalization, Position-based, and Homoglyph. 41.2% of trials successfully encode the target payload in the generated response, while 29.8% survive the memory-write step with the encoding intact. Overall, 25.4% of trials yield a recoverable payload at retrieval, and 20.1% achieve exact-match recovery, including synthetic API keys and cryptographic material never exposed to the receiver. Among the exact-match transmissions, 71.4% also pass primary task-completion scoring and are independently judged safe by the oversight model, corresponding to 14.4% of all trials in which a successful covert transmission would appear to be an ordinary, benign interaction under task-level evaluation. Our results demonstrate that agentic memory can function as a persistent cross-session covert channel. The results further show that the principal bottleneck occurs at memory persistence rather than retrieval: once a steganographic payload survives the memory-write stage, a substantial fraction remains recoverable. We therefore argue that memory integrity, information-flow control, and covert-channel detection should be explicit security requirements for agentic systems.
tldr: Agentic memory in LLM systems can serve as a persistent cross-session covert channel for steganographic payloads, with a significant fraction evading safety oversight.
motivation: The paper investigates whether agentic memory is robust against stealthy steganographic attacks that could encode attacker-controlled strings across sessions without triggering safety mechanisms.
method: A large-scale red-teaming exercise with 14,000 attack trials across 91 model-attack configurations, 13 models, and 7 steganographic schemes, using SHADE-Arena-style tasks with independent task-completion and safety oversight.
result: 41.2% of trials encoded the target payload, 29.8% survived memory-write, 25.4% yielded recoverable payloads, and 20.1% achieved exact-match recovery; 14.4% of all trials resulted in successful covert transmission while appearing benign under task-level evaluation.
conclusion: Agentic memory can function as a persistent covert channel, and the main bottleneck is memory persistence rather than retrieval, motivating explicit security requirements for memory integrity, information-flow control, and covert-channel detection.

title: Fractional-order Differential Geometry Of Gielis Curves: Chart Regularization, Caputo Curvature, And The Fate Of Singularities
authors: Derya Sa\u{g}lam Umut Selvi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gielis curves describe many natural shapes, and some of them have corners or cusps. We apply two recent ideas from the differential geometry of curves to Gielis curves: "regularizing" changes of metric and fractional curvatures based on the Caputo derivative. First, we show that the smoothness of a Gielis curve is controlled by the exponents [MATH] and [MATH], not by [MATH]. A change of coordinates, the Gielis chart, maps every Gielis curve that closes after one turn onto the unit circle. However, the corners and cusps of the curve reappear as a loss of regularity of the metric; they are transported, not removed. Second, for the fractional curvature defined by Caputo scaling, we distinguish two conventions that differ in the choice of parameter and derive their scaling laws under homotheties. We prove that the memory of the Caputo operator breaks the rotational symmetry: the fractional curvature takes different values at corresponding points of congruent arcs. For fractional order [MATH], the curves of constant fractional curvature are spirals, and the clothoid is a special case. We also introduce a fractional total turning for curves with corners, give closed forms for regular polygons, and show that fractional general and slant helices coincide with the classical ones. The Python library used in the computations is listed in the appendix.
tldr: This paper studies fractional differential geometry of Gielis curves using chart regularization and Caputo curvature, analyzing singularities and rotational symmetry breaking.
motivation: Gielis curves can exhibit corners and cusps, and the authors aim to apply recent ideas from metric regularization and fractional calculus to understand their smoothness and curvature properties.
method: They introduce a Gielis chart that maps closed Gielis curves to the unit circle, analyze regularity loss in the metric, and define fractional curvature via the Caputo derivative with two scaling conventions.
result: They show that curve smoothness depends on certain exponents, that singularities are transported rather than removed, and that Caputo memory breaks rotational symmetry in fractional curvature; constant fractional curvature yields spirals, with the clothoid as a special case.
conclusion: The work provides a fractional-geometric framework for Gielis curves, including fractional total turning and closed forms for regular polygons, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multi-Index Recovery For Total-Degree Multivariate Vandermonde Matrices
authors: Samuel Santos-P\'erez
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For multivariate polynomial bases of total degree at most n, a column of the Vandermonde matrix is identified by a multi-index of exponents. In this work, we give a direct, recursive map from the scalar column index to this multi-index, based on a prescribed ordering in which exponents of the last variable are increased at the block level and the same rule is applied recursively to the remaining variables. The map is first derived explicitly in the bivariate case, where it yields closed-form column indices for the univariate Vandermonde matrices, and is then extended recursively to arbitrary dimension by means of a binomial counting function, with a proof of correctness by induction. The procedure provides random access to any total-degree column without forming the full tensor-product matrix, and is particularly advantageous for streaming construction and matrix-free evaluation. It is basis independent and applies directly to Chebyshev--Vandermonde matrices. For the full dense matrix, nested loops over the exponent multi-indices achieve the same asymptotic cost; the gain of the present approach lies in exact indexing and the avoidance of superfluous intermediate arrays.
tldr: This paper provides a direct recursive indexing scheme for total-degree multivariate Vandermonde matrices, enabling random access to columns without forming the full matrix.
motivation: Multivariate Vandermonde matrices are commonly used in polynomial interpolation and approximation, where efficient column indexing is needed for streaming or matrix-free evaluation.
method: The authors derive explicit closed-form column indices for the bivariate case and extend the construction recursively to arbitrary dimensions using a binomial counting function, with a proof of correctness by induction.
result: The proposed map yields exact indexing for total-degree polynomial bases and is basis-independent, applying also to Chebyshev--Vandermonde matrices while avoiding superfluous intermediate arrays.
conclusion: The approach offers practical advantages for memory-efficient construction and evaluation of multivariate Vandermonde matrices, though it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Two-level Filtered Subspace Iterative Method For Generalized Hermitian Interior Eigenvalue Problems
authors: Qi Li, Shi Shu, Xiaofei Xu, Juan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a two-level filtered subspace iterative (TLFSI) method for computing all eigenpairs whose eigenvalues in the interval of interest [MATH] after finite element discretization of self-adjoint PDE eigenvalue problems. The method combines a two-level approach with a modern filtered subspace iteration framework. In this paper, we use contour integral filtering as an example. The two-level method constructs a coarse space according to the spectral location of the eigenvalues of interest and obtains from it an approximation to the target invariant subspace. We prove that the distance between the approximate and target subspaces depends only on the separation between the spectral region of interest and the remainder of the spectrum, together with the coarse mesh size \(H\). Numerical experiments on benchmark elasticity problems confirm the theoretical predictions.
tldr: The paper proposes a two-level filtered subspace iterative method for computing interior eigenpairs of generalized Hermitian eigenvalue problems arising from finite element discretizations of self-adjoint PDEs.
