motivation: Efficiently computing all eigenvalues within a given interval for large-scale generalized Hermitian eigenvalue problems is important in applications such as elasticity, where standard methods can be costly or lack rigorous convergence guarantees.
method: The method combines a two-level approach with filtered subspace iteration, using contour integral filtering, and constructs a coarse space based on the spectral location of the target eigenvalues to approximate the desired invariant subspace.
result: The authors prove that the subspace approximation error depends only on the spectral separation and the coarse mesh size H, and numerical experiments on benchmark elasticity problems confirm the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The TLFSI method provides a theoretically justified and practically effective approach for interior eigenvalue problems, with error bounds controlled by spectral separation and coarse discretization.

title: Umbral Hermite Representations Of Canonical Catastrophe Integrals
authors: Giuseppe Dattoli (ENEA, Nuclear Department, Frascati Research Center, Via E. Fermi 45, 00044 Frascati, RM, Italy), Roberto Ricci
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher-order multivariable Hermite-Kamp\'e de F\'eriet polynomials provide a unified construction of umbral representations for canonical catastrophe integrals. Expanding the unfolding exponential in these polynomials and integrating against the leading catastrophe kernel gives convergent moment expansions on suitable decay contours. A universal formal umbral operator then expresses the resulting fields through explicit moment ground states. We develop this construction for the fold, cusp and swallowtail, and relate the Euclidean Pearcey field to quartic scalar partition functions. The distinction between formal and analytic umbral frameworks becomes essential when integration is performed before umbral evaluation. For Euclidean Pearcey, the integrated linearized kernel is a rational function whose action is not specified by the original formal rules. The Analytic Umbral Framework supplies a convergent Mellin pairing for this kernel and recovers the independently obtained bivariate Pearcey representation. This establishes, in this example, an exchange of integration and analytic evaluation and identifies a specific extension beyond the formal framework.
tldr: The paper develops umbral representations of canonical catastrophe integrals (fold, cusp, swallowtail) using multivariable Hermite-Kampé de Fériet polynomials and relates the Euclidean Pearcey field to quartic scalar partition functions.
motivation: The authors aim to unify the construction of catastrophe integrals through umbral calculus, extending formal umbral methods to analytic settings where the formal rules break down.
method: Higher-order multivariable Hermite-Kampé de Fériet polynomials are used to expand the unfolding exponential, yielding convergent moment expansions on decay contours; a formal umbral operator expresses the resulting fields, and an Analytic Umbral Framework supplies a Mellin pairing for the integrated linearized Pearcey kernel.
result: The construction is carried out explicitly for the fold, cusp, and swallowtail catastrophes, and the analytic framework recovers the independently known bivariate Pearcey representation, demonstrating an exchange of integration and analytic evaluation beyond the formal umbral rules.
conclusion: The work identifies where formal umbral methods must be replaced by analytic ones, providing a convergent Mellin-based extension and highlighting a specific limitation of the purely formal framework.

title: Stochastic Sequential Feedback Optimization For Wind Farm Control Under Time-Varying Inflow
authors: Sergio Grammatico Shijie Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider steady-state optimization of nonlinear dynamical systems under time-varying stochastic operating conditions, where the objective is an expected-value function over the current operating-condition distribution, so that changes in the distribution induce a moving stochastic optimum. To address this problem, we propose stochastic sequential feedback optimization (S2FO), which combines projected feedback-gradient updates with sequential sensitivity estimates obtained by linearizing the plant at realized stochastic operating conditions. We analyze the closed-loop performance of S2FO through expected dynamic regret, instantaneous tracking in expectation, and almost-sure convergence under diminishing step sizes. We then apply the method to wind farm power maximization under time-varying stochastic inflow. Simulations on a benchmark layout and on a realistic offshore wind farm show that S2FO improves average power generation when persistent wake interactions are present, and that its advantage decreases as wind-direction variability increases.
tldr: The paper proposes stochastic sequential feedback optimization (S2FO) for steady-state optimization of nonlinear dynamical systems under time-varying stochastic conditions, applied to wind farm power maximization.
motivation: Wind farm power maximization under time-varying inflow is hampered by moving stochastic optima induced by changing operating-condition distributions, requiring online control methods that adapt to non-stationary conditions.
method: S2FO combines projected feedback-gradient updates with sequential sensitivity estimates obtained by linearizing the plant at realized stochastic operating conditions, and is analyzed via expected dynamic regret, instantaneous tracking, and almost-sure convergence under diminishing step sizes.
result: Simulations on a benchmark layout and a realistic offshore wind farm show S2FO improves average power generation under persistent wake interactions, with the advantage diminishing as wind-direction variability increases.
conclusion: S2FO offers a theoretically grounded framework for closed-loop optimization of nonlinear systems under time-varying stochastic conditions, with practical benefits demonstrated for wind farm control.

title: Why Does The Slope Definition Of $e$ Work?: A Self-Contained Exploration After Real Analysis
authors: Hung Viet Chu, Steven J. Miller, Joshua M. Siktar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Euler's number [MATH] is often introduced through compound interest, an infinite series, an area, or the slope of an exponential function. The last viewpoint is especially attractive: choose the base [MATH] so that the graph of [MATH] has tangent slope [MATH] at [MATH]. However, a curious student may raise several questions that a brief introduction necessarily leaves implicit. What does [MATH] mean when [MATH] is irrational? Why is [MATH] differentiable at [MATH]? How can one show that the slopes corresponding to bases [MATH] and [MATH] lie on opposite sides of slope [MATH]? Finally, why is there a unique base whose slope is exactly [MATH]? The paper provides an answer using tools from a first course in real analysis, including limits, continuity, derivatives, and the Intermediate Value Theorem. Its primary audience is undergraduate students familiar with standard concepts from an introductory analysis course who wish to apply what they have learned to explore questions left open in earlier courses. A secondary audience is instructors who may use selected portions as supplementary material in an introduction-to-proofs course. The mathematical ingredients are classical; our aim is to organize them into a self-contained exposition and to make explicit the logical steps that are often compressed in standard treatments.
tldr: A self-contained real-analysis exposition justifying why Euler's number e is the unique base whose exponential function has tangent slope 1 at x = 0.
motivation: Undergraduate treatments of Euler's number often assert the slope-based definition without justifying implicit claims about irrational exponents, differentiability, or uniqueness of the base.
method: The authors use standard tools from a first course in real analysis — limits, continuity, derivatives, and the Intermediate Value Theorem — to fill in the logical steps that are typically compressed.
result: They show that the slopes of exponential functions for bases 2 and 3 straddle 1, and via the Intermediate Value Theorem establish existence and uniqueness of a base e with slope exactly 1 at the origin.
conclusion: The paper is a pedagogical, self-contained exposition aimed at undergraduates and instructors, rather than a contribution to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A New Insight Into The Ambrosio--Reshetnyak Approach To Sobolev Maps
authors: Alexander Tyulenev
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given [MATH], let [MATH] be a metric measure space such that the measure [MATH] is uniformly locally doubling and [MATH] supports a weak local [MATH]-Poincar\'e inequality. Let [MATH] be a complete pointed metric space. We prove that the equivalence class of a Borel map [MATH] (modulo coincidence [MATH]-a.e.) belongs to the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak--Sobolev class [MATH] if and only if [MATH] belongs to the Sobolev space [MATH] for every [MATH]-Lipschitz function [MATH].
tldr: The paper characterizes the Ambrosio–Reshetnyak–Sobolev class of Borel maps between a metric measure space and a complete pointed metric space via composition with Lipschitz functions.
motivation: The Ambrosio–Reshetnyak theory of Sobolev maps into metric spaces is a central tool in nonsmooth analysis and geometric measure theory, and a sharper characterization of the Sobolev class is desirable.
method: Working on a uniformly locally doubling metric measure space supporting a weak local Poincaré inequality, the author proves a characterization of the Sobolev class through equivalence of Borel maps modulo almost-everywhere coincidence.
result: A Borel map belongs to the Ambrosio–Reshetnyak–Sobolev class if and only if its composition with every Lipschitz function belongs to the corresponding Sobolev space.
conclusion: The result gives a new insight into the Ambrosio–Reshetnyak approach and extends the characterization of Sobolev maps to general metric measure space targets.

title: Largest Rashomon Sets Of Decision Trees For Robust Contextual Optimization
authors: David Pisinger Lorenzo Bonasera
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many decision trees fit the same data almost equally well, yet they can route a query point to different leaves and induce different local empirical distributions. We study decisions that meet prescribed cost, shortage or risk targets despite this predictive multiplicity. We propose the joint Rashomon and robustness optimization framework for optimal decision trees. It jointly selects an operational decision and the largest Rashomon set of trees, so that the targets hold under the local empirical distribution that every tree in this set induces at the query point. We specialize the framework to the regression setting, and we show that a tree affects the decision only through the training observations sharing the query leaf, which we call its query neighborhood. As a result, the robust problem involves only finitely many distinct constraints, which can be examined in order of increasing estimation loss. We develop a constraint generation algorithm that combines query-path pricing with dynamic programming to identify violating neighborhoods without enumerating trees. On synthetic newsvendor instances, the algorithm typically needs few neighborhoods and runs substantially faster than full neighborhood enumeration. On restaurant demand data, the robust orders increase the mean tolerated excess estimation loss by 17.6% and reduce the empirical conditional value-at-risk of the worst 10% of realized costs by 8.3% relative to the sample average approximation orders of the optimal tree, while the mean cost difference is not statistically significant. An interpretability analysis further shows how the retained neighborhoods explain the decision and its robustness limit.
tldr: This paper develops a joint Rashomon and robustness optimization framework for decision trees, selecting trees and decisions that remain robust to predictive multiplicity in contextual optimization.
motivation: Many decision trees fit data similarly well but induce different local empirical distributions, so operational decisions based on a single tree may fail to meet cost, shortage, or risk targets.
method: The authors formulate a robust optimization problem over the largest Rashomon set of decision trees, specialize it to regression, characterize query neighborhoods, and propose a constraint generation algorithm using query-path pricing and dynamic programming.
result: On synthetic newsvendor and restaurant demand data, the method runs faster than full enumeration and improves robustness: it increases tolerated excess estimation loss by 17.6% and reduces empirical CVaR of worst-case costs by 8.3% compared to sample average approximation orders.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical way to make decisions robust to model multiplicity in tree-based contextual optimization, with interpretability analysis explaining the retained neighborhoods and robustness limits.

title: ProsaBuddy: Assisting Mechanized Real-Time Schedulability Analysis With LLM-based Agents
authors: Junyi Liu, Tianchi Ren, Fei Guan, Xu Jiang, Zhe Jiang, Wang Yi, Nan Guan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rigorous schedulability analysis is essential for the design of hard real-time systems, yet errors in pen-and-paper proofs threaten the safety of critical applications. The Prosa initiative addresses this by offering a foundation for building machine-checkable schedulability analysis proofs in the Rocq proof assistant. However, the substantial time and expertise required to construct such proofs remain a major barrier for wider adoption of Prosa. This work presents ProsaBuddy, an LLM?based agent system designed to lower the effort needed to develop mechanized real-time schedulability proofs. ProsaBuddy employs a ReAct loop with retrieval over the Prosa codebase, access to Rocq tools and optional human-written hints. It uses a subgoal?delegation architecture, decomposing a lemma into subgoals and dispatches them to subagents for proof. We evaluate ProsaBuddy on a mini benchmark drawn from real-time scheduling literature. Experiment results show that ProsaBuddy significantly outper?forms state-of-the-art LLM-based Rocq automated proving agent systems and a general coding agent OpenCode.
tldr: ProsaBuddy is an LLM-based agent system that automates the construction of mechanized real-time schedulability proofs in the Rocq proof assistant, lowering the expertise barrier for using the Prosa framework.
motivation: Rigorous schedulability analysis is critical for hard real-time systems, but pen-and-paper proofs are error-prone and machine-checkable proofs in Rocq require substantial time and expertise, limiting adoption of the Prosa framework.
method: The system uses a ReAct loop with retrieval over the Prosa codebase, access to Rocq tooling, and optional human hints, plus a subgoal-delegation architecture that decomposes lemmas into subgoals dispatched to specialized proving subagents.
result: On a mini benchmark drawn from real-time scheduling literature, ProsaBuddy significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLM-based Rocq proving agents and the general coding agent OpenCode.
conclusion: LLM agent architectures with retrieval and subgoal delegation can meaningfully reduce the effort of mechanizing real-time schedulability proofs, though the work lies outside quantum information science.

title: Ascertaining Learning: Generative Ai, The Proxy Problem, And Cognitive Competence In University Mathematics
authors: Bob Osano
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For decades, university mathematics assessed executable procedure, computing and reproducing standard proofs, as a proxy for the understanding it cared about, because procedure was cheap to mark and understanding was not. Generative AI now executes much of this procedure. It does not merely let students bypass the proxy; it exposes how much of what was certified was a proxy. The crisis is not simply cheating but a proxy problem, and resolving it forces a question the discipline has long avoided: what is the irreducible human core of mathematical competence, and how can it be built when some of the executable work can be offloaded? We set out two futures: displacement-and-re-centering, in which AI takes over some execution and education moves toward judgment, formulation and verification; and atrophy, in which premature offloading may erode capacities that depend on prior construction. At the heart of the optimistic future is a verification instability: some forms of oversight are cheap and bounded, while others approach the competence required to construct the work. The outcome is a design choice, not a technological destiny. Rather than add a model, we state the response as two principles: construct before you delegate, and let verification set the ceiling: how far a student can independently verify AI output limits what they may safely delegate. We illustrate with a sequence and two worked problems, and close on the question: whether the construct-before-delegate dependency is a hard constraint or an artefact of how mathematics has been taught.
tldr: The paper argues that generative AI exposes the 'proxy problem' in university mathematics assessment and proposes design principles for preserving genuine mathematical competence.
motivation: University mathematics has long assessed executable procedures as a proxy for understanding, and generative AI now performs much of that procedure, forcing a reconsideration of what mathematical competence should mean.
method: The author presents a conceptual analysis with two future scenarios—displacement-and-re-centering and atrophy—and illustrates the argument using a sequence and two worked problems.
result: The analysis identifies a verification instability: some oversight is cheap and bounded, while other oversight approaches the competence needed to construct the work; the outcome is a design choice, not technological destiny.
conclusion: The paper proposes two principles: construct before you delegate, and let verification set the ceiling for safe delegation, closing by asking whether the construct-before-delegate dependency is a hard constraint or a pedagogical artefact.

title: Monochromatic Almost-Pythagorean Quadruples
authors: James Leng, Redmond Mcnamara, Andreas Mountakis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for any set [MATH] with positive multiplicative upper density, there exist [MATH], [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH] in [MATH] such that [MATH], generalizing a result of Frantzikinakis, Klurman and Moreira. Our techniques apply more broadly to a wide class of systems of equations, allowing us to solve these equations simultaneously and furthermore to restrict the w variable in an entirely different multiplicatively dense set. To do this, we prove a novel multiple recurrence result for multiplicative dynamical systems.
tldr: The paper proves that any set of positive multiplicative upper density contains a monochromatic almost-Pythagorean quadruple, generalizing prior work via a new multiple recurrence theorem for multiplicative dynamical systems.
motivation: The authors aim to extend known combinatorial recurrence results for multiplicative structures, specifically generalizing a result of Frantzikinakis, Klurman and Moreira on patterns in dense sets.
method: They develop a novel multiple recurrence result for multiplicative dynamical systems, which allows them to handle a broad class of systems of equations simultaneously and to restrict one variable to another multiplicatively dense set.
result: For any set with positive multiplicative upper density, there exist elements x, y, z, w in the set satisfying an almost-Pythagorean quadruple relation, and the techniques solve related systems of equations with additional multiplicative density constraints.
conclusion: The work advances combinatorial and ergodic-theoretic recurrence for multiplicative structures, with a general framework applicable to multiple equations, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Discontinuous Generalized Hyperbolicity And Structural Stability
authors: Sergey Tikhomirov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new method based on Michael's continuous selection theorem for stability of Banach-space dynamics with possibly discontinuous generalized-hyperbolic splittings. The method converts uniform orbitwise solvability estimates into bounded continuous solutions of cohomological equations. For generalized-hyperbolic diffeomorphisms in the uniform global [MATH] category, it yields continuous semiconjugacies in both directions under sufficiently small bounded Lipschitz perturbations; surjectivity is not asserted. For an infinite product of one-dimensional Morse-Smale systems, we construct compatible forward and reverse cohomological solution operators and obtain full structural stability without expansivity. This result holds on every [MATH], [MATH], including perturbations that couple coordinates. These products have no compact global attractor and, for [MATH], have uncountably many hyperbolic fixed points. The continuous-selection argument underlying the general semiconjugacy theorem is developed for generalized-hyperbolic cocycles, yielding bounded continuous solvability of cohomological equations. The cocycle analysis also gives Lipschitz shadowing for the induced operator on bounded continuous vector fields.
tldr: The paper develops a continuous-selection method to prove structural stability for discontinuous generalized-hyperbolic Banach-space dynamics without compact attractors.
motivation: Classical structural stability results often rely on compactness, expansivity, or uniform hyperbolicity, which fail for infinite products of Morse-Smale systems and other non-compact settings.
method: The authors use Michael's continuous selection theorem to convert uniform orbitwise solvability estimates into bounded continuous solutions of cohomological equations, yielding semiconjugacies and shadowing for generalized-hyperbolic cocycles.
result: They obtain continuous semiconjugacies in both directions under small Lipschitz perturbations and prove full structural stability for an infinite product of one-dimensional Morse-Smale systems on every sequence space, even with coordinate coupling.
conclusion: The work extends structural stability beyond compact or expansive settings, showing that generalized hyperbolicity and continuous selection can replace classical compactness assumptions.

title: Operator Splitting Methods For Non-autonomous Evolution Equations Comprising Three Parts, With Application To The Bloch-Torrey Equation Of Mri
authors: Barbara Kaltenbacher, Pablo Mu\~noz, Mechthild Thalhammer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we devise and analyze Lie Trotter splitting schemes for non-autonomous evolution equations, following two approaches: 1) A fully non-autonomous scheme, motivated by the potential use of explicit solutions of some subproblems. 2) A splitting scheme relying on the concept of Magnus integrators, where we freeze the operators at the beginning of each time interval as this suffices for first order convergence of the Lie-Trotter integrator. We derive first order convergence in a general setting and apply the analysis to the Bloch-Torrey equation of magnetic resonance imaging, where a decomposition into three subproblems is well-motivated by the physical role of the underlying operators. Numerical tests, complementing the time stepping scheme by a finite element space discretization, illustrate the theoretical findings.
tldr: The paper develops and analyzes Lie-Trotter splitting schemes for non-autonomous evolution equations, with an application to the Bloch-Torrey equation in MRI.
motivation: Non-autonomous evolution equations require efficient numerical integrators, and the Bloch-Torrey equation of MRI provides a physically motivated three-part decomposition.
method: Two splitting approaches are proposed: a fully non-autonomous Lie-Trotter scheme and a Magnus-integrator-based scheme that freezes operators over each time interval. First-order convergence is proved and combined with finite element space discretization.
result: The theoretical first-order convergence is established in a general setting, and numerical tests illustrate the performance of the schemes for the Bloch-Torrey equation.
conclusion: The proposed operator splitting methods are effective for non-autonomous evolution equations, particularly for MRI modeling, but they lie outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Beware EviLLM: Enabling Vulnerability Injection Via Large Language Models
authors: Zeezoo Ryu, Simon Chung, Muhammad Faraz Karim, Anna Raymaker, Karan Singh Jodha, Yash Chaturvedi, Sukarno Mertoguno
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled AI-driven code generation from natural language specifications, introducing new attack surfaces for injecting vulnerabilities into software. Prior work has studied this problem only in benign settings where vulnerabilities are introduced inadvertently, or under unconventional threat models where the LLM itself is malicious (backdooring) or the user is the attacker (jailbreaking). In this paper, we study a more realistic threat model: a third-party adversary, with capabilities comparable to existing cybercriminals, compromises the AI code generation pipeline to deliberately introduce vulnerabilities. We call this the EviLLM attack. We have implemented two instances of EviLLM, each of which only requires the underlying LLM to be accessed through a compromised account or browser, and can inject vulnerabilities from 13 CWE classes. As we show in our feasibility study, both attack vectors are already used to implement many existing cyberattacks. Our user study shows that 7 out of 8 and 10 out of 13 participants did not notice the vulnerabilities injected by the two instances of EviLLM, and 13 out of 21 participants "rarely" or "never" considered the risk of an attack like EviLLM.
tldr: The paper introduces the EviLLM attack, where a third-party adversary compromises an LLM-based code generation pipeline to deliberately inject vulnerabilities into generated software.
motivation: AI-driven code generation creates new attack surfaces, but prior work only considered benign settings or unconventional threat models such as malicious LLMs or jailbreaking users.
method: The authors implemented two instances of EviLLM that require only compromised account or browser access to the underlying LLM, and they can inject vulnerabilities from 13 CWE classes.
result: A user study found that 7 out of 8 and 10 out of 13 participants did not notice the injected vulnerabilities, and 13 out of 21 participants rarely or never considered such attack risks.
conclusion: The EviLLM attack is feasible with realistic adversary capabilities and highlights the need for security-aware AI code generation pipelines.

title: Adaptive Co-Serving Llm Watermarking On Modern Inference Engines
authors: Kieu Dang, Phung Lai, Ching-Yun Ko, Pin-Yu Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) watermarking is important for ownership verification and intellectual property protection. However, existing approaches focus on algorithmic design while treating LLM inference engines as separate components. This separation often introduces auxiliary models or external tools, increasing latency and memory overhead while limiting the use of modern inference optimizations. As a result, a deployment gap remains: practical watermarking must preserve utility, detectability, and robustness while minimizing serving overhead. To bridge this gap, we propose SWIFT, a framework that co-designs LLM watermarking with modern inference infrastructure. SWIFT (i) integrates text generation and watermark construction within a shared LLM backend to reduce re-computation, improve cache reuse, and simplify system complexity; (ii) uses instruction-guided candidate generation with semantic protection to preserve factual consistency and meaning; (iii) executes watermarking concurrently with generation through asynchronous co-serving and adaptive scheduling to reduce latency and improve resource utilization; and (iv) leverages vLLM optimizations to enhance serving efficiency. Extensive experiments across domains and tasks show that SWIFT achieves strong utility, detectability, robustness, and downstream performance while substantially improving serving efficiency. Specifically, it achieves the highest utility score (4.87), 99.65% detection accuracy compared with 76.65% for the low-latency baseline SynthID, and up to 97.7% detection under watermark removal attacks, with 5.9x lower latency than the highest-utility baseline, SafeSeal. These results demonstrate the benefits of co-designing watermarking with inference infrastructure for practical LLM serving. Code and artifacts are available at: [URL].
tldr: SWIFT co-designs LLM watermarking with modern inference engines to improve serving efficiency while preserving utility, detectability, and robustness.
motivation: Existing LLM watermarking methods treat inference engines as separate components, causing latency, memory overhead, and a deployment gap for practical serving.
method: SWIFT integrates text generation and watermark construction in a shared LLM backend, uses instruction-guided candidate generation with semantic protection, and executes watermarking concurrently with generation via asynchronous co-serving and adaptive scheduling on vLLM.
result: SWIFT achieves the highest utility score (4.87), 99.65% detection accuracy versus 76.65% for SynthID, up to 97.7% detection under removal attacks, and 5.9x lower latency than SafeSeal.
conclusion: Co-designing watermarking with inference infrastructure bridges the deployment gap, enabling practical LLM serving with strong utility, detectability, robustness, and efficiency.

title: Fluid Antenna Secure Channel-driven Constellation (fascc): A Physical Layer Security Approach
authors: Risto Wichman Daniel Dinis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have recently emerged as a promising technology for future wireless networks due to their ability to access a large number of channel realizations using a single radio-frequency chain. This capability creates new opportunities for physical-layer security beyond conventional beamforming and artificial-noise approaches. In this paper, we propose a novel Fluid Antenna Secure Channel-driven Constellation (FASCC) framework for downlink communications, in which information is conveyed through channel-domain constellation points generated by FAS port selection and phase adaptation. Two complementary FASCC schemes are developed, depending on the availability of eavesdropper's channel state information. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed FASCC framework achieves significant secrecy gains in terms of bit error rate and mutual-information secrecy performance, even when Eve is significantly closer to the base station than Bob.
tldr: The paper proposes a fluid antenna secure channel-driven constellation (FASCC) framework that uses fluid antenna port selection and phase adaptation for physical-layer security in wireless downlink communications.
motivation: Fluid antenna systems can access many channel realizations with a single RF chain, offering new opportunities for physical-layer security beyond conventional beamforming and artificial noise.
method: The authors develop two FASCC schemes depending on whether eavesdropper channel state information is available, encoding information through channel-domain constellation points generated by antenna port selection and phase adaptation.
result: Numerical results show significant secrecy gains in bit error rate and mutual-information secrecy performance, even when the eavesdropper is much closer to the base station than the legitimate user.
conclusion: FASCC provides an effective physical-layer security approach for future wireless networks using fluid antenna systems.

title: A Divisor-Weighted Golomb Sequence: Zeta Asymptotics And Arithmetic Fluctuations
authors: Marco Mantovanelli
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a divisor-weighted version of Golomb's self-description: the nondecreasing sequence [MATH] in which each positive integer [MATH] occurs [MATH] times. This rule has a unique solution, and $[MATH][MATH]w[MATH]w(1)=1[MATH]\sum_q w(q)q^{-\varphi}<\infty[MATH]O_\gamma((\log n)^{-\gamma})[MATH]0<\gamma<1[MATH]\sum_{d\mid m}d^{1-\varphi}[MATH][1,\infty)$, determine all real Mellin moments, obtain the sharp maximal order of the fluctuations, and show that sampling sequence positions instead of block labels produces the size-biased law.
tldr: The paper studies a divisor-weighted version of Golomb's self-describing sequence, analyzing its zeta asymptotics and arithmetic fluctuations via analytic number theory.
motivation: Golomb's sequence is a classical self-describing object, and the author generalizes it by introducing a divisor weight to study new analytic behavior.
method: The work uses analytic number theory techniques, including zeta asymptotics, Mellin moments, and fluctuation analysis for the weighted sequence.
result: It establishes unique existence, sharp maximal order of fluctuations, and a size-biased law when sampling sequence positions instead of block labels.
conclusion: The results contribute to number theory and combinatorics, but have no direct relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Accelerated Benders Decomposition For Bi-objective Mixed Integer Programming
authors: Duleabom An, Chungmok Lee, Sophie N. Parragh
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate bi-objective mixed integer programming to which Benders decomposition can be applied, a widely used technique for exploiting problem structures in real-world applications. Our study focuses on a sustainable supply chain network design problem that aims to minimise both economic and environmental objectives. To address the bi-objective nature, we employ the weighted sum method, which requires solving similar problems repeatedly with different weight values. To tackle this, we propose a straightforward acceleration technique that reuses Benders cuts generated in previous iterations of the weighted sum method. This approach enables the Benders decomposition master problem to be initialised with pre-generated cuts. Our computational experiments demonstrate that reusing these cuts significantly reduces computing time.
tldr: This paper proposes an accelerated Benders decomposition method for bi-objective mixed integer programming, applied to sustainable supply chain network design.
motivation: Bi-objective mixed integer programming problems require solving similar subproblems repeatedly under the weighted sum method, which is computationally expensive.
method: The authors reuse Benders cuts generated in previous weighted-sum iterations to initialize the master problem with pre-generated cuts, thereby accelerating the decomposition.
result: Computational experiments demonstrate that reusing Benders cuts significantly reduces computing time compared to standard Benders decomposition.
conclusion: The proposed acceleration technique improves the efficiency of bi-objective mixed integer programming and is particularly useful for sustainable supply chain network design.

title: Modal Input-output Theory For Quantum Nanophotonics From The First-order Maxwell Operator
authors: Ankit Kundu, Ishita Agarwal, Adhyyan S. Mansukhani, Jonathan D. Hood
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a quantum input-output theory for open photonic systems based on macroscopic quantum electrodynamics using the first-order electromagnetic Green's function. Quantum fields enter and leave the photonic system through waveguide ports, while the electromagnetic Green's function propagates the fields through the arbitrary interior of the photonic system, which may be dispersive and absorbing. The resulting relation contains a port-to-port scattering matrix and a Langevin-noise contribution from material absorption that together preserve the bosonic output commutation relations. For embedded emitters, the low-saturation and single-excitation scattering response is determined by Green's functions connecting the ports and emitters while retaining the non-Markovianity of the photonic environment. Using finite-difference time-domain simulation, we calculate the emitter-modified transmission for a nanophotonic cavity and inverse-designed coupler, providing a direct route from computed electromagnetic response to a quantum input-output model.

title: Asymptotic Analyis Of An Optimal Control Problem For A Phase Field Tumor Growth Model With Hyperbolic Relaxation Of The Chemical Potential
authors: Pierluigi Colli, Elisabetta Rocca, J\"urgen Sprekels
abstract: ArXiv:2610.04380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal control of a phase field tumor growth model of Cahn--Hilliard type with possibly singular potential in which the often assumed parabolic relaxation of the chemical potential is replaced by a hyperbolic one. We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the control problem as the relaxation parameter [MATH] approaches zero. It is shown that the corresponding state and adjoint state variables of the relaxed problem converge in a suitable sense to their counterparts for the unrelaxed regime where [MATH]. Also, weak limits of optimal controls for the relaxed problem can be shown to be optimal controls for the unrelaxed case. Moreover, every fixed optimal control [MATH] for the unrelaxed system turns out to be the limit of a family [MATH] of minimizers of suitable optimal control problems for the relaxed systems, where the original cost functional is replaced by the so-called ``adapted'' cost functional. It is also shown that the variational inequalities satisfied by [MATH], which constitute the first-order necessary optimality conditions of the relaxed problems with adapted cost functional, converge to the corresponding variational inequality fulfilled by [MATH] for the unrelaxed problem with the original (nonadapted) cost functional.
tldr: This paper analyzes the asymptotic behavior of an optimal control problem for a phase-field tumor growth model of Cahn-Hilliard type with hyperbolic relaxation of the chemical potential as the relaxation parameter tends to zero.
motivation: Phase-field models of tumor growth often assume parabolic relaxation of the chemical potential; replacing it with a hyperbolic relaxation is more physically realistic but complicates the optimal control analysis.
method: The authors study a Cahn-Hilliard-type phase-field system with singular potential and hyperbolic relaxation, and investigate the limit of the optimal control problem as the relaxation parameter approaches zero using asymptotic analysis and variational inequalities.
result: They prove convergence of state and adjoint variables to the unrelaxed regime, show that weak limits of relaxed optimal controls are optimal for the unrelaxed problem, and establish that every unrelaxed optimal control is a limit of minimizers of relaxed problems with adapted cost functionals.
conclusion: The relaxed optimal control problems converge to the unrelaxed problem in a suitable sense, with the corresponding first-order optimality conditions passing to the limit.
